label: S0903
statement:
statement: For every finite search language F subseteq {0,1}^N with a specified valid witness w(x) for each x in F, a deterministic layered transducer can recognize F and output w(x) using N state bits and zero fan-in-2 update gates per input step, if arbitrary final decoding is allowed. The state after t bits is the length-N register containing the read prefix in positions 1..t and zeros elsewhere. On input bit b at step t+1, the next-state function wires b into position t+1 and copies all other positions, requiring no gates. At t=N, the decoder interprets the register as x, rejects if x not in F, and outputs w(x) otherwise. Thus the achievable resource point is (S,G,D)=(N,0,D_F), where D_F is the size/cost of this final decoder and is not bounded here.
scope: All finite F subseteq {0,1}^N with a fixed witness selector w:F->{0,1}^*; layered deterministic model, free wires, final decoding permitted, and no bound asserted on decoder cost.
proof: The register invariant holds initially for the empty prefix. If it holds after t bits, the prescribed wiring fills exactly position t+1 with the next bit and preserves all earlier positions and zeroes in later positions; induction gives the invariant through t=N. The final register is therefore exactly the input x. The stated decoder is correct by its definition on F and its reject branch outside F. Each update consists only of wires and constants, so uses zero fan-in-2 gates.

label: S0904
statement:
statement: For every finite language F subseteq {0,1}^N, let R_t(p) = {z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F} for each prefix p of length t. The layered machine whose layer-t states are the distinct residuals R_t(p), plus the empty residual when it occurs, recognizes F exactly and has at most sum_{t=0}^N |{R_t(p): p in {0,1}^t}| states across its layers.
proof: The initial state is R_0(empty). On bit b at layer t, map residual R_t(p) to {z: bz in R_t(p)}. If R_t(p)=R_t(q), these sections are equal, so the transition is well-defined on residual states. By definition, this section equals R_{t+1}(pb). Inductively, after reading prefix p the machine is in R_t(p). At layer N the residual is {empty} exactly when p is in F, and is empty otherwise, so accepting precisely in the former case recognizes F. The layer-t state count is the number of distinct residuals at that layer; summing gives the stated total.
scope: All finite binary languages F subseteq {0,1}^N. This is a state-count construction only: it provides no upper bound on Boolean update-gate cost or decoder cost, and therefore does not resolve the Lemma M Pareto frontier.

label: S0905
statement:
statement: Let a deterministic transition map k source states to l destination states on one input bit. Assign distinct binary codes of width a=ceil(log2 k) to source states and width b=ceil(log2 l) to destination states. There is an exact fan-in-two Boolean circuit for the next code using O(k a + k b) gates.
proof: For each source state i, compute its equality indicator e_i by ANDing the a literals specifying its code; this costs O(a) gates per state. For each destination-code bit r, OR the indicators e_i over source states whose transition (for the given input bit) leads to a destination with bit r equal to 1. Each of the k indicators occurs in at most b such ORs, so all OR trees cost O(kb). The next-code bits are exactly these ORs because exactly one source code is valid. Hence the total is O(ka+kb). Constant-width and empty-OR cases can be handled with constants.
scope: One transition on one input bit, with valid binary source codes and fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates. The bound is O(k log(k+1)+k log(l+1)); it does not establish a useful fixed-S Pareto point for SC_{n,s} or bound decoder cost.

label: S0906
statement:
statement: Let u=(u_1,...,u_r) be the primary input wires of a Boolean circuit over AND, XOR, NOT, and constants, with every nonconstant gate counted and fan-out free. A zero-gate circuit output computes exactly 0, 1, or one of the input projections u_i. For a multi-output map required only on R subseteq {0,1}^r, a zero-gate implementation exists iff each output coordinate restricted to R agrees with a constant or an input projection.
proof: With zero counted gates, there are no gate outputs. Each output must therefore be connected directly to a primary input or a permitted constant. This proves necessity. Conversely, if each output coordinate agrees on R with one such source, connect it directly to that source. Fan-out permits reuse, so this implements all coordinates simultaneously. Behavior outside R is unrestricted.
scope: All finite r>=0, arbitrary finite output dimension, and arbitrary reachable input set R. NOT is counted as a nonconstant gate.

label: S0907
statement: statement: Let N>=1 and F be any subset of {0,1}^N. For a prefix p of length t define R_t(p)={v in {0,1}^{N-t}: pv in F}. For b in {0,1}, define the section operator D_b(R)={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv in R}. Then R_{t+1}(pb)=D_b(R_t(p)). Moreover, if p and q satisfy R_t(p)=R_t(q), their one-bit successors pb and qb have equal residuals and therefore may be assigned the same next-layer state in the exact residual-state automaton. Proof: For every suffix v of length N-t-1, v belongs to R_{t+1}(pb) iff (pb)v belongs to F iff p(bv) belongs to F iff bv belongs to R_t(p) iff v belongs to D_b(R_t(p)). This proves set equality. If R_t(p)=R_t(q), applying the same set map D_b gives D_b(R_t(p))=D_b(R_t(q)); by the first equality these are the residuals of pb and qb. Thus the successor-state map is well-defined on residual classes. This is a constructive exact transition rule for every finite language; it makes no bound on Boolean gate complexity of D_b or the decoder. Scope: all finite F subseteq {0,1}^N and 0<=t<N. Status: VERIFIED MATHEMATICS candidate; not a bound on Lemma M's (S,G_max,D) frontier.

label: S0908
statement: For every finite language F subseteq {0,1}^N, every 0 <= t < N, every length-t prefix p, and bit b, define R_t(p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F}. Then R_{t+1}(pb)={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv in R_t(p)}. Consequently, equality of residuals is preserved by the deterministic one-bit derivative transition. Proof: For any v of length N-t-1, v belongs to R_{t+1}(pb) iff (pb)v belongs to F, iff p(bv) belongs to F, iff bv belongs to R_t(p), which is exactly membership in the right-hand set. Thus the derivative depends only on R_t(p), not on the representative prefix. This gives a well-defined canonical layered recognizer whose states are residual sets; at t=N it accepts precisely when the empty string belongs to the residual. Scope: all finite binary languages and all cuts.

label: S0909
statement:
statement: For every finite binary language F subseteq {0,1}^N, every 0<=t<N, every length-t prefix p, and b in {0,1}, define R_t(p)={v in {0,1}^{N-t}:pv in F}. Then R_{t+1}(pb)={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}:bv in R_t(p)}. Consequently storing R_t(p) gives an exact layered deterministic recognizer for F: update by deleting the first bit b from each residual word beginning with b; accept at t=N iff the stored residual contains the empty word.
proof: For any v of length N-t-1, v belongs to R_{t+1}(pb) iff (pb)v belongs to F by definition. Concatenation gives (pb)v=p(bv), so this is equivalent to bv belonging to R_t(p), which is exactly membership in the set on the right. Thus the update computes the exact next residual. At t=N, R_N(w) is {empty word} if w is in F and the empty set otherwise, so checking whether it contains the empty word decides membership.
scope: All finite binary languages F subseteq {0,1}^N and all cuts, prefixes, and next bits.

label: S0910
statement:
statement: For every finite language F subseteq {0,1}^N, let K=max_{0<=t<=N} |{R_t(p): p in {0,1}^t}|, where R_t(p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F}. There is a deterministic layered membership recognizer for F with S=ceil(log2(K+1)) state bits and at most S(S+2)2^(S+1) AND/XOR/NOT/constant gates in each transition circuit.
proof: At each layer t, assign distinct S-bit codes to its distinct residual sets and reserve one additional code for the empty residual if it is not already represented. At most K+1 codes are needed, and 2^S>=K+1. For a represented residual R and next bit b, transition to the code of R_b={z: bz in R} at layer t+1. If R=R_t(p), then z is in R_b iff bz is in R_t(p), iff pbz is in F; hence R_b=R_{t+1}(pb), so the transition is well-defined. Define it arbitrarily on unused state/input pairs. Each next-state bit is a Boolean function of S state bits and b. Its DNF has at most 2^(S+1) terms; each term costs at most S gates and combining terms costs at most 2^(S+1) gates. Thus each output bit costs at most (S+2)2^(S+1), and all S bits meet the stated bound. At layer N the residual is {epsilon} exactly for accepted inputs and empty otherwise, so the final state decides membership.
scope: Finite binary languages and deterministic layered membership recognizers, with layer-dependent state codes. This does not cover witness-output decoders or prove an update-cost lower bound.

label: S0911
statement:
statement: For every finite F subseteq {0,1}^N, let K=max_{0<=t<=N}|{R_t(p):p in {0,1}^t}|, where R_t(p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t}:pz in F}. There is a deterministic layered membership recognizer with S=ceil(log2(K+1)) state bits and at most S(S+3)2^(S+1) gates per transition, over AND, XOR, NOT, and constants.
proof: At each layer assign distinct S-bit codes to its residuals, using at most K codes, and reserve one further code for the empty residual if needed. Since 2^S>=K+1 this is possible. For a represented residual R and next bit b, transition to the code for R_b={z:bz in R}. If R=R_t(p), then z in R_b iff bz in R_t(p), iff pbz in F; hence R_b=R_{t+1}(pb), so the transition is well-defined. Define unused state/input transitions arbitrarily. Each output bit is a Boolean function of d=S+1 inputs. If its DNF has T<=2^d terms, form complemented input literals using at most d NOT gates, each conjunction with at most d-1=S AND gates, and combine terms by repeated OR using at most 2(T-1) AND/NOT gates. Total <= d+TS+2(T-1) <= d+T(S+2) <= (S+3)2^d, since d=S+1<=2^d. Thus all S output bits use at most S(S+3)2^(S+1) gates. At layer N the residual is {epsilon} exactly for accepted words and empty otherwise; the final state decides membership.
scope: Finite binary languages; layered membership recognition with layer-dependent state codes and transition circuits over the stated basis. Upper bound only; no witness-output guarantee or SC_{n,s} lower bound.

label: S0912
statement:
statement: ZERO-GATE COORDINATE-TRACE LEMMA. Fix the basis AND, XOR, NOT and constants, with fan-out free and non-constant gates counted. Consider a deterministic layered transducer with fixed initial state, S state bits, and one input bit read per layer. If every transition F_t:{0,1}^{S+1}->{0,1}^S has gate cost zero, then after t input bits each state coordinate is either a constant or equals one of the first t input bits. Consequently, the final state can distinguish at most 2^t input prefixes and, for t>S, at most 2^S distinct prefixes; it cannot injectively encode a live-prefix set of cardinality greater than 2^S. Proof: A circuit with zero non-constant gates in this basis contains no AND, XOR, or NOT operation. Each output is therefore either a constant or a wire among the state and current-input wires. At time zero every state coordinate is constant because the initial state is fixed. Inductively, suppose each state coordinate after t bits is a constant or one of the first t input bits. Each coordinate after the next transition selects a constant, a previous state coordinate, or the newly read input bit, so it is a constant or one of the first t+1 input bits. This proves the coordinate claim for every t. The state is a deterministic function of the t-bit prefix and has at most min(2^t,2^S) possible values, giving the cardinality consequence. This lemma covers only G_max=0; it does not imply any positive gate lower bound or constrain encodings when G_max>=1.
derivation: Induction on layers using the fact that a zero-gate output is a constant or a direct input wire. The state-value count is bounded both by the number of prefixes and by the number of S-bit states.
scope: All finite layered deterministic transducers with a fixed initial state, S bits, one input bit per layer, basis AND/XOR/NOT/constants, and zero counted nonconstant gates per transition.

label: S0913
statement:
statement: MINTERM TRANSITION UPPER BOUND. For integers S>=0 and r>=0, every deterministic one-bit transition F:{0,1}^{S+1}->{0,1}^S has an implementation over AND, XOR, NOT, and constants, with fan-out free and nonconstant gates counted, using at most S(2^{S+1}-1) gates. Proof: For each output coordinate j and each input a in {0,1}^{S+1} with F_j(a)=1, form its indicator minterm m_a=AND_{i=1}^{S+1} l_i, where l_i=x_i if a_i=1 and l_i=NOT x_i otherwise. Compute the literals with at most S+1 NOT gates total, shared across all outputs. Compute each minterm with at most S AND gates (a binary AND tree). For each output j, OR its selected minterms using XOR/AND/NOT via u OR v = NOT((NOT u) AND (NOT v)), or the cheaper identity u OR v = u XOR v XOR (u AND v); this naive expression does not establish the stated bound. Instead use De Morgan: OR of q minterms is NOT(AND of their negations), requiring at most q NOT gates and q-1 AND gates, exceeding the claimed count. Therefore replace the numerical bound by the safe bound S[(S+1)+(S+1)2^{S+1}+(2^{S+1}-1)] gates: shared input negations cost at most S+1; all output minterms at most S(S+1)2^{S+1}; output OR trees cost at most S(2^{S+1}-1) AND gates and S2^{S+1} NOT gates. This yields the stated safe bound S(S+1)2^{S+1}+S(2^{S+1}-1)+S2^{S+1}+(S+1). This construction is independent of r and applies to every transition table; it is an upper bound only, not an SC_{n,s} lower bound.
derivation: Explicit truth-table DNF for each output bit, shared input negations and fan-out, with OR implemented in the allowed basis using De Morgan and binary AND trees.
scope: All Boolean transition tables with S state bits and one input bit, basis AND/XOR/NOT/constants, fan-out free, nonconstant gates counted. No optimality claim.

Therefore replace the numerical bound by the safe bound S[(S+1)+(S+1)2^{S+1}+(2^{S+1}-1)] gates: shared input negations cost at most S+1; all output minterms at most S(S+1)2^{S+1}; output OR trees cost at most S(2^{S+1}-1) AND gates and S2^{S+1} NOT gates. This yields the stated safe bound S(S+1)2^{S+1}+S(2^{S+1}-1)+S2^{S+1}+(S+1). This construction is independent of r and applies to every transition table; it is an upper bound only, not an SC_{n,s} lower bound.

scope: All Boolean transition tables with S state bits and one input bit, basis AND/XOR/NOT/constants, fan-out free, nonconstant gates counted. No optimality claim.

label: S0006
statement: LEMMA (split sensitivity, matching family). Let k >= 2 be even, n = 2k, and F(x,y) = OR_{j=1..k} (x_j AND y_j), where x = (x_1..x_k) and y = (y_1..y_k) with y_j the variable k+j of pair P_j = {j, k+j}. Each AND is THR with weights (1,1) and threshold 2, and the OR is THR, so F is THR o THR with k bottom gates. (a) For the split S_1 = {1..k} | rest, D = 2^k. Proof: the residual of x is R_x(y) = OR_{j in supp(x)} y_j. If x != x', pick j in supp(x) minus supp(x') (or the symmetric case); then R_x(e_j) = 1 and R_x'(e_j) = 0, so x -> R_x is injective and D = 2^k. (b) For the balanced split S_2 = {1..k/2} union {k+1..k+k/2}, F = a(x) OR b(y), where a(x) = OR_{j<=k/2} (x_j AND x_{k+j}) and b(y) = OR_{k/2<j<=k} (y_j AND y_{k+j}). If a(x) = 1 the residual is constant 1; otherwise it equals b. Hence D <= 2. Consequence: for this family min over balanced splits of D is at most 2, while the first-half split gives 2^k. Scope: one explicit family for even k; a fact about one quantity, not a bound for all THR o THR circuits. It does not close G0001 or G0002 and is not counted as progress.

label: S0010
statement: LEMMA (single-gate and union residual distance, integer weights). Let g_j(x,y) = [a_j.x + v_j.y >= t_j] for j = 1..m, with a_j integer in Z^k, v_j integer in Z^(n-k), r_j = number of nonzero entries of v_j, and |v_ji| >= 1 on the support. Let f(x,y) = [sum_j g_j(x,y) >= T] and let y be uniform on {0,1}^(n-k). Then for all x, x' in {0,1}^k: Pr_y[f(x,y) != f(x',y)] <= sum_j |a_j.(x-x')| * C(r_j, floor(r_j/2)) / 2^(r_j), where a term with r_j = 0 is replaced by 1 if g_j(x,.) and g_j(x',.) differ. PROOF: (i) If all g_j agree at (x,y) and (x',y), the sums agree, so f agrees; hence a disagreement needs some g_j to disagree. (ii) For r_j >= 1, g_j(x,y) != g_j(x',y) forces v_j.y to lie in a half-open interval of integers of length |a_j.(x-x')|. (iii) Erdos (1945): for real |v_i| >= 1, an open interval of length 2 contains at most C(r, floor(r/2)) subset sums; so for each integer s, Pr_y[v_j.y = s] <= C(r_j, floor(r_j/2))/2^(r_j). Sum over the integers in (ii) and over j. QED. This is an enumeration-free certificate for one pair (x,x') of residuals.

statement:
statement_start: RANK-SENSITIVE SIGNATURE COUNTING LEMMA. Let f(z)=[sum_{j=1}^m v_j [w_j.z >= t_j] >= T], with integer weights bounded by W. Split z=(x,y), x in {0,1}^h. Let u_1,...,u_r be the distinct restrictions w_j|_X, and let q be their rank over Q. The number of attainable signatures (u_i.x)_{i=1}^r is at most min(2^h,(2Wh+1)^q). Thus signature grouping computes #f in poly(L,n,m)*(2^h + min(2^h,(2Wh+1)^q)*2^(n-h)) time, with L the input bit length.
derivation: Choose q independent restrictions b_1,...,b_q spanning the u_i over Q. Each u_i is a rational linear combination of the b_k, hence for every x its value u_i·x is determined by the q integer values b_k·x. Each b_k·x lies in [-Wh,Wh], so there are at most (2Wh+1)^q basis-value vectors, and at most 2^h because there are only 2^h x assignments. Enumerate x and tabulate the multiplicity of each full signature. For each attainable signature enumerate y, evaluate all bottom gates from the signature and y, and count accepted y. Summing multiplicity times this count is exact by S0027's grouping identity. Exact rational basis computation and coefficient representation use polynomial bit complexity in L and n; the total enumeration work is as stated.

label: S0054
statement: REPAIRED RESIDUAL-DISTANCE BOUND. Let g_j(x,y)=[a_j·x+v_j·y≥t_j] for j=1,…,m, with integer vectors and thresholds, and f(x,y)=[sum_j g_j(x,y)≥T]. For x,x'∈{0,1}^k, put d_j=|a_j·(x−x')| and let r_j be the number of nonzero coordinates of v_j. For uniform y∈{0,1}^{n−k}, Pr[f(x,y)≠f(x',y)] ≤ sum_{j:r_j>0} d_j·binom(r_j,floor(r_j/2))/2^{r_j} + sum_{j:r_j=0} 1[g_j(x,·)≠g_j(x',·)]. Proof: An output change requires at least one bottom gate to change. If r_j>0, gate disagreement confines the integer v_j·y to a half-open interval containing d_j integer values (and is impossible when d_j=0). By complementing variables corresponding to negative coefficients, each point probability of v_j·y is a subset-sum multiplicity divided by 2^{r_j}. Subsets with any fixed sum form an antichain because all transformed weights are positive integers; Sperner’s theorem bounds its size by binom(r_j,floor(r_j/2)). A union bound over the d_j values and gates gives the first sum. For r_j=0 the gate is constant in y, giving exactly the indicator term. This repairs the invalid interval claim in S0010; it provides only a pairwise residual-distance bound, not a cheap joint certificate or a CAPP speed-up.

statement: statement: COMMON-SUPPORT SIGNATURE LEMMA. Let a_1,...,a_m in Z^h and let U subseteq [h] have size r such that every a_j is zero outside U. Then the number of distinct signatures (a_1·x,...,a_m·x) as x ranges over {0,1}^h is at most 2^r. Proof: If x and x' agree on U, every dot product agrees because all coefficients outside U are zero. Therefore the signature map factors through the restriction map {0,1}^h -> {0,1}^U, which has 2^r possible inputs, proving the bound. The bound is attained by taking the r coordinate-selector rows e_i, whose joint signature is the restriction x|_U.

label: S0022
statement: S0012 (repair of the caveat in S0010 review, CLAIMED by R1090): the O(1)-gate memory/cost separation for DISJ_n also holds for a STATIONARY update circuit F (one circuit for all t), not only for time-dependent F_t. Construction: state = data ring D (n cells, FIFO), pointer ring P (n cells, one-hot, rotating every step, initial one-hot at cell 1), phase bit f (initially 0), result bit r (initially 0). Input bit w per step. Update: D'_1 = f ? D_n : w; D'_j = D_{j-1} for j >= 2 (wires); P rotates (wires); f' = f OR P_n; r' = r OR (f AND D_n AND w). Proof: steps 1..n: f=0, so D'_1 = w and the FIFO holds a_t; P_n fires first at step n, so f=1 from step n+1 on. After step n, D_n = a_1. Step n+i (i=1..n): reads D_n = a_i and w = b_i, sets r to r OR (a_i AND b_i), and cycles a_i back to D_1, so D_n becomes a_{i+1} for the next step. After 2n steps r = OR_i (a_i AND b_i) = DISJ_n. Cost: the update has O(1) gates (two gates for D'_1, one for f', two for r'); all other cells are wires, which are free in gate counting. State is 3n+1 bits, so memory is linear, as in S0010. Scope: this is a correction of the stationary caveat only. It does not give sublinear memory, and it does not bear on G0001 or G0002 (superlinear online cut-width). It is a construction, not a lower bound, and it closes no open obligation.

label: S0024
statement: L1 (memory lower bound for one-pass DISJ, bookkeeping level, does NOT close G0001 or G0002): let M be any one-pass machine reading a stream of length 2n, first a in {0,1}^n then b in {0,1}^n, with 2^S states (transitions may depend on time, no uniformity). If it outputs DISJ_n(a,b) = OR_i(a_i AND b_i) at the end, then S >= n. Proof: let q(a) be the state after reading a. Suppose a != a' with q(a) = q(a'). Choose i with a_i != a'_i. If a_i = 1, a'_i = 0: the pair (a', not-a) has DISJ = 0 (because a'_i' AND not a_i' = 0 for every i') and the pair (a, not-a) ... use the chain: run on (a', not-a') gives 0 and run on (a, not-a') has the same final state as (a', not-a') because q(a) = q(a'); but DISJ(a, not-a') = 1 since a_i AND not a'_i = 1. Contradiction. The case a_i = 0, a'_i = 1 is symmetric (swap a and a'). So q is injective on {0,1}^n, hence 2^S >= 2^n. Scope: arbitrary deterministic one-pass machines, any time-dependent transitions, state counted in bits. It matches S0022 (2n+2 bits), so linear memory is tight for DISJ. It says nothing about the number of gates or the total cost sum_t CC(F_t) + CC(D_N), which is what G0002 needs. Novelty: standard one-way communication fooling-set argument (Kremer-Nisan-Ron line); no claim of novelty.

label: S0028
statement: LEMMA R (unrolling, CLAIMED, session R-current, author Claude Haiku 5.5). Setting: L_n: {0,1}^N -> {0,1}; one-pass realisation with state space {0,1}^S, initial state c_0, update circuits F_t: {0,1}^S x {0,1} -> {0,1}^S (t = 1..N, each with CC(F_t) gates, fan-in 2, fixed complete basis), readout D_N: {0,1}^S -> {0,1}. Claim: chaining F_1,...,F_N and D_N (state wires internal, c_0 hard-wired) gives a general Boolean circuit computing L_n with at most sum_t CC(F_t) + CC(D_N) gates. Proof: the chained circuit is a fan-in-2 circuit over the same basis; its gate set is the disjoint union of the gates of the F_t and D_N; wires cost nothing; a constant input to a gate is removed without adding gates (c_0 is a constant, so no gate is added). Correctness: by induction on t the wires after step t carry psi_t = state after reading x_1..x_t. Consequence: any total-cost bound omega(N) for an explicit L_n with S(n) < N gives an omega(N) general circuit size lower bound for the same L_n. So G0002 is at least as hard as a superlinear general circuit lower bound for that explicit L_n; the restriction S(n) < N is discarded by unrolling.

label: S0033
statement: LEMMA C* (explicit constants, sharpens spec item 5 / subclaim C; does not close G0001 or G0002). Let m>=2, eta in (0,1], S=ceil(log2 m), R=floor((2-eta)S), Q={0..m-1}. For G>=0 let N=R+1+G and C(G,R)=(G+1)(16N^2)^G N^R (circuits with <=G fan-in-2 gates over a 16-function basis on R+1 inputs, R outputs). If Rm + log2 C(G,R) < 2m log2 m, then some pair (d0,d1) of maps Q->Q has CC_E(d0,d1) > G for EVERY injective E: Q->{0,1}^R. Proof: for fixed E the set P_E(G) of pairs realised under E with <=G gates injects into the circuits, so |P_E(G)| <= C(G,R); there are <= 2^{Rm} injective E; the union has size <= 2^{Rm} C(G,R) < m^{2m} = #pairs. Explicit choice G=floor(eta m/4): for m>=16 with (eta/2) m log2 m > 2m + 3 log2^2 m, the hypothesis holds (since N<=m, the sum is <= (2-eta/2) m log m + 2m + 3 log^2 m < 2m log m), so CC_E > eta m/4 for every injective E. Scope: only R <= (2-eta)S; R>=2S is not covered; no time-dependent or one-to-many codes; no explicit hard pair; no cost bound for G0002.

label: S0035
statement: Lemma (per-encoding counting). Fix m, an injective encoding E: Q -> {0,1}^R with |Q| = m, and fan-in-2 circuits over a fixed basis of 16 functions. A circuit with R+1 inputs (a selector bit and a code word) and G gates that has R outputs realises at most one pair (delta_0, delta_1) of maps Q -> Q under E. The number of such circuits is at most ((R+G+3)^2 * 16)^G * (R+G+3)^R. Since there are m^(2m) pairs, if G satisfies G*(2*log2(R+G+3)+4) + R*log2(R+G+3) < 2*m*log2(m), then some pair has circuit complexity > G under THIS E. For R = rho*m with constant rho in [0,1], the left side is G*(2*log2(m)+O(1)) + O(m*log m), so G > (1 - rho/2)*m - o(m) suffices. In particular, at R = 2S = 2*log2(m) (rho -> 0) the bound is G = Omega(m), and it holds up to R = Theta(m). This extends Claim C (which covered only R <= (2-eta)S = (2-eta)*log2(m)) to the full range R = O(m).

label: S0038
statement: PER-ENCODING PAIR BOUND. Let |Q|=m, let E: Q -> {0,1}^R be injective (fixed, not a union over encodings), and consider fan-in-2 circuits over a fixed basis of at most 16 binary gate types with R+1 inputs and R outputs and G gates. Let N(R,G) be the number of such circuits. If N(R,G) < m^(2m), then for this E some pair (delta_0, delta_1) of maps Q->Q has CC_E > G. Proof: each pair realised under E by a circuit of size <= G determines, via its values on the codes E(q), a unique pair, so choosing one realising circuit per pair gives an injection from realisable pairs into circuits of size <= G. There are m^(2m) pairs, so if N(R,G) < m^(2m) some pair is not realisable with size <= G. Count: N(R,G) <= (16 (R+G+1)^2)^G (R+G+2)^R, so log2 N <= G(4 + 2 log2(R+G+1)) + R log2(R+G+2). Consequences: (i) for R <= m and fixed eps>0, G = (1/2 - eps) m satisfies the inequality for all large m, since the left side is at most m(2 log m + 6) - eps m (2 log m + 8) < 2m log m; (ii) for R = 2 log2 m, G = (1 - eps) m works for large m. The silence at R >= 2S claimed in the spec came from the union bound over 2^(Rm) encodings, which this per-encoding statement does not need.

structure.gap: Still open (G0006, G0002): the lemma is existential. No explicit hard pair is given. It does not handle time-varying or one-to-many codes, and the bound degrades once R log R is comparable to m log m (R about m or more). Its novelty is probably low (Shannon-Lupanov counting), so it should be checked against the literature before any novelty claim.

label: S0060
statement: LEMMA (counting threshold, CLAIMED, not reviewed). Let m >= 1, S = ceil(log2 m), R >= 2S+1. Then the number of injective maps E: Q -> {0,1}^R with |Q| = m is (2^R)_m >= m^{2m} = number of pairs (delta0, delta1) of maps Q -> Q. Proof: (2^R)_m >= (2^R - m)^m; m <= 2^S <= 2^{R-1} gives 2^R - m >= 2^{R-1} >= 2^{2S} >= m^2. Sharp: for m = 2^S >= 2, R = 2S fails since each factor m^2 - i < m^2. Scope: counting existence only; bounds no circuit cost; closes neither G0001 nor G0002; does not use S(n) < N. Status: bookkeeping relative to the open gap.

label: S0065
statement: LEMMA W (online width, exact; CLAIMED, no closes-field: width is a state count, not an update-cost bound). Setting: f on n variables, cut t = the first t variables form the prefix; width_t(f) = number of distinct residual functions f|prefix over the suffix assignments; W(f) = max_t width_t(f). (a) EQ_h, n = 2h, f = AND_{i<h}[x_i = x_{h+i}]. For t <= h: prefix p gives residual g_p(suffix) = AND_{i<t}[p_i = x_{h+i}] AND AND_{t<=i<h}[x_i = x_{h+i}]. For p != p' pick the suffix with x_{h+i} = p_i (i<t) and x_i = x_{h+i} (i>=t): g_p = 1 and g_{p'} = 0. So width_t = 2^t. For t > h the residual is 0 when the prefix has a mismatch, else the indicator of a suffix pattern c in {0,1}^(n-t), so width_t = 2^(n-t)+1 <= 2^(h-1)+1. Hence W(EQ_h) = 2^h exactly. (b) INDEX_k, n = k+2^k, address a = first k bits, data = last 2^k bits, f = x_{k+a}. For t <= k: residual determined by the address prefix; distinct prefixes give residuals differing on some data assignment, so width_t = 2^t. For t >= k+1 the address is fixed to a, so the residual is a constant (if the selected data bit is in the prefix) or the projection onto x_{k+a} (if unfixed); the residual set is {0, 1} plus one projection per unfixed data bit, so width_t = 2 + 2^k - (t-k), and width_{k+1} = 2^k+1 is the maximum. So W(INDEX_k) = 2^k+1 for k>=1, NOT 2^k: the earlier prediction omitted the two constant residuals. Consequence: online width is a representation-invariant STATE count (exact one-pass lower bound in stream order), so W(EQ_h) = 2^(n/2) = sqrt(N) is a state lower bound for stream-order realisations, not a superlinear circuit or update-cost bound. Verification: cm-6f538fe8121a4cd4 (per-cut values match both formulas for EQ n=6..14 and INDEX k=1..3) and an independent tuple-residual recount in the next experiment (k<=4, h<=4).

Not used as a premise by other steps.

label: S0084
statement: REPAIR of the class-counting threshold (session R1302). Let M = 2^S, m <= M, and let h(lambda) = min CC over permutations of {0,1}^S with cycle type lambda. Claim (finite part, exact scope S = 9..16): max_lambda h(lambda) >= g*(S), where g*(S) = max{g : (g+1)*2^{L(g)} < p(M)}, L(g) = (4g+S)*log2(4(g+S)), p = partition function. Proof: every cycle type needs one circuit of size <= g in the class, so the number of circuits of size <= g is at least p(M); a circuit of size g is encoded by at most (g+1)*2^{L(g)} bits-worth of descriptions, so if that is below p(M), some class has h > g. The reduction H(delta) = h(lambda(delta)) is the cycle-matching lemma (checked exhaustively at N = 4, 8). Exact check cm-78b701c9b375494a: g*(S) = 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 19, 27 for S = 9..16, all >= sqrt(M)/(8S). For S = 3..8 the constant 1/8 fails (g* = 0), so the repaired statement is restricted to S >= 9. Asymptotic form (NOT yet proved with explicit constants): log2 p(M) ~ 3.70*sqrt(M) (Hardy-Ramanujan), so g*(S) = Omega(sqrt(M)/log M) = Omega(sqrt(m)/log m) for m <= M <= 2m. label: S0087
statement: PROOF. (1) Elementary partition bound: p(n) >= 2^{floor(sqrt(2n))-2} for n >= 2. Let k = floor(sqrt(2n)) - 1. Map each subset A of {2..k} with sum(A) <= n to the partition A plus (n - sum A) copies of 1. Since k(k+1)/2 <= n - sqrt(2n)/2 <= n, every subset qualifies; the non-1 parts recover A, so the map is injective. This gives 2^{k-1} = 2^{floor(sqrt(2n))-2} partitions. (2) Let g = floor(sqrt(M)/(4S)). For S >= 14, 4(g+S) <= sqrt(M)/S + 4S <= sqrt(M) (at S = 14: 56 <= 128, and the gap grows with S), so log2(4(g+S)) <= S/2. Also 4g+S <= sqrt(M)/S + S. Thus L(g) = (4g+S) log2(4(g+S)) <= sqrt(M)/2 + S^2/2, and log2(g+1) <= S/2. (3) Hence log2((g+1) 2^{L(g)}) <= sqrt(M)/2 + (S^2+S)/2. By (1) with n = M, p(M) >= 2^{sqrt(2M)-3}. The inequality sqrt(M)/2 + (S^2+S)/2 < sqrt(2)sqrt(M) - 3 is equivalent to f(S) := (sqrt2 - 1/2) 2^{S/2} - (S^2+S)/2 - 3 > 0. f(14) = 0.9142*128 - 108 = 9.0 > 0, and f(S+1) - f(S) = (sqrt2 - 1)(sqrt2 - 1/2)2^{S/2} - (S+1) > 0 for S >= 14 (the first term is 48 at S = 14 and grows exponentially), so f(S) > 0 for all S >= 14. (4) So (g+1) 2^{L(g)} < p(M). By the S0084 counting argument (distinct cycle types give p(M) distinct permutations; if every class had h <= g, each would have a circuit of size <= g, giving at most (g+1) 2^{L(g)} circuit descriptions), some cycle type has h >= g+1. QED. Restriction to 2^S states: subclaim A's lower bound for |Q| = m with m not a power of 2 still needs the sub-multiset case (open).

structure.lemma: Exact-size sub-multiset bound. Let N = 2^S (S >= 1), N/2 < m <= N, and lambda any partition of N. Then lambda contains at most p(m) - 1 sub-multisets of size m (each is a partition of m contained in lambda). Proof: sub-multisets of size m are distinct partitions of m, so the count is at most p(m). Exhibit one partition of m not contained in lambda. Case lambda_1 < m: (m) is not contained. Case lambda_1 >= m: lambda has at most 1 + (N - lambda_1) <= 1 + N - m parts; since N is even and m >= N/2 + 1, 1 + N - m <= N/2 < m, so (1^m) is not contained. Hence the count is at most p(m) - 1 < p(m).

label: S0091
statement: LEMMA D (sharp sub-multiset bound, CLAIMED, self-made, not reviewed by this session). Let F be any function (possibly non-injective, partial on its image) on a set of N >= 1 points. Its cycles are pairwise disjoint, so their lengths form a partition lambda of some n <= N. Let P(lambda) = prod_i (k_i + 1), k_i = multiplicity of part i. Then: (a) the number of sub-multisets of lambda (as multisets of parts) is P(lambda); (b) P(lambda) <= exp(sqrt(2N) + 3/2) for every lambda of size <= N. PROOF OF (b): Let K = sqrt(2N) >= 1 and M = floor(K). For any k >= 0 and integer i >= 1, put a = i/K. Then phi_i(k) = log(k+1) - a k satisfies: if a <= 1 its maximum over k >= 0 is -log a - 1 + a = log(K/i) - 1 + i/K (at k+1 = 1/a); if a > 1 its maximum is 0 (at k = 0). Weak duality: sum_i log(k_i+1) = sum_i phi_i(k_i) + (1/K) sum_i i k_i <= sum_{i<=M} [log(K/i) - 1 + i/K] + n/K <= sum_{i<=M} [log(K/i) - 1 + i/K] + N/K. Estimate the first sum: S1 = sum_{i<=M} log(K/i) = M log K - log M! <= M log(K/M) + M <= K (using log M! >= M log M - M and that M log(K/M) + M is nondecreasing on [0,K]). S2 = -M + M(M+1)/(2K) <= -(K-1) + (K+1)/2 = 3/2 - K/2 (using M <= K, M >= K-1). Total: S1 + S2 + N/K <= K + 3/2 - K/2 + N/K = K/2 + N/K + 3/2 = sqrt(2N) + 3/2, since K/2 = N/K = sqrt(N/2). Hence log P(lambda) <= sqrt(2N) + 3/2. QED. CONSEQUENCE for gap (i): a single circuit F realises at most P(lambda) <= exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2) cycle types of size m (its m-subsets that are unions of its cycles), with N = 2^S < 2m, so at most exp(2 sqrt m + 3/2) types, versus p(m) = exp((pi sqrt(2/3) + o(1)) sqrt m) = exp((2.565+o(1)) sqrt m). This replaces the p(m) - 1 bound of S0090 (which is far too weak) and gives the counting bound #circuits >= exp((0.56 - o(1)) sqrt m). The sub-multiset count in (a) is over ALL sizes, so it upper-bounds the exact-size count used here. NOT PROVED HERE: the reduction from circuit codes to cycle types for the actual recoding model (time-varying / value-free unused codes), and any constant-explicit p(m) lower bound (verify Erdos 1942 constant before use).

label: S0092
statement: REDUCTION R1 (self-made, CLAIMED, not reviewable by this session). Fix an encoding psi: Q -> {0,1}^S (injective, |Q| = m, N = 2^S) and an update circuit F: {0,1}^S -> {0,1}^S that computes psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q). Then psi(Q) is F-invariant, because F(psi(q)) = psi(delta(q)) lies in psi(Q). So every F-cycle meeting psi(Q) lies wholly inside psi(Q), and the cycle type of delta is a sub-multiset of lambda(F), the cycle type of the function F on N points (cycles of a function are disjoint, so lambda(F) is a partition of some n <= N). Hence, for fixed psi, the set of cycle types of size m realised by one circuit F has size at most P(lambda(F)) <= exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2) by LEMMA D (S0091). With N = 2^S < 2m this is at most exp(2 sqrt(m) + 3/2). This closes the reduction from circuit codes to cycle types for a FIXED psi, which was the missing link in gap (i). NOT COVERED: (a) the per-delta statement needs a single delta fixed across psi, not a cycle-type class; (b) time-varying or one-to-many encodings; (c) the claim that every cycle type of size m must be realised is not re-derived here.

label: S0097
statement: LEMMA U (psi-uniform form, repair of the S0092 gap). Let S>=1, N=2^S, N/2 < m <= N, G>=1. Let Lambda_G be the set of partitions mu of m for which there exist a circuit F:{0,1}^S->{0,1}^S of size <= G and a set A subset {0,1}^S with |A|=m such that F restricted to A is a bijection A->A of cycle type mu. Then |Lambda_G| <= C_G * exp(2 sqrt(N) + 3/2), where C_G is the number of circuits of size <= G on S inputs, and log2 C_G <= c*G*log(G+S) for an absolute c. Hence if C_G * exp(2 sqrt(N)+3/2) < p(m), some mu |- m is not in Lambda_G. For such mu take any delta in Sym(Q), |Q|=m, of cycle type mu. Then for EVERY injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S, CC(psi delta psi^-1) > G, where the circuit size is that of any extension of the partial map to {0,1}^S. Proof. (i) A is invariant and F|A is a bijection, so each point of A lies on a cycle of the functional graph of F; the cycle type of F|A is therefore a sub-multiset of the cycle-type multiset lambda_F of F, whose total is <= N (pad with fixed points to total N). (ii) The number of sub-multisets of size m of a partition of N is prod_i (m_i+1) over distinct part sizes i with multiplicities m_i, and by Lemma D (S0091) this is <= exp(2 sqrt(N)+3/2). (iii) F does not depend on psi, so the union over circuits gives |Lambda_G| <= C_G * exp(2 sqrt(N)+3/2). (iv) mu not in Lambda_G excludes every F of size <= G simultaneously for all psi, since A = psi(Q) is one such set. Asymptotically, p(m) = exp(pi sqrt(2m/3)(1+o(1))) and log2 C_G = O(G log(G+S)) with S=log m, so G = c' sqrt(m)/log m gives the required inequality for large m. This gives Claim A (max over delta of min over psi) as Omega(sqrt(m)/log m) for m = 2^S-range large enough.

label: S0101
statement: LEMMA D* (kind LEMMA; closes gap G0050 part (a), i.e. the general proof of the Lemma D form used by S0097 and S0091). For every N>=1 and every multiset of positive part sizes with multiplicities m_i and total sum_i i*m_i <= N: prod_i (m_i+1) <= exp(sqrt(2N) - 0.29) < exp(sqrt(2N)). PROOF. statement: LEMMA (per-encoding, R = 2S; supersedes the R=m and 'for some pair for every E' forms in S0038/S0112). Let m >= 64, S = ceil(log2 m), L = log2 m, R = 2S, G = floor(m/2). For every injective E: Q -> {0,1}^R (|Q| = m) there is a pair (delta0, delta1) of maps Q -> Q with CC_E > G. Proof: the number of fan-in-2 circuits over a 16-type basis on R+1 inputs and R outputs with G gates is N <= (16(R+G+1)^2)^G (R+G+2)^R, so log2 N <= G(4+2 log2(R+G+1)) + R log2(R+G+2). For m >= 64 one has R+G+1 <= m, R+G+2 <= m+1, R <= 2(L+1), so log2 N <= (m/2)(4+2L) + 2(L+2)^2 = mL + 2m + 2(L+2)^2. This is < 2mL iff m(L-2) > 2(L+2)^2, which holds at m = 64 (256 > 128) and for all larger m since the left side grows faster. Each pair realised under E by a circuit with <= G gates determines a distinct circuit, so fewer than m^(2m) circuits cannot realise all pairs. Check at m = 64: log2 N <= 545.6 < 768 = 2m log2 m. Scope: fixed injective E only; R = 2S exactly; no union bound over encodings; no time-dependent or one-to-many codes; no explicit hard pair; does not close G0001 or G0002. statement: LEMMA L-G0064 (CLAIMED, Haiku-authored, needs a non-Haiku review). For every integer S >= 13, with M = 2^S and g = floor(floor(sqrt(M))/(4S)): log2(g+1) + (4g+S)*log2(4(g+S)) < floor(sqrt(2M)) - 2. PROOF. (i) S = 13..19: direct high-precision evaluation (cm-c3cdd985d53849e3 covers S=13..200 with no failures; margins 26.3 at S=13 and 268.4 at S=17). (ii) S >= 20: let x = 2^(S/2), u = x/S + 4S. Then g <= x/(4S), so g+1 <= u, 4g+S <= u, 4(g+S) <= u. Hence LHS <= (u+1)*log2(u). Since 4S <= x(1-1/S) for S >= 13, u <= x, so log2(u) <= S/2 and LHS <= (u+1)*S/2 = x/2 + 2S^2 + S/2 + S/2 - ... (to be exact: (u+1)S/2 = x/2 + 2S^2 + S/2). Since floor(sqrt(2M)) - 2 > sqrt(2)*x - 3, it suffices that x/2 + 2S^2 + S/2 < sqrt(2)*x - 3, i.e. (sqrt(2) - 1/2)*x > 2S^2 + S/2 + 3. This holds at S=20 (about 936 > 813). Passing from S to S+1 multiplies the left side by sqrt(2) and the right side by at most 1.2 for S >= 20, so it holds for all S >= 20. The link check cm-70c3710488f646f6 confirms link_g, link_u, link1, link2 for S=13..200 and link3 for S=20..200.

statement: CANDIDATE LEMMA (sub-multiset case, obligation (i)). Let m >= 2, S = ceil(log2 m), M = 2^S, so m <= M <= 2m. For lambda |- m let pi_lambda be the permutation of {0,1}^S with cycle type lambda plus M-m fixed points. Distinct lambda give distinct cycle types, so there are p(m) classes. Claim: if S >= 14 and sqrt(2m) > S^2+S+6, then max over lambda |- m of h(pi_lambda) >= floor(sqrt(M)/(4S)) + 1, where h is the minimum circuit size (fan-in-2, S-bit state) over permutations of that cycle type. Proof sketch: put g = floor(sqrt(M)/(4S)). Every class needs a circuit of size <= g, so if (g+1)2^{L(g)} < p(m) then some class has h > g. Here L(g) = (4g+S)log2(4(g+S)) as in S0084, and the S0087(2)-(3) bounds give log2((g+1)2^{L(g)}) <= sqrt(M)/2 + (S^2+S)/2 <= sqrt(2m)/2 + (S^2+S)/2. By S0087(1), log2 p(m) >= sqrt(2m) - 3. The difference is at least sqrt(2m)/2 - (S^2+S)/2 - 3 > 0 under the stated condition. GAP (open): (a) the embedding of an m-state permutation into the padded M-state one is not checked for circuits that use codes outside the m used states; (b) the claim that h is taken over circuits on S-bit input with unused codes fixed needs an explicit argument; (c) the explicit constant in the condition sqrt(2m) > S^2+S+6 is not checked beyond the inequality. Scope: counting existence bound only; no update-time bound; closes neither G0001 nor G0002.

Claim: if S >= 14 and sqrt(2m) > S^2+S+6, then max over lambda |- m of h(pi_lambda) >= floor(sqrt(M)/(4S)) + 1, where h is the minimum circuit size (fan-in-2, S-bit state) over permutations of that cycle type. Proof sketch: put g = floor(sqrt(M)/(4S)). Every class needs a circuit of size <= g, so if (g+1)2^{L(g)} < p(m) then some class has h > g. Here L(g) = (4g+S)log2(4(g+S)) as in S0084, and the S0087(2)-(3) bounds give log2((g+1)2^{L(g)}) <= sqrt(M)/2 + (S^2+S)/2 <= sqrt(2m)/2 + (S^2+S)/2. By S0087(1), log2 p(m) >= sqrt(2m) - 3. The difference is at least sqrt(2m)/2 - (S^2+S)/2 - 3 > 0 under the stated condition. structure.lemma: LINEAR-R PAIR BOUND (extends S0038 from R <= m to R <= delta*m). Fix delta in [0,2) and eps in (0, 1-delta/2). Let |Q| = m, let R <= delta*m, let E: Q -> {0,1}^R be ANY injective map (no stationarity), and let G = floor((1-delta/2-eps)*m). If m >= 2^(6/eps), then some pair (delta0, delta1) of maps Q -> Q has CC_E > G, where CC_E is the least number of gates of a fan-in-2 circuit over the fixed basis with R+1 inputs (E(q), b) and R outputs computing (b,E(q)) -> E(delta_b(q)). PROOF. (1) Injection: for each realisable pair choose one realising circuit of size <= G and pad it with dummy gates to exactly G gates; the padded circuit still computes the pair on all inputs (E(q),b), and the pair is recovered from its values on E(q), so the map pair -> circuit is injective into circuits with exactly G gates. (2) Count: N(R,G) <= (16(R+G+1)^2)^G (R+G+2)^R (S0038). Since R+G+1 and R+G+2 are at most 3m, log2 N <= G(4+2 log2(3m)) + R log2(3m) <= m[(1-delta/2-eps)(2 log2 m + 7.17) + delta(log2 m + 1.585)] <= m[(2-2eps) log2 m + 10.4], using monotonicity of the bound in R and G and delta < 2. (3) For m >= 2^(6/eps): 10.4 <= 2 eps log2 m - 1.6 (approximately; 2 eps log2 m >= 12), so log2 N < 2 m log2 m = log2 m^(2m). Since there are m^(2m) pairs, the injection cannot be onto, so a pair is not realisable with <= G gates. QED. SCOPE: per-encoding existence of a hard pair with CC_E = Omega(m) for R = delta*m, delta < 2. CORRECTNESS OF THE TRANSFER: delta=1 gives G ~ m/2, i.e. S0038(i); delta -> 0 gives G ~ (1-eps)m. The regime R >= 2m (log N >= R log R >= 2m log m, so counting gives nothing) remains open; R = O(log m) is S0038(ii).

label: S0135
statement: LEMMA L (stationary cycle-type realisation, CONDITIONAL on S0091(b), which is still CLAIMED). Let m >= 2, S = ceil(log2 m), N = 2^S, so m <= N < 2m. Let Circ(G) be the fan-in-2 circuits over the fixed basis with S inputs and S outputs and at most G gates. For a circuit C, let lambda(C) be the multiset of lengths of the periodic cycles of the functional graph of C; it is a partition of some n <= N. Let T_G(m) be the set of cycle types mu of size m such that some C in Circ(G), some injective psi: Q -> {0,1}^S and some delta in Sym(Q) of type mu satisfy C(psi(q)) = psi(delta(q)) for all q. Then |T_G(m)| <= |Circ(G)| * exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2) <= |Circ(G)| * exp(2 sqrt(m) + 3/2). PROOF: if C realises (psi, delta), then A = psi(Q) is C-invariant and C restricted to A is a bijection, so A is a union of periodic cycles of C. Its cycle lengths form a sub-multiset nu of lambda(C) with |nu| = m, and nu = mu because C restricted to A is conjugate to delta. So mu is a sub-multiset of lambda(C), and by S0091(b) lambda(C) has at most exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2) sub-multisets. Summing over C gives the bound. COROLLARY: if |Circ(G)| exp(2 sqrt(m)+3/2) < p(m), some mu |- m is realised by no circuit of size <= G under any injective stationary psi, so for every delta of type mu and every psi, CC_psi(delta) > G. This is the quantifier exists-mu forall-delta forall-psi, so it gives max_delta min_psi CC >= G+1. With log|Circ(G)| <= G(4+2 log(S+G)) + S log(S+G) and log p(m) >= pi sqrt(2m/3) - O(log m), G = c sqrt(m)/log m with c < 0.56 works for large m, so H_1(m) = Omega(sqrt(m)/log m) for the stationary model.

statement: Proof. (1) For m>=8: 2S <= 2log2 m + 2 <= m, so R <= m. (2) G <= m/2, so R+G+1 <= 2m and R+G+2 <= 2m for m>=4; hence log2(R+G+1) and log2(R+G+2) are both <= 1+log2 m. (3) G>=0 and the coefficient 4+2log2(.) is positive, so F <= (1/2-eps)m(6+2log2 m) + m(1+log2 m) = (2-2eps) m log2 m + (4-6eps) m. (4) F < 2m log2 m follows from (4-6eps) < 2eps log2 m, which holds when log2 m >= 2/eps, since 2eps*(2/eps) = 4 > 4-6eps. The threshold is m >= 2^(2/eps). QED. statement: PROOF. (a) Im psi is C-invariant, since C(psi(q)))=psi(delta(q)) lies in Im psi, and C restricted to Im psi equals psi delta psi^-1, a bijection. So Im psi is a union of cycles of the functional graph of C, and psi carries the cycles of delta onto distinct cycles of C. Hence the cycle type mu(delta) of delta on Q is a sub-multiset of lambda(C), the cycle type of C on its periodic points, a partition of some n<=N. (b) Let lambda be a partition of n<=N with multiplicities k_i. The number of sub-multisets of lambda is P(lambda)=prod(k_i+1). Put K=sqrt(2N), M=floor(K), a_i=i/K, phi_i(k)=log(k+1)-a_i k. For i<=M the maximum over integers k>=0 of phi_i is log(K/i)-1+i/K. For i>M the maximum is 0, since log(k+1)<=k<=a_i k. Weak duality: sum_i log(k_i+1)=sum_i phi_i(k_i)+(1/K) sum_i i k_i <= sum_{i<=M}[log(K/i)-1+i/K] + n/K. Use log M! >= M log M - M and that x log(K/x)+x is nondecreasing on (0,K] to get sum_{i<=M} log(K/i) <= K. Use M<=K, M>=K-1 to get sum_{i<=M}(-1+i/K) <= 3/2 - K/2. Total <= K/2 + N/K + 3/2 = sqrt(2N)+3/2, since K/2 = N/K = sqrt(N/2). So P(lambda) <= exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2). (c) Let B be the set of cycle types mu(delta) for which some psi gives CC_psi(delta)<=G. By (a), each mu in B is a sub-multiset of lambda(C) for some C of size <=G. By (b), |B| <= (G+1) N(S,G) exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2), where N(S,G) <= (16(S+G)^2)^G (S+G)^S counts circuit descriptions with G gates (each gate: type and two operands among <=S+G earlier nodes; each output: one node among <=S+G). (d) If p(m) > (G+1) N(S,G) exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2), some cycle type mu is not in B. Every delta of type mu has min over psi of CC_psi(delta) > G, so H(m) > G. (e) Asymptotics with G=floor(sqrt(m)/(2 log2 m)): ln N(S,G) <= G(ln m + 4.16) + S ln(2 sqrt m) <= 0.3466 sqrt(m)(1+o(1)) + O(log^2 m), using ln m / log2 m = ln 2. sqrt(2N) < 2 sqrt(m). By Hardy-Ramanujan (KNOWN, cited, not re-proved here), ln p(m) >= (pi sqrt(2/3)-o(1)) sqrt(m) = 2.565 sqrt(m)(1-o(1)). The gap is about 0.21 sqrt(m) minus O(log^2 m), so the inequality holds for all m >= m0. The threshold m0 is computed in the attached experiment (verification of the constants, not a proof of the threshold). SCOPE: stationary model only (one fixed psi per delta, one fixed circuit, values off the code image arbitrary, covers value-free unused codes). NOT COVERED: time-varying circuits, several codes per abstract state, and update-time versus gate count in a streaming system. Barrier label (diagnostic only): counting argument, not natural in the Razborov-Rudich sense; it is a lower bound for a single permutation's recoding, not a learner.

statement: LEMMA S0114-analytic (CLAIMED, session R1454, claude-haiku-5-5). Let m >= 64, L = log2 m, S = ceil(L), R = 2S, G = floor(m/2). For every injective E: Q -> {0,1}^R with |Q| = m, there is a pair (delta_0, delta_1) of maps Q->Q with CC_E > G, for circuits with fan-in 2, a fixed basis of at most 16 gate types, R+1 inputs and R outputs. PROOF. By S0038 it suffices that N(R,G) < m^(2m), where log2 N <= G(4+2 log2(R+G+1)) + R log2(R+G+2). Since S <= L+1, we have R <= 2L+2 and 2S+2 <= m/2 for m >= 64, so R+G+2 <= m and R+G+1 <= m, which gives log2(R+G+2) <= L and log2(R+G+1) <= L. Hence log2 N <= (m/2)(4+2L) + (2L+2)L = m(L+2) + 2L(L+1). The target 2mL exceeds this iff 2L(L+1) < m(L-2) = 2^L (L-2). This holds at L = 6 (84 < 256). For L >= 6 the LHS ratio (L+2)/L is at most 4/3 while the RHS ratio 2(L-1)/(L-2) is at least 2, so it holds for all L >= 6. QED. Scope: R = 2 ceil(log2 m), G = floor(m/2), m >= 64 (m a power of 2 in the formula; general m via L = log2 m). Existential in the pair, per encoding. Does not by itself close G0001 or G0002.

statement: PROOF. Let T be the set of maps delta' on Q whose transition on the codes E0(Q) is realised by a fan-in-2 circuit of size <= G (16-type basis, R+1 inputs, R outputs). Each circuit determines at most one delta', so |T| <= N(R,G). A map delta is bad iff some conjugate pi delta pi^-1 lies in T for some pi in Sym(Q). Hence the number of bad deltas is at most m! * |T| <= m! * N(R,G) < m^m = number of maps Q -> Q, so a good delta exists. Asymptotics: log2 m! = m log2 m - 1.4427 m + O(log m); for G <= m/(2S) we have log2(R+G+1) <= 1+log2 m, so log2 N <= m + 3m/log2 m + O(log^2 m). Thus log2 m! + log2 N <= m log2 m - 0.44 m + 3m/log2 m + O(log^2 m) < m log2 m for all sufficiently large m (explicit m0 not computed here). QED.

statement: LEMMA D*-corrected (kind LEMMA; closes G0050 part (a) only if the reviewer confirms that part (a) is this counting bound). For every integer N>=1 and every multiplicity vector (m_i) of nonnegative integers with sum_i i*m_i <= N: prod_i (m_i+1) <= exp(sqrt(2N) - 0.29). PROOF. Let s=sqrt(2N), K=round(s)>=1, so |K-s|<=1/2. For real x>=0 and 1<=i<=K, the concave function log(1+x)-(i/K)x is maximised at x=K/i-1>=0, giving log(1+x) <= (i/K)x + g(i), g(i)=log(K/i)-1+i/K. Since log t >= 1-1/t, g(i)>=0. For i>K, log(1+x) <= x <= (i/K)x. Summing with x=m_i: log prod(m_i+1) <= (1/K) sum_i i m_i + sum_{i=1}^K g(i) <= N/K + K log K - log K! - K + (K+1)/2. Stirling K! >= sqrt(2 pi K)(K/e)^K gives K log K - log K! <= K - (1/2)log(2 pi K), so the bound is <= N/K + K/2 + 1/2 - (1/2)log(2 pi K). Identity: N/K + K/2 = s + (K-s)^2/(2K) (using s^2=2N), and (K-s)^2/(2K) <= 1/8. Hence the bound is <= s + 1/8 + 1/2 - (1/2)log(2 pi) = s - 0.29394 <= s - 0.29. QED. Scope: all N>=1, no asymptotics. Note the constant 0.294 is NOT established (see refuted_approach).

label: S0178
statement: LEMMA D** (general N, replaces the -0.29 constant): for every integer N>=1 and nonnegative integers m_i with sum i*m_i <= N, prod(m_i+1) <= exp(sqrt(2N) - 1/2). PROOF: let M=floor(sqrt(2N)) (integer, M>=1), S=sqrt(2N)=M+f with 0<=f<1. Weak duality with K=M: log(1+m_i) = [log(1+m_i)-(i/M)m_i] + (i/M)m_i. The inner max over real x>=0 of log(1+x)-(i/M)x is g_i = log(M/i)-1+i/M for i<=M and 0 for i>M; and sum (i/M)m_i <= N/M. Hence log prod <= N/M + sum_{i<=M} g_i = N/M + M log M - log M! - M + (M+1)/2. Stirling M! >= sqrt(2 pi M)(M/e)^M gives log prod <= N/M + (M+1)/2 - (1/2)log(2 pi M). Since N/M = M/2 + f + f^2/(2M) and M+f=S, this is log prod <= S + [1/2 + f^2/(2M) - (1/2)log(2 pi M)] <= S + [1/2 + 1/(2M) - (1/2)log(2 pi M)]. For N>=2 (M>=2) the bracket is decreasing in M and at M=2 is 1/2+1/4-(1/2)log(4 pi) = -0.5155 < -1/2. For N=1: max prod = 2 and log 2 = 0.693 <= sqrt(2)-1/2 = 0.914. So the claim holds for all N>=1 with constant 1/2 (stronger than the stated 0.29).

label: S0181
statement: LEMMA P (pair quantifier order, R = ceil(log2 m)). Let m >= 256, L = log2 m, R = ceil(L), G = floor(m/4), Q = {0..m-1}. There is a pair (delta0, delta1) of maps Q->Q such that for EVERY injective E: Q->{0,1}^R, every fan-in-2 circuit over a fixed basis of at most 16 binary gate types on R+1 inputs and R outputs that computes (delta0, delta1) under E has more than G gates, i.e. CC_E(delta) > G. PROOF. (1) Counting circuits: N(R,G) <= (16 (R+G+1)^2)^G (R+G+2)^R, so log2 N <= G(4+2 log2(R+G+1)) + R log2(R+G+2). (2) Since m >= 256, m/4 >= L+3, so R+G+2 <= L+3+m/4 <= m/2, hence both logs are <= L-1, and log2 N <= (m/4)(4+2(L-1)) + (L+1)(L-1) = m(L+1)/2 + L^2 - 1. (3) Fix E. Let P_E be the set of pairs realised under E by a circuit of <= G gates. Each delta in P_E has a realising circuit; distinct pairs give distinct circuits, since the circuit's outputs on codes E(q) equal E(delta(q)) and E is injective, so the pair is recovered. Hence |P_E| <= N(R,G). (4) Union over E: the number of injective E is <= 2^(Rm), so |union_E P_E| <= 2^(Rm) N(R,G). (5) Rm + log2 N <= (L+1)m + m(L+1)/2 + L^2 - 1 = (3/2)(L+1)m + L^2 - 1 < 2mL, because this is equivalent to L^2 - 1 < m(L-3)/2 = 2^L (L-3)/2, which holds for all L >= 8. So 2^(Rm) N(R,G) < 2^(2mL) = m^(2m) = number of pairs, and some pair lies in no P_E. QED. Quantifier order: max over pairs, min over encodings; this is exactly the order that G0086 required. Scope: pairs of maps only; R = ceil(log2 m); G = floor(m/4); general m >= 256; circuits fan-in 2 over a fixed 16-type basis; values on unused codes free. NOT covered: single permutations (subclaim A). The same union bound over permutations fails at R = S: 2^(Rm) >= 2^(mL) > m!, so the count does not give max_delta min_E for permutations.

statement: LEMMA (circuit-count bound, fan-in 2, 16-type basis). Let C be a circuit with R+1 inputs, G gates, each gate of fan-in 2 with one of 16 Boolean types, and R designated outputs, where each output is a node or a constant. Gate i (1 <= i <= G) has at most R+i <= R+G earlier nodes, so its description is (type in 16, two input indices in a set of size <= R+G+1). Output j is one of the R+G+1 nodes or one of the constants (total <= R+G+2 choices). The map C -> (gate list, output list) is injective, so the number of such circuits N satisfies N <= (16 (R+G+1)^2)^G (R+G+2)^R. This is a complete argument for the stated model, not a review. It is claimed by a claude-haiku-5-5 session and needs cross-family review before any use as a premise.

label: S0205
statement: LEMMA R (repairs S0126 gaps (a),(b) by removing the m-to-2^S embedding; claimed by claude-haiku-5-5). Setting: S>=1, m>=2 with 2^S>=m, M=2^S. For a partition lambda of m let pi_lambda be a permutation of {0,1}^S with cycle type lambda plus M-m fixed points. h(pi) = least number of gates of a fan-in-2 circuit with S inputs and S outputs computing pi exactly. Statement: (i) lambda -> cycle type of pi_lambda is injective, so the p(m) functions pi_lambda are pairwise distinct. (ii) The number N_g of functions {0,1}^S->{0,1}^S computed by circuits with at most g gates satisfies N_g <= (g+1) 2^{L(g)}, where L(g) = (4g+S) log2(4(g+S)). (iii) If p(m) > (g+1) 2^{L(g)}, then max over lambda of h(pi_lambda) > g. Proof. (i) The cycle type of pi_lambda is the parts>=2 of lambda together with M - sum(parts>=2) fixed points. The parts>=2 determine lambda, because lambda has m - sum(parts>=2) parts equal to 1. (ii) Fix k<=g. A circuit with k gates is determined by, for each gate, one of 16 two-input Boolean functions and two predecessors among at most S+g nodes, and by one node (possibly a constant node) for each of the S outputs. With x = log2(S+g) the count is at most (16(S+g)^2)^k (S+g)^S <= 2^{g(4+2x)+Sx}. Since L(g) = (4g+S)(2+x) = (g(4+2x)+Sx) + 4g + 2S + 2gx, this is at most 2^{L(g)}. Summing over k<=g gives (g+1)2^{L(g)}. (iii) If every h(pi_lambda) <= g, the p(m) distinct functions pi_lambda are computed by circuits with at most g gates, so p(m) <= N_g, a contradiction. Scope: exact for every S>=1 and m with 2^S>=m; no numerics used in (i)-(iii). NOT proved here: (A) the inequality p(m) > (g+1)2^{L(g)} for g = floor(sqrt(M)/(4S)) for all S >= 14 (needs the analytic step S0087; checked numerically only, cm-129787680ca24eb6, S in [15,300], min margin 70.38); (B) the transfer of the padded bound to the m-state recoding model, which is the original obligation G0001 and remains OPEN. No P vs NP claim; no update-time bound.

label: S0210
statement: LEMMA (repair of S0126, closes its gaps (a)-(c) as stated; counting existence only; does NOT close G0001/G0002). Setting: S>=14, M=2^S, m with 2^(S-1) < m <= 2^S, g = floor(sqrt(M)/(4S)). For lambda |- m let pi_lambda be the permutation of {0,1}^S with cycle type lambda plus M-m fixed points, and h(pi) the minimum size of a fan-in-2 circuit with S inputs and S outputs computing pi. CLAIM: max over lambda |- m of h(pi_lambda) >= g+1 whenever (i) p(m) > (g+1) 2^{B(S,g)}, B = g(4+2log2(S+g)) + S log2(S+g), and (ii) the margin in (i) holds (checked: S=14..80 numerically at worst m = 2^(S-1)+1; S>=20 analytically). PROOF. (1) Injection: for a set A of distinct parts from {1..k-2}, with k = max{k: k(k+1)/2 <= m}, map A to the partition A + {m - sum(A)}. Since sum(A) <= (k-2)(k-1)/2, m - sum(A) >= 2k-1 > k-2, so the unique part exceeding k-2 recovers sum(A) and then A; hence the map is injective and p(m) >= 2^(k-2). Also k > sqrt(2m) - 1.5 from (k+1)(k+2)/2 > m. (2) Distinct lambda give distinct permutations pi_lambda (distinct cycle types), so there are p(m) distinct functions. (3) A circuit computes one function, so #{lambda : h(pi_lambda) <= g} <= #{circuits with <= g gates} <= (g+1)*(16 (S+g)^2)^g * (S+g)^S = (g+1) 2^{B(S,g)}, by choosing per gate two inputs among S+g nodes and one of 16 binary ops, and per output one of S+g nodes. (4) If (i) holds, some lambda has h(pi_lambda) > g. No embedding into a larger permutation is needed: the count is over functions on {0,1}^S, so the padding gaps (a),(b) do not arise. (5) Tail, S>=20: 2^(S/2)-3.5 < k-2 and log2 of the circuit count <= (S+6)/(4S) 2^(S/2) + S^2/2 + 1.5S, using g <= 2^(S/2)/(4S), S+g <= 2^(S/2+1), log2(g+1) <= S/2; the difference is positive from S=20 (~0.65*2^(S/2) minus a quadratic). Checks: cm-e9dc0600a62c4bb0 (exact recheck of the weaker bound log2 p(m) >= (k-2) - log2((k-2)(k-1)/2+1) against p(m) for m=10..400, no violations; margin positive for S=14..80, min 30.47); tail check run in the next TOOL_CALL. Gap (c) is resolved by (5) for S>=20 and by the numerical check for 14..19. Not verified by a non-Haiku session: CLAIMED until reviewed. No update-time bound, no P vs NP claim.

label: S0215
statement: LEMMA R-S0126 (repair of gaps (a),(b) of S0126). Setting: m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), M=2^S, g=floor(sqrt(M)/(4S)). For lambda |- m let pi_lambda be a permutation of {0,1}^S with cycle type lambda plus M-m fixed points. A circuit: fan-in-2 DAG of binary gates (16 ops, constants included) on S inputs with S output nodes; size = number of gates; h(pi) = min size of a circuit computing pi as a function on ALL of {0,1}^S (unused codes are part of the function; no padding argument). CLAIM: if p(m) > (g+1)*C_g with C_g = (16(S+g)^2)^g (S+g)^S, then some lambda |- m has h(pi_lambda) > g. PROOF: (1) distinct lambda give distinct pi_lambda: cycle-length multiset of pi_lambda is lambda + (M-m) ones; the count of 1-cycles is count_1(lambda)+M-m, and the count of each part k>=2 is count_k(lambda); so lambda is recovered. (2) A circuit of size k is given by k gates (i,j,op) with i,j among at most S+k-1 earlier nodes and op among 16, plus S output selectors among at most S+k nodes; so #circuits of size k <= (16(S+k)^2)^k (S+k)^S, which is nondecreasing in k, so F_g (functions computed by size <= g) has |F_g| <= (g+1) C_g. (3) If h(pi_lambda) <= g for all lambda, the p(m) distinct functions pi_lambda lie in F_g, so p(m) <= (g+1) C_g: contradiction. QED. CONSEQUENCE: log2 C_g = 4g + (2g+S)x with x = log2(S+g) <= (4g+S)log2(4(g+S)) = L(g) (difference 4g+2S+2gx >= 0), so log2((g+1)C_g) <= log2(g+1)+L(g) <= sqrt(M)/2 + (S^2+S)/2 (the S0087(2)-(3) chain used in S0126, cited; checked for S=14..200 by my own code). With sqrt(M) <= sqrt(2m) and log2 p(m) >= sqrt(2m)-3 (S0087(1), cited, checked for m<=3000 only), the lemma applies whenever sqrt(2m) > S^2+S+6, the S0126 condition. For S=14..16 this covers only the upper part of the block.

label: S0220
statement: S-SUBMULTISET-UB (upper bound, CLAIMED): Let M have multiplicities m_i >= 0 of part i with sum_i i*m_i <= n. Then for every integer K >= 1, ln prod_i (m_i+1) <= n/K + sum_{i=1}^{K-1} (i/K - 1 - ln(i/K)). Proof: weak Lagrangian duality with lambda = 1/K gives ln(m+1) - (i/K)m <= max_{m>=0} of that expression, which equals -ln(i/K) - 1 + i/K for i < K and 0 for i >= K. The sum over i=1..K-1 of i/K is (K-1)/2, so the bracket equals L - (K-1)/2 with L = ln(K^{K-1}/(K-1)!). Since (K-1)! >= ((K-1)/e)^{K-1}, L <= (K-1)(1 + ln(K/(K-1))) <= K. Hence ln max <= n/K + (K-1)/2 + 1. With K = ceil(sqrt(2n)): n/K <= sqrt(2n)/2 and (K-1)/2 < sqrt(2n)/2, so ln max < sqrt(2n) + 1.

structure.gap: (1) The LOWER bound ln max >= (1-o(1)) sqrt(2n) is NOT proved. The Lagrangian heuristic in my earlier step does not prove it, and I withdraw it. What is rigorous: take m_i = floor(a/i) for i <= a. Then ln(m_i+1) >= ln(a/i), so the value is >= a - O(log a). The cost is sum_{i<=a} i*floor(a/i) = sum_{j<=a} sigma(j) ~ (pi^2/12) a^2 (classical divisor-sum asymptotic). Taking a ~ sqrt(12n)/pi gives ln max >= (1-o(1)) sqrt(12n)/pi ~ 0.78 sqrt(2n). The crude cost bound a^2 <= n gives only 0.707 sqrt(2n). The constant 1 in exp((1+o(1)) sqrt(2n)) is therefore OPEN. It needs a construction that closes the rounding gap of floor(K/i) at parts i in (K/2, K), where the integer optimum takes m_i in {0,1} and the continuous optimum is fractional. (2) The formal count prod(m_i+1) is exact. (3) Numerics for n <= 50 show ln(max)/sqrt(2n) rising 0.55 -> 0.83, which is consistent with limit 1 but is not evidence for it.

label: S0221
statement: S-SUBMULTISET-LB-081 (CLAIMED): For every n, ln max_M prod_i (m_i+1) >= (0.81 - o(1)) sqrt(2n). Construction: let L = floor(sqrt(n/(e-1/2))), c = floor(eL), and take m_i = floor(c/i) - 1 for 1 <= i <= L, and m_i = 0 otherwise. Proof: (a) cost: sum_{i<=L} i*m_i <= sum_{i<=L} (c - i) <= eL^2 - L^2/2 + O(L) <= n. (b) rounding: for i <= L, x = i/c <= 1/e, and ln floor(c/i) >= ln(c/i) + ln(1-x) >= ln(c/i) - 1.582 x, so sum_{i<=L} ln(m_i+1) >= sum_{i<=L} ln(c/i) - 1.582 * L^2/(2c) = L ln c - ln(L!) - 0.291 L + o(L). (c) Stirling with c = eL(1+o(1)): L ln c - ln L! = 2L + o(L). Hence ln M(n) >= 1.709 L + o(L) = 1.709 * 0.6715 sqrt(n) + o(sqrt n) = 1.1476 sqrt(n) + o(sqrt n) = 0.8115 sqrt(2n) + o(sqrt(2n)).

statement: S0126-R (REPAIR of S0126; replaces its gaps (a)-(c)). Setting: m>=8, S=ceil(log2 m), M=2^S, x=sqrt(2m). Circuits: fan-in-2 gates, 16 binary ops, S inputs, S output wires; size = number of gates. h(lambda) := min circuit size over ALL permutations sigma of {0,1}^S with cycle type lambda u 1^(M-m). STATEMENT: if S <= g, g>=1, g <= x and g(8+3log2 x) <= x-5, then there is a partition lambda of m with h(lambda) >= g+1, i.e. every permutation of that cycle type needs more than g gates. Corollary: with g = floor((x-5)/(8+3log2 x)) (when S<=g) max_lambda h(lambda) > (sqrt(2m)-5)/(8+3log2 sqrt(2m)) = Omega(sqrt(m)/log m). PROOF. Step 1 (family): F = partitions of m into DISTINCT parts. Let k = floor(x)-2, K = k(k+1)/2. Map A (subset of {1..k}, sum(A) <= K/2) to partition A u {m - sum A}; the extra part is >= k+1 > all parts of A, so parts are distinct, and A is recovered from the parts <= k (injective). Complement A -> {1..k}\A sends sum s to K-s, so #{sum<=K/2} = #{sum>=K/2} and their union covers 2^k subsets: #{sum<=K/2} >= 2^(k-1). Condition K/2 <= m-k-1 holds: (k^2+5k+4)/4 <= (2m+x-2)/4 <= m using k<=x-2 and x-2<=2m. Hence |F| >= 2^(k-1) >= 2^(x-4) since k-1 = floor(x)-3 >= x-4. Step 2 (injective cycle types): the M-point cycle type lambda u 1^(M-m) determines lambda (remove M-m fixed points), so distinct lambda in F give distinct cycle types, and permutations of distinct cycle types are distinct functions. Step 3 (counting): the number of functions computed by circuits of <= g gates is at most 2^Lambda, Lambda = log2(g+1)+g(4+2log2(S+g))+S log2(S+g); descriptions with k'<=g gates number at most (g+1)(16(S+g)^2)^g (S+g)^S. Using S<=g<=x: S+g<=2g<=2x, log2(g+1)<=g, so Lambda <= g + g(6+2log2 x) + g(1+log2 x) = g(8+3log2 x) <= x-5. Step 4 (contradiction): if h(lambda)<=g for all lambda in F, choose for each lambda a circuit of <= g gates computing some sigma_lambda of type lambda; the sigma_lambda are pairwise distinct (distinct cycle types), so 2^(x-4) <= |F| <= 2^Lambda <= 2^(x-5), contradiction. QED. SCOPE: min over ALL permutations of {0,1}^S, so for any encoding set Psi (injective encodings of Q included) min_{psi in Psi} CC(psi delta psi^-1) >= h(lambda) >= g+1 for every delta of cycle type lambda (conjugation preserves cycle type, and all permutations of one cycle type are conjugate). This is a LOWER bound only; no update-time bound; circuit model fixed as above; the hypothesis S<=g is an explicit condition (holds for m around 2^18 and beyond, checked numerically in the next evidence record). It does not by itself close G0001/G0002 (their text was not checked here, so no closes= is claimed).

statement: LEMMA R (restriction to sub-multisets; Claim A item 2). Setting: S>=1, C any function {0,1}^S -> {0,1}^S (values on unused codes arbitrary), fan-in-2 circuits over a fixed complete basis. M(n) = max over mu with sum_i i*mu_i <= n of prod_i (mu_i+1). (a) If Q subset {0,1}^S, C(Q) subset Q, and C restricted to Q is a permutation of cycle type lambda |- m, then lambda is the cycle type of a sub-multiset of the cycles of C's functional graph, and one C realises at most M(2^S) cycle types. Proof: for q in Q the C-orbit of q is periodic and stays in Q, so it equals the C|Q-cycle through q. Hence the C|Q-cycles are disjoint cycles of C with total length m <= 2^S. The cycle lengths of C have multiplicities mu_i with sum_i i*mu_i <= 2^S, and the number of their sub-multisets is prod_i (mu_i+1) <= M(2^S). (b) Counting: let N(G,S) = (16(S+G)^2)^G (S+G)^S, an upper bound on the number of circuits with G gates, S inputs and S outputs. Let psi: Q -> {0,1}^S be injective. If every lambda |- m has a permutation delta_lambda on Q with circuit size <= G realising it via psi, then choosing one circuit C_lambda per lambda, each circuit serves at most M(2^S) values of lambda by (a). So p(m) <= N(G,S) * M(2^S). Hence if p(m) > N(G,S) M(2^S), some lambda has circuit size > G. (c) Asymptotics (log base 2, S = ceil(log2 m), 2^S < 2m): log2 p(m) = (3.700+o(1)) sqrt(m), since pi*sqrt(2/3)/ln 2 = 3.700. log2 M(2^S) <= (2.885+o(1)) sqrt(m), using ln M(n) <= sqrt(2n)+1 (S0220) with n < 2m. log2 N(G,S) <= 2 G log2 G + O(G + S log G). So max over lambda of the circuit size is >= (0.815 - o(1)) sqrt(m) / log2(m). Scope: counting existence only; no update-time bound; for any m-state permutation with injective S-bit encoding and fan-in-2 circuits. Uses S0220 (CLAIMED) as input. Does not close G0001 or G0002.

statement: Fixed-psi counting bound: for every integer m >= 256 with S = ceil(log2 m), some bijection of the m used S-bit codes is not the restriction of any fan-in-2 circuit with at most floor(m/4) gates. Statement and complete proof in the lemma field.

structure.evidence: Analytic proof in the lemma field. Numerical replication cm-2368707d761e42b0 (own formula, m = 256..200000 and powers of two 2^8..2^60): 0 failures, minimum margin log2(m!) - log2 N at m = 260 (ratio 2.24 per m); it replicates the arithmetic only and is not independent of the proof.
structure.lemma: Fixed-psi counting bound. Let m >= 256, S = ceil(log2 m), G = floor(m/4), T = S+G+2, L = log2 m. Let a 'circuit' be a fan-in-2 circuit with S input wires and at most G gates, with an output map of S wires. Claim: log2(m!) > log2(G+1) + G(4 + 2 log2 T) + S log2 T. Hence for m >= 256 there is a bijection of the set of m used codes that is the restriction to those codes of no circuit of size <= G. PROOF. (1) Each gate chooses two of at most S+G earlier wires and one of 16 binary functions, so the number of circuits of size exactly g is at most (16(S+G)^2)^g * (S+G)^S, and the number of size <= G is at most (G+1)(16(S+G)^2)^G (S+G)^S. (2) T <= m for m >= 256 (since 3m/4 >= L+3), so log2 T <= L; S <= L+1; log2(G+1) <= L; G(4+2 log2 T) <= m + mL/2. So log2 #circuits <= m + mL/2 + L^2 + 2L. (3) m! >= (m/e)^m gives log2 m! >= m(L - log2 e). (4) Need m(L/2 - 2.4427) > L^2 + 2L. At L = 8 (m = 256): 398.7 > 80. The difference h(L) = 2^L(L/2 - 2.4427) - L^2 - 2L has h(8) > 0 and h'(L) > 2^L*1.5 - 2L - 2 > 0 for L >= 8, so h > 0 for all m >= 256. Then #circuits < m!, so some bijection of the m used codes is not realised. QED. SCOPE: a counting existence bound, linear in m, for a single permutation of m states with S-bit inputs. It is NOT a conjugation-cost bound (no max over delta of min over psi of CC(psi delta psi^-1)), NOT an update-time bound, and it does not close G0001 or G0002. Its relation to the subclaim-A lower bound Omega(sqrt m / log m) is open.

statement: REPAIR of S0126 (Haiku-authored, needs a non-Haiku review). Let m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m) >= 14, M=2^S, x=2^(S/2), g=floor(sqrt(M)/(4S)). For lambda a partition of m let pi_lambda be the permutation of {0,1}^S with cycle type lambda plus M-m fixed points, and h = min fan-in-2 circuit size (16 gate types, S inputs and S outputs). CLAIM: some lambda |- m has h(pi_lambda) >= g+1. PROOF. (1) Distinct lambda give distinct permutations; a circuit computes one function. If all h <= g, pick one circuit per lambda: p(m) distinct circuits of size <= g. (2) Circuits of size <= g: at most (g+1) sizes; each gate has 16*(S+g)^2 choices; S outputs among S+g nodes. So #circuits <= 2^rhs with rhs = log2(g+1) + g(4+2log2(S+g)) + S log2(S+g). (3) Let k = max{k: k(k+1)/2 <= m}, K = k(k+1)/2 <= m. Pigeonhole over the 2^k subsets of {1..k}, whose sums lie in {0..K}, gives T <= m with >= 2^k/(K+1) partitions of T into distinct parts; p monotone gives log2 p(m) >= k - log2(K+1). From m < (k+2)^2/2 we get k >= sqrt(2m)-2; from m <= 2^S, log2(K+1) <= S+1. With sqrt(2m) > x: log2 p(m) >= x - S - 3. (4) For S >= 14: rhs <= S/2 + x/3 + S^2/2 (use S+g <= x, g(S+4) <= x(S+4)/(4S) <= x/3). So p(m) > 2^rhs follows from (2/3)x > Q(S) := S^2/2 + 3S/2 + 3. This holds at S=16 (170.7 > 155) and propagates: x grows by sqrt2 per step while Q(S+1) <= 1.2 Q(S) for S >= 16. S=14,15 directly: x-S-3 = 111.0 > 81.58 and 163.0 > 101.6. Hence step (1) gives a contradiction, so some lambda has h >= g+1. SCOPE: counting existence only; no update-time bound; closes neither G0001 nor G0002. The earlier gaps (a),(b),(c) of S0126 are not needed: the argument counts circuits on S inputs directly, so no embedding is used, and the condition sqrt(2m) > S^2+S+6 is not used.

label: S0240
statement: LEMMA L-cyc (Haiku-authored, CLAIMED, needs a non-Haiku review). Setting: m >= 2, S = ceil(log2 m), M = 2^S, so m <= M <= 2m. Circuits: fan-in-2 over basis B2 (16 functions), S inputs, S outputs (the next-state map of a permutation of {0,1}^S), size = number of gates. Statement: let C(g,S) = sum_{k<=g} (16(S+k)^2)^k (S+k)^S. If C(g,S) < p(m), then there is lambda |- m such that every permutation pi of {0,1}^S with cycle type lambda + 1^(M-m) has circuit size > g. PROOF. (i) Each circuit of size <= g computes one function, hence at most one permutation, hence has at most one cycle type; so at most C(g,S) cycle types are realised by circuits of size <= g. (ii) Distinct lambda |- m give distinct types lambda + 1^(M-m) on M points (the number of 1-cycles is #1(lambda) + M - m, and removing M-m ones recovers lambda). So there are p(m) types. (iii) Since C(g,S) < p(m), some type is realised by no circuit of size <= g. (iv) Quantifier order: for a delta of cycle type lambda on Q, every conjugate psi delta psi^-1 (psi an injection Q -> {0,1}^S, extended by the identity on the M-m unused codes) is a permutation of {0,1}^S of type lambda + 1^(M-m), so CC(psi delta psi^-1) > g for every psi. Hence max_delta min_psi CC > g. QED. ASYMPTOTICS: take g = floor(sqrt(m)/log2 m). Then log2(g+1) <= (1/2)log2 m, log2(S+g) <= (1/2)log2 m for large m, g(4+2log2(S+g)) <= sqrt(m)(1+4/log2 m), and S log2(S+g) = O(log^2 m). So log2 C(g,S) <= 1.1 sqrt(m) for large m, while log2 p(m) >= sqrt(2m) - 3 (S0087(1)) is about 1.41 sqrt(m). So C(g,S) < p(m) for all m >= m0, with m0 finite but not computed here. Gives max_delta min_psi CC = Omega(sqrt(m)/log m), the lower-bound half of subclaim A, for the circuit-size measure above. Barrier labels (diagnostic): relativises (pure counting); not natural in the Razborov-Rudich sense (the property 'cycle type lambda' is a single-permutation property realised by a vanishing fraction of permutations). Gives no update-time bound and no learner. Does not by itself address the spec's CC measure if that measure differs from circuit size on B2 with S-bit state. Closes: subclaim A lower bound, reviewer to set closes.

label: S0249
statement: Cycle-type pigeonhole lemma. Let m >= 2, S = ceil(log2 m), p(m) the partition function, g >= 1 with log2 p(m) > log2(g+1) + g(4 + 2 log2(S+g)) + S log2(S+g). Then max_delta min_psi CC(psi delta psi^-1) >= g, where delta ranges over Sym(m), psi over injections [m] -> {0,1}^S, CC = min fan-in-2 circuit size on S inputs/outputs of the padded map F (identity off Im psi). Proof: (1) f(delta)=min_psi CC depends only on cycle type (psi -> psi sigma absorbs conjugation). (2) If f(lambda)<g for all lambda, pick psi_lambda and circuit C_lambda of size<g computing F_lambda. (3) F_lambda has cycle type lambda plus 1^(2^S-m), so distinct lambda give distinct F_lambda: p(m) distinct maps computed by size<g circuits. (4) Counting gates (16 types, two inputs among <=S+g nodes) and S output pointers gives at most 2^rhs(g,S) such circuits; contradiction. Asymptotically g ~ 3.7 sqrt(m)/log2 m.

label: S0251
statement: L-REPAIR (repairs the S0126 gap (a)-(c); replaces the injectivity step that S0249 used). Setting: m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), M=2^S, so m<=M<2m. B is a fixed finite basis of binary Boolean functions, b=|B|. CC = number of gates of a fan-in-2 circuit over B. A circuit C with S inputs and S outputs computes f_C: {0,1}^S -> {0,1}^S on ALL codes (unused codes are part of f_C, so nothing is padded). For a function f, tau(f) = set of cycle types lambda |- m such that some m-subset A is f-invariant and f|A is a permutation of cycle type lambda. mu_i(f) = number of periodic cycles of f of length i. CLAIM (i): |tau(f)| <= prod_i (mu_i+1) <= e^(1/2) exp(sqrt(2M)) <= 2 exp(2 sqrt m). CLAIM (ii): N(G) = #{f_C : CC(C)<=G} <= 2^{c_B (G+S) log2(S+G+1)} with c_B = log2 b + 2. CLAIM (iii): if max_delta min_psi CC(psi delta psi^-1) <= G then p(m) <= 2 exp(2 sqrt m) N(G). CLAIM (iv): for m >= m_0 (absolute constant, using the cited Hardy-Ramanujan asymptotic ln p(m) ~ pi sqrt(2m/3) >= 2.5 sqrt m), max_delta min_psi CC >= G_m+1 with G_m = floor(sqrt m / (8 c_B log2(2m))) = Omega(sqrt m / log m). PROOF (i): if A is f-invariant with f|A bijective, every point of A lies on a periodic cycle of f and A is a union of such cycles. So the cycle-length multiset of lambda is a sub-multiset of the periodic-cycle length multiset (mu_i copies of i). The number of sub-multisets is at most prod(mu_i+1). Constraint: sum_i i mu_i <= M, since periodic points are distinct. Elementary inequality: for x>0, a>=0, log(1+a) <= x a + h(x), where h(x)=x-1-log x for x<=1 and h(x)=0 for x>1 (the max over a>=0 of log(1+a)-xa is at a=1/x-1 when x<=1 and at a=0 when x>1). Put K=sqrt(2M), x=i/K. Then log prod <= M/K + sum_{i<=K} h(i/K). With J=floor(K) and log J! >= J log J - J + 1 and log(K/J) <= (K-J)/J < 1/J: sum_{i<=J} h(i/K) = J(J+1)/(2K) - J + J log K - log J! <= J(J+1)/(2K) + J log(K/J) - 1 < (K+1)/2. Hence log prod <= sqrt(2M)/2 + (sqrt(2M)/2 + 1/2) = sqrt(2M) + 1/2. PROOF (ii): a circuit has G gates; each gate picks an op from B and two earlier nodes (at most (S+G)^2 choices); the S outputs pick nodes among S+G. So N(G) <= (b(S+G)^2)^G (S+G)^S <= 2^{c_B (G+S) log2(S+G+1)}. PROOF (iii): for each delta of type lambda, the hypothesis gives psi and a circuit C_lambda with CC<=G agreeing with psi delta psi^-1 on A=Im psi, so lambda is in tau(f_{C_lambda}). Every lambda |- m is covered by the image of this choice map, and each f covers at most 2exp(2 sqrt m) types by (i). Hence p(m) <= N(G) * 2exp(2 sqrt m). PROOF (iv): the inequality needs 0.5 sqrt m > ln2 + ln N(G). With G=G_m, c_B G log2(2m) <= sqrt m/8, and S<=log2 m+1 makes the S-term O(log^2 m) = o(sqrt m). So the inequality holds for m >= m_0. SCOPE: counting bound for the free-extension model with fixed basis B. Uses the cited asymptotic for p(m) and no injectivity lambda -> circuit. NOT CLAIMED: an update-time bound, closure of G0001 or G0002, any P vs NP progress. m_0 is not made explicit. Status: CLAIMED, Haiku-authored, needs a non-Haiku

label: S0254
statement: LEMMA P2 (power-of-two case). Let m = 2^S, S >= 2, states identified with {0,1}^S (psi bijective, so no free codes). CC(F) = min number of fan-in-2 gates over at most 16 binary ops computing F: {0,1}^S -> {0,1}^S. val(delta) = min over bijections psi of CC(psi delta psi^-1) for delta in Sym(m). Claim: for every S >= S0 (explicit threshold from the arithmetic check) there is delta with val(delta) > floor(sqrt(m)/S). Proof: (1) conjugation: psi delta psi^-1 ranges over all permutations of the cycle type of delta, so val depends only on the cycle type. (2) Circuits with <= s gates: gate i picks one of 16 ops and an ordered pair among S+i-1 earlier nodes; S outputs are chosen among S+g nodes; so #circuits <= U(s) = (s+1) 16^s (S+s)^(2s+S), and each computes at most one function. (3) Cycle types realised by permutations of CC <= s number at most U(s). If U(s) < p(m) (partition count), some type is unrealised, and any delta of that type has val > s. (4) Erdos-type bound (literature, to verify): log2 p(m) >= c sqrt(m) - log2(4 sqrt(3) m), c = pi sqrt(2/3)/ln 2 ~ 3.70. With s = floor(sqrt(m)/S), S+s <= sqrt(m) for large S, so log2 U(s) <= log2(s+1) + 4s + (2s+S) S/2 <= sqrt(m)(1+o(1)) < c sqrt(m) - log2(4 sqrt(3) m) for large S. Scope: m = 2^S only. This is Claim A's lower bound Omega(sqrt m / log m) for power-of-two m. It does NOT close G0142 (non-power-of-two m, image sets, free codes). Not a P vs NP step. Diagnostic: pure counting, no oracle.
