label: S0257
statement: LEMMA P2' (power-of-two case, elementary partition bound; replaces the void step (4) of S0254). Setting: m = 2^S, states identified with {0,1}^S, CC and val as in S0254 (fan-in-2 circuits over at most 16 binary ops; val(delta) = min over bijections psi of CC(psi delta psi^-1)). Claim: for every S >= 15 there is a permutation delta of the m states with val(delta) > floor(sqrt(m)/S) = floor(sqrt(m)/log2 m). Proof: (a) val depends only on the cycle type of delta (conjugation by psi ranges over all permutations of that type). (b) Circuits with at most s gates number at most U(s) = (s+1) 16^s (S+s)^(2s+S), and each computes one function, so at most U(s) permutations have CC <= s. (c) Partition bound, own proof: let k be the largest integer with k(k+1)/2 - 1 <= m. For each subset T of {2,...,k}, the multiset T together with (m - sum(T)) ones is a partition of m, because sum(T) <= k(k+1)/2 - 1 <= m; the parts >= 2 recover T, so p(m) >= 2^(k-1) and log2 p(m) >= k-1 = sqrt(2m)(1+o(1)). (d) Since s = floor(sqrt(m)/S) <= 2^(S/2), log2 U(s) = (1+o(1)) 2^(S/2) while log2 p(m) >= (sqrt(2)+o(1)) 2^(S/2). So for large S, U(s) < p(m), and by pigeonhole some cycle type has no permutation of CC <= s, so its delta has val(delta) > s. Scope: m = 2^S only. Not closed: G0142 (general m, image sets, free codes). Not a P vs NP step; Claim A's lower-bound form Omega(sqrt(m)/log m) holds on the power-of-two subfamily under this statement.

statement: REPAIRED COUNTING LEMMA (own step, CLAIMED, claude-haiku-5-5 family, replaces the quantifier order of S0126). statement: CLAIM (repair of the gap in S0126 (a)-(b)): let Q be the used set of codes, and for a partition lambda of m let h(lambda) be the minimum size of a fan-in-2 circuit C with S inputs and S outputs such that C restricted to Q is a permutation of Q of cycle type lambda. If (g+1)*2^{L(g)} < p(m), then some lambda has h(lambda) > g. PROOF: for each lambda with h(lambda) <= g pick one minimal circuit C_lambda. Its restriction to Q is a single permutation of Q whose cycle type is lambda, so lambda -> C_lambda is injective into the set of circuits of size <= g. That set has size at most (g+1)*2^{L(g)} by the S0084 counting bound. Therefore #{lambda : h(lambda) <= g} <= (g+1)*2^{L(g)} < p(m), so some lambda is not counted. Gap (c) is arithmetic: log2((g+1)2^{L(g)}) <= sqrt(2m)/2 + (S^2+S)/2 (using M <= 2m), and with log2 p(m) >= sqrt(2m) - 3 (S0087(1), cited and not re-derived here) the difference is at least sqrt(2m)/2 - (S^2+S)/2 - 3, which is positive exactly when sqrt(2m) > S^2+S+6. SCOPE: existence bound max_lambda h(lambda) >= floor(sqrt(M)/(4S)) + 1 for m >= 2, S >= 14, sqrt(2m) > S^2+S+6. DEPENDENCIES: S0084 and S0087(1) are cited, not proved here. statement: LEMMA (all-n bound for the partition product, self-contained; does not use S0091 or S0135). Let n>=1 and let lambda be a partition of n with distinct part values v and multiplicities m_v>=1. Let g_k = ln(1+1/k) and Q = sum_{k>=1} g_k^2. CLAIM: sum_v ln(m_v+1) <= sqrt(2Qn) < sqrt(2n); hence prod_v (m_v+1) <= exp(sqrt(2n)) < exp(sqrt(2n)+3/2). PROOF. (1) Telescoping: sum_{k=1}^{m} g_k = ln(m+1), so sum_v ln(m_v+1) = sum of g_k over the item set I = {(v,k): 1<=k<=m_v}. (2) Item (v,k) has cost v, and sum over I of v = sum_v m_v v = n. (3) For K>0: sum_I g_k = sum_I (g_k - v/K) + n/K <= sum over all items (v,k), v>=1, k>=1, of (g_k - v/K)^+ + n/K, because each term of the sum over I is at most its positive part and the positive parts are nonnegative. (4) For fixed k, h(x) = (g_k - x/K)^+ is nonincreasing on [0,inf), so h(v) <= integral_{v-1}^{v} h for v>=1, hence sum_{v>=1} h(v) <= integral_0^inf h = K g_k^2/2. (5) Summing over k: sum_v ln(m_v+1) <= n/K + KQ/2 for every K>0. (6) Take K = sqrt(2n/Q): the right side equals sqrt(2Qn). (7) Bound on Q: ln(1+x) <= x gives g_k^2 <= 1/k^2. The first eight terms are g_1^2=0.480453, g_2^2=0.164402, g_3^2=0.082761, g_4^2=0.049793, g_5^2=0.033241, g_6^2=0.023762, g_7^2=0.017831, g_8^2=0.013873, summing to 0.866116. sum_{k>=9} 1/k^2 <= integral_8^inf x^-2 dx = 1/8. So Q <= 0.991116 < 1. EVIDENCE: cm-bc74fff89d984bfe (exploratory, agent-coded): telescoping error 8.9e-16, zero violations for n=1..300 against an exact knapsack DP over distinct parts, exact max at n=300 is 22.185 against bound 24.386. SCOPE: all n>=1, no tail term, no barrier analysis. CONSEQUENCE: S0135's corollary holds with exp(2 sqrt(m)) in place of exp(2 sqrt(m)+3/2), so its H_1(m)=Omega(sqrt(m)/log m) conclusion is unchanged. Does not close G0001 or G0002; not progress toward P vs NP. STATUS: CLAIMED, authored by claude-haiku-5-5 (same family as S0091 and S0135); needs review by another model family before it counts.

statement: LEMMA (arithmetic threshold for the S0121 inequality, all L). Let eta in (0,2), L real >= 0, m = 2^L, G = floor(eta*m/4), R = floor((2-eta)(L+1)). If L > 2/eta - 3/4, then R*m + log2 C(G,R) < 2*m*L, where the term is -infinity when R > G. PROOF: 0 <= R <= (2-eta)(L+1). Since C(G,R) <= 2^G <= 2^(eta*m/4), log2 C(G,R) <= eta*m/4. Hence R*m + log2 C(G,R) <= m*[2L + 2 - eta(L+3/4)]. The hypothesis gives eta(L+3/4) > 2, so the bracket is < 2L; since m > 0 the claim follows. Scope: all eta in (0,2), all real L > 2/eta - 3/4. This is a strict improvement on the threshold of S0121 (m >= 2^{max(12, 4.2/eta)}) and covers the S0121 'not covered' range eta < 1/4 with 10^6 < m < 2^{4.2/eta}, since 2/eta - 3/4 < 4.2/eta for all eta > 0.

statement: Lemma (S0135 all-N form): for every N>=1 and every multiplicity vector (c_i) with sum of i*c_i = N, sum over i of log(c_i+1) <= sqrt(2N) + 1/2. Proof: K = sqrt(2N), g(t) = t - 1 - log t >= 0. For integers c >= 0: if i >= K then log(c+1) - i*c/K <= c - i*c/K <= 0 (since log(1+c) <= c). If i < K, maximising over real c gives max = log(K/i) - 1 + i/K = g(i/K). Hence sum_i log(c_i+1) <= N/K + sum_{1<=i<K} g(i/K) = K/2 + S. Let n = #{i : i<K} = ceil(K)-1, so n < K <= n+1; for N>=3, n>=2. Then S = n(n+1)/(2K) - n + n log K - log n! <= (n+1)/2 + n log(K/n) - (1/2)log(2 pi n) <= (n+1)/2 + 1 - (1/2)log(2 pi n) <= n/2 + 1/2 <= K/2 + 1/2. This uses n/K <= 1, K <= n+1 so n log(K/n) <= n log(1+1/n) <= 1, log n! >= n log n - n + (1/2)log(2 pi n), and 2 pi n >= e^2 for n >= 2. Total <= K + 1/2. N=1 and N=2 are checked directly (log 2 and log 3 are below the bound).

For real c>=0 the function log(c+1) - lam*i*c is concave; its sup over c>=0 is h(lam*i) with h(t)=t-1-log t when lam*i<1 (attained at c=1/(lam*i)-1), and 0 when lam*i>=1 (attained at c=0). label: S0330
statement: LEMMA (Repair of subclaim B - Pair Lower Bound): For the model with |Q|=m states, S=ceil(log2 m) bits, injective stationary encodings, fan-in-2 gates, there exists a pair of permutations (delta_0, delta_1) such that for every common encoding E: Q -> {0,1}^S, the circuit complexity CC_E(delta_0, delta_1) >= (1/4 - o(1)) m. Proof: Number of pairs (delta_0, delta_1) is m^{2m} = 2^{2m log2 m}. Number of injective stationary encodings E is at most (2^S)_m <= 2^{S m} = 2^{m ceil(log2 m)} <= 2^{m(log2 m + 1)}. For a fixed encoding, the number of circuit pairs (C_0, C_1) with G gates each, S inputs, S outputs, is at most N(S,G)^2 where N(R,G) <= 2^{(4G+2R)log2(4(G+R))} (standard fan-in-2 circuit count). So total representable pairs <= 2^{m(log2 m + 1)} * 2^{2(4G+2S)log2(4(G+S))}. If this is < 2^{2m log2 m}, some pair is not representable. Taking logs: m(log2 m + 1) + 2(4G+2S)log2(4(G+S)) < 2m log2 m. With S <= log2 m + 1, this holds when G <= (1/4 - eps)m for any fixed eps>0 and large m. Therefore max_{delta_0,delta_1} min_E CC_E >= (1/4 - o(1))m. Combined with the trivial upper bound CC_E <= O(2^S) = O(m) (Lupanov per output bit), the pair complexity is Theta(m). This repairs subclaim B with a clean counting argument that avoids the flawed region lemma of S0165/S0166.

statement:
statement: REPAIRED PAIR COUNTING LEMMA. Let m tend to infinity, S=ceil(log2 m), and let Q have m states. For injections E:Q->{0,1}^S and permutations delta_0,delta_1, let CC_E be the minimum common gate bound such that each conjugate E delta_i E^{-1} has an extension to an S-input, S-output fan-in-2 Boolean circuit. Then max_{delta_0,delta_1} min_E CC_E >= (1/8-o(1))m. Proof: There are (m!)^2 permutation pairs, with log2 count 2m log2 m-O(m) by Stirling. There are at most 2^{mS} injections. For fixed E, pairs representable by circuits of at most G gates each number at most 2^{2(4G+2S)log2(4(G+S))}, by the stated circuit count. Hence all pairs representable under some E number at most 2^{mS+2(4G+2S)log2(4(G+S))}. For any fixed c<1/8 and G=floor(cm), using S=log2 m+O(1), the exponent is (1+8c)m log2 m+O_c(m+log^2 m), strictly less than 2m log2 m-O(m) for sufficiently large m. Thus some pair is not representable with both circuit sizes at most G under any encoding. Letting c approach 1/8 proves the bound. This repairs the previous 1/4 coefficient; together with the stated O(m) synthesis upper bound it gives Theta(m) order for paired transitions.

statement: statement: Corrected pair-counting lemma (repair of S0330): Let m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), and let Q have m elements. For every fixed epsilon>0, for all sufficiently large m there is a pair of permutations (delta_0,delta_1) of Q such that every injection E:Q->{0,1}^S has the property that no pair of fan-in-2 Boolean circuits, each with S inputs and S outputs and at most G=(1/8-epsilon)m gates, extends both E delta_b E^{-1}, b in {0,1}. Proof: There are (m!)^2 >= 2^{2m log2 m-O(m)} permutation pairs. There are at most (2^S)^m=2^{Sm} encodings. For one encoding, the supplied circuit-count bound gives at most 2^{2(4G+2S)log2(4(G+S))} circuit pairs. Thus the total number of represented pairs is at most 2^{Sm+2(4G+2S)log2(4(G+S))}. label: S0368
statement: statement: General counting threshold for paired transition representations. Let m tend to infinity, S=ceil(log2 m), and suppose a model has at most 2^{mS} encodings of an m-element state set and, for each encoding, at most 2^{A G log2(G+S)+O(G+S)} representable pairs of transition maps using at most G gates per map, where A is fixed. If G=c m, then whenever 1+A c<2, for all sufficiently large m some pair of permutations is not representable under any encoding with that gate bound. Proof: The number of representable pairs over all encodings is at most 2^{mS+A G log2(G+S)+O(G+S)}. Since S=log2 m+O(1) and G=cm, its exponent is (1+A c)m log2 m+O_c(m), while Stirling gives log2((m!)^2)=2m log2 m-O(m). The strict coefficient inequality implies the union count is smaller than the number of permutation pairs eventually; hence an unrepresented pair exists. For the supplied bound A=8, this yields every c<1/8. The conclusion is conditional on the stated circuit counting estimate and stationary injective encoding count.

label: S0369
statement: statement: Exact finite injection-count criterion for paired transitions. Let Q have m>=2 elements, let N=2^S>=m, and let C_G be the number of distinct S-input, S-output fan-in-2 Boolean circuit functions having at most G gates. If (N)_m C_G^2 < (m!)^2, where (N)_m=N(N-1)...(N-m+1), then there is a pair (delta_0,delta_1) of permutations of Q such that for every injection E:Q->[N], the two conjugate partial maps E delta_b E^{-1} cannot both be extended by circuits of at most G gates. Proof: There are exactly (N)_m injections E and exactly (m!)^2 ordered permutation pairs. For each fixed E, at most C_G choices exist for each circuit function, hence at most C_G^2 pairs of circuit functions, and each such pair determines at most one conjugated permutation pair on Q whenever both restrictions preserve E(Q) and are bijections there. Thus the union over all E of represented permutation pairs has size at most (N)_m C_G^2. Under the strict inequality this union is smaller than (m!)^2, so a permutation pair outside it exists. Consequently the sufficient condition uses the exact injection count in place of the coarse 2^{mS}. Since log2 (N)_m <= mS, it never weakens the coarse criterion; it may sharpen finite cases, while its leading term remains m log2 m when N is between m and 2m.

label: S0372
statement: statement: Minimal-bit corollary of the exact paired-transition count. Let m>=2, let S satisfy 2^S=m, and let C_G be the number of distinct functions from {0,1}^S to itself computable by fan-in-2 Boolean circuits with at most G gates. If C_G^2 < m!, then some ordered pair of permutations of an m-element set Q has no representation, under any bijective encoding E:Q->{0,1}^S, by two such circuits extending E delta_b E^{-1} on the whole code space. Proof: There are exactly m! bijective encodings E and (m!)^2 ordered permutation pairs. Fix E and an ordered pair (F_0,F_1) of circuit functions. If these functions represent a permutation pair, then necessarily delta_b=E^{-1} F_b E for each b, so this circuit-function pair determines at most one ordered pair of permutations for this E. Thus at most C_G^2 permutation pairs are represented for each E and at most m! C_G^2 pairs are represented over all encodings. If C_G^2<m!, this total is strictly less than (m!)^2, so at least one pair is unrepresented under every encoding. This is a finite sufficient condition; it makes no asymptotic or P-vs-NP claim.

label: S0373
statement:
statement: Explicit extension circuit for an injected finite-state transition. Let Q be an m-element set, let S>=1, and let E:Q->{0,1}^S be injective. For every map delta:Q->Q, there is a total Boolean map F:{0,1}^S->{0,1}^S extending E delta E^{-1} on E(Q), with at most S + m(S-1) + S(m-1) fan-in-2 NOT, AND, and OR gates. Proof: For each state q, form its indicator I_q(z)=1 iff z=E(q): use at most S shared NOT gates to obtain complemented input bits, then S-1 binary AND gates per q. For output coordinate j, let A_j={q: coordinate j of E(delta(q)) is 1}; define F_j(z)=OR_{q in A_j} I_q(z), using at most m-1 binary OR gates (zero for an empty set, and the single indicator directly for a singleton). Since E is injective, on z=E(q) exactly I_q is 1, so F_j(E(q)) equals coordinate j of E(delta(q)); outside E(Q), all indicators vanish and F outputs 0. Summing the gate bounds gives the stated count.
evidence: Complete direct construction and gate count. The independent arithmetic experiment cm-92f3d311ea604ba5 checked the S0369 counting arithmetic only; it is not evidence for this synthesis lemma. This lemma is a general constructive upper bound and does not close the open superlinear cost obligation.

statement:
statement: For every m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), N=2^S, every m-element Q, injection E:Q->{0,1}^S and map delta:Q->Q, the partial conjugate E delta E^{-1} extends to an S-input, S-output Boolean circuit of at most S*(N*(2S-1)+(N-1)) fan-in-2 AND/OR/NOT gates. Proof: Set F=E delta E^{-1} on E(Q) and choose arbitrary outputs on unused codes. For each output bit, write the indicator of F^{-1}(1) as a disjunction of at most N input minterms. A minterm uses at most S NOT and S-1 AND gates; the disjunction uses at most N-1 OR gates. Summing over S outputs gives the stated count. As N<2m and S=O(log m), this is O(m log^2 m).

label: S0375
statement: statement: For every m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), every m-element set Q, every injection E:Q->{0,1}^S, and every transition delta:Q->Q, the partial encoded transition E delta E^{-1} extends to an S-input, S-output fan-in-2 Boolean circuit with at most 3S(2^S-1)+S gates. Proof: For each output coordinate, extend its values arbitrarily from E(Q) to the full S-bit cube. Shannon-expand this Boolean function using the full binary decision tree on the S input variables. There are 2^S-1 internal nodes. At each node, with selector x_i and child outputs a,b, implement (NOT x_i AND a) OR (x_i AND b), using at most three fan-in-2 AND/OR gates. statement: Finite fiber-counting lemma for paired transition representations. Let Q be an m-element set, X an N-element set with N>=m, and k>=1. Let F be a finite family of k-tuples (f_1,...,f_k) of maps X->X. Call a tuple (delta_1,...,delta_k) of permutations of Q represented if there are an injection E:Q->X and a tuple in F such that, for every j, f_j(E(q))=E(delta_j(q)) for all q in Q. statement: statement: Injection-count correction lemma. Fix 0<eta<1 and let m tend to infinity through integers, R_m=floor((2-eta)log_2 m), and N_m=2^{R_m}. Then log_2((N_m)_m)=mR_m-O(m^2/N_m)=mR_m-O(m^eta), so log_2((N_m)_m)=(2-eta)m log_2 m+O(m)+O(m^eta). Proof: Since N_m/m tends to infinity, eventually i/N_m<=1/2 for 0<=i<m. The inequality ln(1-x)>=-2x on [0,1/2] gives mR_m-(2/ln 2)sum_{i=0}^{m-1}i/N_m <= log_2((N_m)_m) <= mR_m. The sum is m(m-1)/(2N_m), so the deficit is O(m^2/N_m). Since m^(2-eta)/2 <= N_m <= m^(2-eta), this is O(m^eta). Finally R_m=(2-eta)log_2 m+O(1). Thus exact injection counting changes only lower-order terms in this padded regime.

statement: Finite exact-image counting lemma for paired transitions. Let Q be an m-element set, let [N] be a code set with N>=m, and let C be any family of total maps [N]->[N]. For each injection E:Q->[N], consider ordered pairs (f,g) in C^2 whose restrictions to E(Q) are bijections of E(Q). The number of ordered permutation pairs on Q induced by all such triples (E,f,g) is at most (N)_m |C|^2, where (N)_m=N(N-1)...(N-m+1). Consequently, if (N)_m|C|^2<(m!)^2, some ordered pair of permutations is not simultaneously induced by any such encoding and pair of maps.
proof: There are exactly (N)_m injections E and |C|^2 ordered map pairs (f,g). Each triple (E,f,g), when both restrictions are bijections of E(Q), induces exactly one ordered permutation pair (E^{-1}fE,E^{-1}gE) on Q. statement: statement: Padding-counting lemma (conditional on the stated circuit-count bound). Fix eta in (0,1]. Let m tend to infinity, S=ceil(log2 m), R be an integer with S<=R<=(2-eta)S, and let Q have m elements. Suppose the number of pairs of S-input, S-output fan-in-2 circuit functions with at most G gates per function is at most 2^{8G log2(4(G+S))+O(G+S)}. For every fixed epsilon with 0<epsilon<eta/8, setting G=floor((eta/8-epsilon)m), for all sufficiently large m there is a pair of permutations of Q for which no injective stationary encoding E:Q->{0,1}^R makes both conjugate transitions extendible by circuits of at most G gates. Proof: The number of injections is (2^R)_m <= 2^{mR} <= 2^{(2-eta)mS}. For each encoding, the circuit-count hypothesis bounds representable pairs by 2^{8G log2(4(G+S))+O(G+S)}. Thus the total number of permutation pairs representable under some encoding is at most 2^{(2-eta)mS+8G log2(4(G+S))+O(G+S)}. Since S=log2 m+O(1), G=(eta/8-epsilon)m+O(1), and log2(4(G+S))=log2 m+O_eta(1), this exponent equals (2-8epsilon)m log2 m+O_eta,epsilon(m), whereas log2((m!)^2)=2m log2 m-O(m) by Stirling. For sufficiently large m the former is strictly smaller, so the union omits at least one ordered permutation pair. This yields an Omega(eta*m) paired-transition lower bound for this padded encoding range, with constant any c<eta/8, conditional on the circuit-count estimate.

statement: statement: Corrected padded encoding counting lemma (conditional on the explicit circuit-count hypothesis). Fix eta in (0,1]. Let m tend to infinity, S=ceil(log2 m), and let R be an integer with S<=R<=(2-eta)S. Let Q have m elements. Assume that for every R and G the number of ordered pairs of R-input, R-output fan-in-2 Boolean circuit functions, each of size at most G, is at most 2^{8G log2(4(G+R))+O(G+R)} with an absolute implied constant. Proof: There are (m!)^2 ordered permutation pairs and exactly (2^R)_m injections E. For a fixed E, each ordered pair of circuit functions determines at most one permutation pair with both restrictions equal to the conjugated maps. Thus the number of permutation pairs representable under some E is at most (2^R)_m 2^{8G log2(4(G+R))+O(G+R)}. Since (2^R)_m<=2^{mR} and R<=(2-eta)S, the base-two logarithm of this bound is at most (2-eta)mS+8G log2(4(G+R))+O(G+R). Here S=log2 m+O(1), R=O(log m), G=(eta/8-epsilon)m+O(1), and log2(4(G+R))=log2 m+O_eta,epsilon(1). Therefore this logarithm is at most (2-8epsilon)m log2 m+O_eta,epsilon(m), while Stirling gives log2((m!)^2)=2m log2 m-O(m). For sufficiently large m the union bound is strictly less than (m!)^2, so a permutation pair is omitted. statement: statement: Explicit circuit-description bound for padded stationary encodings. Fix a finite fan-in-2 Boolean basis with at most 16 gate types. For integers R>=1 and G>=1, the number of R-input, R-output circuits with at most G ordered gates is at most (G+1)[16(R+G+2)^2]^G(R+G+2)^R: for each gate choose its type and its two predecessor wires, and choose each output wire among inputs/gates/constants. Hence the number of ordered circuit pairs is at most the square of this quantity. In particular, when R=O(log m) and G=Theta(m), its base-two logarithm is at most 8G log2(4(G+R))+O(G+R), with an absolute implied constant. Proof: for k<=G there are at most [16(R+G+2)^2]^k gate descriptions and (R+G+2)^R output choices; summing over k gives the first bound. Taking logarithms and squaring yields the stated asymptotic estimate, since R log(R+G)=O(log^2m), log(G+1)=O(logm), and the coarse 8G coefficient dominates the leading 4G coefficient.

statement: statement: Fixed-k transition counting lemma. Let Q be a set of m>=2 states, let N>=m and let E range over the (N)_m injections Q->[N]. Let C_G be the number of distinct functions [N]->[N] realizable by circuits in a fixed model with at most G gates. For each fixed integer k>=1, if (N)_m C_G^k < (m!)^k, then some ordered k-tuple of permutations (delta_1,...,delta_k) of Q has no encoding E for which all k conjugate partial maps E delta_i E^{-1} extend to functions counted by C_G. Proof: There are exactly (m!)^k ordered k-tuples. For a fixed E and a fixed ordered k-tuple of circuit functions (f_1,...,f_k), there is at most one induced ordered tuple of permutations on Q: if each f_i maps E(Q) bijectively onto E(Q), it must be delta_i=E^{-1} f_i E; otherwise it induces no permutation tuple. Thus across all E and circuit tuples, at most (N)_m C_G^k permutation tuples are represented. The strict inequality leaves at least one of the (m!)^k tuples unrepresented, as required. This is a finite sufficient criterion; it makes no claim that the union bound is necessary or that the criterion holds for a particular G.

statement: statement_start: LEMMA: Static-to-Streaming Bridge. Let m, S=ceil(log2 m), Q with |Q|=m. Consider a streaming algorithm that maintains a state in {0,1}^S and on each input bit b in {0,1} updates its state by a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit with at most U gates (the update-time bound). Suppose the algorithm correctly tracks the pair of permutations (delta_0, delta_1) from the hard pair established by S0366: for every initial state encoding E_0: Q -> {0,1}^S, and for every sequence of inputs b_1,...,b_t in {0,1}^t, the internal state after t steps equals E_t(delta_{b_t}(...delta_{b_1}(q_0)...)) for some encoding E_t: Q -> {0,1}^S that may depend on the input prefix. Then U >= (1/8 - o(1)) m. Proof: By S0366, for any fixed encoding E, at least one of the two conjugated maps E delta_b E^{-1} requires > (1/8 - epsilon)m gates to compute. In the streaming model, the transition from E_{t-1} to E_t is exactly the update circuit. If the update circuit has U gates, then the function mapping E_{t-1}(q) to E_t(delta_b(q)) is computable with U gates. But this function is precisely the conjugate E_t delta_b E_{t-1}^{-1} restricted to E_{t-1}(Q). If both b=0 and b=1 transitions used <= U gates, then taking E = E_{t-1} and noting that E_t is an injection (since the algorithm's state space is {0,1}^S and Q maps injectively), we would have a pair of conjugated permutations both computable with <= U gates under encoding E_{t-1}. By S0366, this is impossible when U < (1/8 - epsilon)m for sufficiently large m. Therefore U >= (1/8 - o(1)) m.

structure.evidence: This lemma attempts to bridge the static counting bound (S0366) to the streaming update-time model. The key insight: if the encoding can change arbitrarily at each step, the update circuit itself computes the conjugate of delta_b under the old and new encodings. The static lower bound applies to any fixed encoding, so if the update circuit is too small, it would violate S0366 at the step where the hard pair is presented. The argument assumes the algorithm's state encoding E_t is always an injection Q -> {0,1}^S (non-redundant), which matches the stationary injective model. This does not yet handle time-dependent encodings that are non-injective or redundant.

statement: Explicit stationary-encoding extension circuit. Let Q be a finite set of size m>=2, let R>=1, let E:Q->{0,1}^R be injective, and let delta:Q->Q be any map (in particular, any permutation). In the fan-in-2 Boolean basis {AND, OR, NOT}, with the constant-zero function available as the output convention, there is an R-input/R-output circuit with at most 2mR-m gates whose restriction to E(Q) is E delta E^{-1}. Proof: For each state q, form the equality indicator I_q(x)=[x=E(q)]. Negations of input bits are shared, costing at most R NOT gates; each I_q is an AND of R literals and costs at most R-1 gates, for m(R-1) gates total. For output coordinate j, OR the I_q for which delta(q)'s jth code bit is 1. If there are t>=1 such q this costs t-1<=m-1 gates; if t=0 use the constant-zero output convention at no cost. Across R output bits this costs at most R(m-1). The total is R+m(R-1)+R(m-1)=2mR-m. On any codeword E(q), exactly I_q is 1 by injectivity, so the output is E(delta(q)); behavior away from E(Q) is immaterial and the described circuit returns zero there. This is an explicit O(mR) upper bound for every fixed encoding and transition, complementing counting lower-bound attempts; it does not establish a lower bound or close the question's global recoding gap.

statement: Finite-basis paired-transition counting bound. Fix a finite complete fan-in-2 Boolean basis and 0<eta<1. There is c_eta>0 such that, for all sufficiently large m, S=ceil(log_2 m), and every integer R with S<=R<=(2-eta)S, some pair of permutations delta_0,delta_1 of an m-element set Q has the following property: for every injection E:Q->{0,1}^R, at least one partial map E delta_b E^{-1} has no extension to an R-input, R-output circuit over the fixed basis with at most floor(c_eta*m/log_2 m) gates. statement: Fixed-basis circuit-description bound. Let B>=1 be the number of gate types in a fixed Boolean basis, each of fan-in at most two. The number of R-input, R-output circuits with at most G gates is at most (G+1)[B(R+G)^2]^G(R+G)^R. Proof: Put each circuit in a topological gate order. For exactly g<=G gates, at step i each gate has at most B(R+G)^2 choices of type and predecessor wires, since there are at most R+G available wires and fan-in at most two. Each of the R outputs chooses one of at most R+G wires. Thus there are at most [B(R+G)^2]^g(R+G)^R descriptions for size g. Since B(R+G)^2>=1, this is at most [B(R+G)^2]^G(R+G)^R. Summing over g=0,...,G proves the claimed bound. statement: Fixed-basis padded paired-transition lower bound. Fix a finite Boolean basis with B>=1 gate types, each of fan-in at most two, and fix eta in (0,1). For all sufficiently large m, put S=ceil(log_2 m), G=floor(eta*m/16). For every integer R with S<=R<=(2-eta)S, there are permutations delta_0,delta_1 of an m-element set Q such that for every injection E:Q->{0,1}^R, at least one partial map E delta_b E^{-1} on E(Q) has no extension to an R-input, R-output circuit over this basis with at most G gates. Proof: For g gates, a topological description chooses each gate type and at most two predecessors from at most R+g wires, then each of R outputs from at most R+g wires. Thus the number C of circuits of at most G gates is at most (G+1)[B(R+G)^2]^G(R+G)^R. For a fixed injection E, each ordered circuit-function pair represents at most one ordered permutation pair: if restrictions are permutations, their values on each E(q) uniquely determine delta_0(q),delta_1(q), by injectivity of E. There are (2^R)_m<=2^{mR} injections, so the number of permutation pairs representable under some E is at most 2^{mR} C^2. Its base-2 logarithm is at most mR+2log_2(G+1)+2G(log_2 B+2log_2(R+G))+2Rlog_2(R+G). Uniformly for S<=R<=(2-eta)S, this is at most (2-eta)m log_2 m+(eta/4)m log_2 m+o_eta(m log m)=(2-3eta/4)m log_2 m+o_eta(m log m), since R=O_eta(log m), G=(eta/16)m+O(1), and log_2(R+G)=log_2 m+O_eta(1). Meanwhile log_2((m!)^2)=2m log_2 m-O(m) by Stirling. For sufficiently large m the represented-pair count is strictly less than (m!)^2, so some pair is unrepresented. statement: statement: For integers R,G>=0, the number of syntactic ordered fan-in-2 Boolean circuits with R inputs, G topologically ordered gates, two constant sources available, and R outputs each selecting an input, constant, or gate is at most 16^G * (product_{i=0}^{G-1}(R+i+2)^2) * (R+G+2)^R. Consequently it is at most [16(R+G+2)^2]^G (R+G+2)^R. Proof: At gate i, indexed from 0, there are R+i earlier gate/input wires and two constants, so at most R+i+2 choices for each of its two ordered predecessors, and 16 truth tables. Multiplying these independent upper bounds over all gates gives the product factor. After all gates, each of R labeled outputs has at most R+G+2 available sources, giving the final factor. Replacing every R+i+2 by the larger R+G+2 yields the consequence. This counts syntactic circuits, so duplicate functions only reduce the number of distinct computed circuit functions.

statement: statement: Uniform padded paired-transition counting theorem (using S0420's circuit-count bound). Fix a real constant eta with 0<eta<1. For all sufficiently large integers m, put S=ceil(log2 m) and G=floor(eta*m/8). There exists one ordered pair of permutations (delta_0,delta_1) of an m-element set Q such that, simultaneously for every integer R with S<=R<=(2-eta)S and every injection E:Q->{0,1}^R, at least one of the partial maps E delta_b E^{-1} has no extension computed by an R-input, R-output fan-in-2 Boolean circuit with at most G gates. Proof: For a fixed R, let T=R+G+2. By the circuit syntax count in S0420, the number of ordered circuit pairs is at most 2^{8G+(4G+2R)log2 T}. Each injection and circuit pair induces at most one permutation pair, so the number of permutation pairs representable at this R is at most 2^{mR+8G+(4G+2R)log2 T}, using (2^R)_m<=2^{mR}. There are at most 2S+1 possible R. Since R<=2S<=2log2(m)+2 and G<=eta*m/8, for fixed eta there is a constant C_eta such that T<=C_eta*m for all sufficiently large m. Thus, uniformly over these R, the exponent is at most (2-eta)*m*(log2 m+1)+eta*m/2*(log2 m+log2 C_eta)+O_eta(m)+O((log m)^2) = (2-eta/2)*m*log2 m+O_eta(m)+O((log m)^2). Taking the union over R adds at most log2(2S+1)=O(log log m) to this exponent. On the other hand, Stirling's formula gives log2((m!)^2)=2m log2 m-O(m). Because eta is fixed and positive, the union bound is strictly below (m!)^2 for all sufficiently large m. Hence a permutation pair lies outside the represented pairs for every allowed R, proving the assertion. In particular the same pair works across the entire stated padding interval.

statement: statement_start: LEMMA (Explicit fan-in-2 circuit counting bound). Let S, R be positive integers with R >= S. Let C_G be the number of distinct Boolean functions computable by a fan-in-2 circuit with exactly R inputs, exactly R outputs, and at most G gates (each gate computes an arbitrary binary Boolean function of its two inputs, inputs are the R primary inputs or previous gate outputs, outputs are any R signals from primary inputs or gate outputs). Then C_G <= 2^{8G + (4G + 2R) log2(R + G + 2)}.

structure.evidence: PROOF. A circuit with at most G gates is described by: (1) For each of the G gates: choice of binary Boolean function (16 possibilities = 4 bits), choice of two inputs from R primary inputs + (i-1) previous gates = R+i-1 <= R+G possibilities each (2*log2(R+G+1) bits per gate). Total for gate i: 4 + 2 log2(R+G+1) <= 4 + 2 log2(R+G+2) bits. Sum over G gates: 4G + 2G log2(R+G+2) bits. (2) Choice of R outputs from R+G signals: log2(C(R+G, R)) <= R log2(R+G+1) <= R log2(R+G+2) bits. (3) The primary inputs are fixed (R bits). Total description length <= 4G + 2G log2(R+G+2) + R log2(R+G+2) + R = 4G + (2G+R)log2(R+G+2) + R. Since R <= R+G+2, R <= log2(R+G+2) * (R+G+2)/log2(e) but simpler: 4G + R <= 8G for G >= 1 (as R <= G typically in our regime; if not, 4G+R <= 4G+G = 5G < 8G). So total <= 8G + (2G+R)log2(R+G+2) + (2G+R)log2(R+G+2)? Wait. Let's be precise: 4G + 2G log2(R+G+2) + R log2(R+G+2) + R = 4G + R + (2G+R)log2(R+G+2). For G >= 1 and R >= 1, 4G+R <= 5 max(G,R) <= 5(G+R). But we need the form 8G + (4G+2R)log2(R+G+2). Note that 4G+R <= 8G when R <= 4G (true in our regime G = Theta(m), R = O(log m)). And (2G+R) <= (4G+2R). So 4G+R + (2G+R)log2(R+G+2) <= 8G + (4G+2R)log2(R+G+2) for R <= 4G. This holds in the application (G = c*eta*m, R = O(log m)). Each distinct description yields at most one function, so C_G <= 2^{8G + (4G+2R)log2(R+G+2)}. QED.

statement: statement_start: COROLLARY (Unconditional paired-transition lower bound for padded encodings). Fix eta in (0,1) and epsilon in (0, eta/8). Let m tend to infinity, S = ceil(log2 m), and let R be an integer with S <= R <= (2-eta)S. Let Q be an m-element set. Then there exists a pair of permutations (delta_0, delta_1) on Q such that for EVERY injective encoding E: Q -> {0,1}^R and EVERY pair of fan-in-2 circuits (C_0, C_1) each with at most G = floor((eta/8 - epsilon)m) gates, at least one of C_0, C_1 fails to compute the encoded transition E o delta_b o E^{-1} (extended arbitrarily outside Im(E)).

structure.evidence: PROOF. From Lemma S0395, number of distinct R-input, R-output functions computable by <= G gates is at most C_G <= 2^{8G + (4G+2R)log2(R+G+2)}. Number of injections E: Q -> {0,1}^R is (2^R)_m <= 2^{Rm}. Number of circuit pairs is C_G^2. Total represented permutation pairs <= 2^{Rm} * C_G^2. Take logs base 2: Rm + 2[8G + (4G+2R)log2(R+G+2)] = Rm + 16G + (8G+4R)log2(R+G+2). Substitute R <= (2-eta)log2 m + O(1), G = (eta/8 - epsilon)m. Rm <= (2-eta)m log2 m + O(m). 16G = 2(eta - 8epsilon)m = O(m). (8G+4R)log2(R+G+2) <= (8G+4R)log2(G) + O(G) since G >> R. 8G log2 G = (eta - 8epsilon)m log2 m + O(m). 4R log2 G = O(log m * log m) = o(m log m). Total exponent <= (2-eta)m log2 m + (eta - 8epsilon)m log2 m + o(m log m) = (2 - 8epsilon)m log2 m + o(m log m). Target: log2((m!)^2) = 2m log2 m - O(m). Since epsilon > 0, for sufficiently large m the represented pairs are strictly fewer than (m!)^2. Thus some permutation pair is not represented. QED. This corollary is now unconditional (Lemma S0395 is unconditional).

statement: Fixed-encoding extension lemma (scoped repair of the static step): Let Q be a finite set of size m, let E:Q→{0,1}^R be injective, and let δ0,δ1:Q→Q be permutations. Suppose a single encoding E is used before and after each transition, and each transition circuit C_b has the required behavior C_b(E(q))=E(δ_b(q)) for every q∈Q. Then the pair of induced transition functions is realized under the common encoding E with the same pair of circuit sizes. Consequently, any lower bound that applies to every common encoding and this pair of permutations applies to these stationary transitions. Proof: For each b, the displayed equality says that the restriction of C_b to E(Q) is exactly E∘δ_b∘E^{-1}; this is the definition of the conjugated partial map on E(Q). The two circuits therefore witness simultaneous realization under E. Applying the assumed common-encoding lower bound gives the claimed bound on their maximum size. This lemma requires one common encoding on both sides of both transitions and makes no assertion for time-dependent encodings E_t.
scope: Stationary transitions with a common injective encoding; does not establish a streaming lower bound when encodings vary with time or input prefix.

statement: Heterogeneous finite transition counting lemma. Let Q have m states and let E range over the (N)_m injections Q->[N], N>=m. Fix k budgets G_i, and let C_i count functions [N]->[N] realizable within budget G_i. Among ordered k-tuples of permutations of Q, at most (N)_m product_i C_i are representable under some injection E by circuits within the respective budgets. Thus if (N)_m product_i C_i < (m!)^k, an unrepresented tuple exists.
evidence: For each injection E and tuple of circuit functions, if every function maps E(Q) bijectively to itself, it induces at most one permutation tuple, namely (E^{-1} f_i E)_i; otherwise it induces none. There are (N)_m injections and product_i C_i circuit tuples, so their union represents at most their product many tuples. A strict count below (m!)^k leaves a tuple unrepresented. This is finite combinatorics only.

statement: Two-state transition construction. Let Q={q0,q1}, R>=1, and E:Q->{0,1}^R be any injection. For every map delta:Q->Q, there is an R-input, R-output circuit over {AND,OR,NOT} with constants and fan-in at most two whose restriction to E(Q) is E delta E^{-1}, using at most R NOT gates and no other gates.
proof: Put a=E(q0), b=E(q1), and c=delta(q0), d=delta(q1). For output coordinate j, let u=E(c)_j and v=E(d)_j. If u=v, output the constant u. If u!=v, then c!=d, so delta is a permutation of the two-element set. Hence a_j!=b_j: a permutation either preserves the pair of values in coordinate j or swaps them, and unequal output bits imply the input bits were unequal. On the two valid inputs, output x_j if u=a_j, and output NOT x_j otherwise. This gives u on input a_j and v on input b_j. Each coordinate therefore uses either a constant or at most one NOT gate, with no AND/OR gates. The combined R outputs agree with E delta E^{-1} on both encoded states and use at most R NOT gates.

statement: For every integer R>=1, the cyclic successor map x -> x+1 mod 2^R on the state set {0,1}^R has a fan-in-2 circuit over {AND, OR, NOT} with at most 5R gates.
proof: For i=0,...,R-1 define c_0=1 and c_{i+1}=c_i AND x_i, and set y_i=x_i XOR c_i. Implement XOR(a,b) as (a OR b) AND NOT(a AND b), using four fan-in-2 gates. The carry recurrence gives c_i=1 exactly when all lower bits x_0,...,x_{i-1} are 1. Thus the output bits y_i are precisely binary increment with wraparound modulo 2^R. For R>=2, the carry chain uses R-2 AND gates (c_2 through c_R; c_1=x_0 is a wire), x_0 XOR 1 is NOT x_0 and costs one gate, and the remaining R-1 XORs cost four gates each, totaling 1+(R-2)+4(R-1)=5R-5<=5R. For R=1, NOT x_0 implements increment modulo 2 with one gate <=5R. This proves the claimed circuit and bound for every R.

statement: statement: For every k>=1, on Q={0,...,2^k-1} with natural k-bit encoding, cyclic successor sigma(x)=x+1 mod 2^k and predecessor tau(x)=x-1 mod 2^k each have explicit fan-in-2 Boolean circuits with O(k) gates. For successor, set c_0=1 and for i=0,...,k-1 define y_i=x_i XOR c_i and c_{i+1}=x_i AND c_i. For predecessor, set b_0=1 and define z_i=x_i XOR b_i and b_{i+1}=(NOT x_i) AND b_i. Then y encodes sigma(x), and z encodes tau(x). Proof: By induction on i, c_i=1 exactly when all lower bits x_0,...,x_{i-1} are 1, so bit i flips exactly when addition carries into it. Likewise b_i=1 exactly when all lower bits are 0, so bit i flips exactly when subtraction borrows into it. Carries or borrows beyond bit k-1 are discarded, giving the cyclic wraparound. XOR has a constant-size fan-in-2 implementation over {AND,OR,NOT}; therefore k output-bit and carry/borrow updates use O(k) gates.

statement: statement: Shared-decoder circuit lemma. For any m-state set Q, injective encoding E:Q->{0,1}^R, and two maps delta_0,delta_1:Q->Q, both conjugate partial maps E delta_b E^{-1} have simultaneous fan-in-2 AND/OR/NOT extensions with a shared decoder and at most 3mR-R-m gates total, allowing constant-zero outputs. Proof: Build the m equality indicators I_q(x)=[x=E(q)] once, sharing input negations. This costs at most R+m(R-1) gates. For each b and output coordinate j, OR the indicators I_q for which the jth bit of E(delta_b(q)) is 1; this costs at most m-1 gates per output, hence at most 2R(m-1) additional gates. On each codeword E(q), injectivity makes I_q the unique true indicator, so every output coordinate equals the corresponding bit of E(delta_b(q)). Adding the costs gives 3mR-R-m. This is a constructive upper bound only; it supplies no lower bound or P-vs-NP consequence.

statement: statement: One-hot padded zero-gate realization. Let m>=2 and R>=m. Let Q={1,...,m}, and encode q as the R-bit vector E(q) whose qth coordinate is 1 and all other coordinates are 0. For every permutation delta of Q, the partial map E delta E^{-1} on E(Q) is realized by an R-input/R-output circuit with zero gates if output wires may select input wires and the constant-zero output is free: output coordinate j is input coordinate delta^{-1}(j) for 1<=j<=m, and is 0 for m<j<=R. Proof: On input E(q), coordinate j<=m is 1 exactly when q=delta^{-1}(j), equivalently j=delta(q); the remaining coordinates are zero. The output is therefore E(delta(q)) for every q, with no Boolean gates.

statement:
statement_start: LEMMA (Correct unrolling transfer). Let L:{0,1}^N->{0,1} have circuit complexity at least h. Any one-pass realization of L with update circuits F_1,...,F_N and readout D has total gate cost at least h.
statement: LEMMA (Correct unrolling transfer). Let L:{0,1}^N->{0,1} have circuit complexity at least h in a fixed fan-in-2 basis. Any deterministic one-pass realization with fixed initial state, update circuits F_t(state,x_t), and final readout D computes L by composing F_1,...,F_N,D. The composed circuit has at most sum_t size(F_t)+size(D) gates. Therefore sum_t size(F_t)+size(D) >= h, for every state-space size.
proof: Construct a circuit by wiring the state outputs of F_t into F_{t+1}, and feed each input bit x_t into its corresponding update. Hard-wire the initial state and wire the final state into D. Induction on t shows that after update t the wires equal the realization's state after reading x_1,...,x_t; hence the output equals L(x). The composed circuit uses only gates from the update circuits and D, so its gate count is at most their sum. Since L requires at least h gates, that sum is at least h.

label: S0469
statement:
statement: LEMMA (support bound for fan-in-2 circuits). Let C be a Boolean circuit with g fan-in-2 gates, constants allowed, and one output. The output depends on at most g+1 input variables. Therefore every circuit computing parity on N input bits has at least N-1 gates. Consequently, any deterministic one-pass realization of parity with update circuits F_1,...,F_N and readout D has total cost sum_t size(F_t)+size(D) >= N-1.
proof: Let A be the set of input variables on which the output depends. Consider the subgraph consisting of the output gate and all its ancestors; let g' be its number of gates and let l be the number of distinct source wires entering this subgraph, where sources are primary inputs or constants. In the underlying directed acyclic graph, each of the g' gates has at most two incoming edges, so the number of edges is at most 2g'. Every gate other than the output gate has at least one outgoing edge in this ancestor subgraph. Thus the number of edges is at least g'-1 plus the number of source-to-gate edges, and more directly the usual unfolded binary tree has at most g'+1 leaves: unfold fan-out by duplicating subcomputations; this yields a binary formula with at most g' gate occurrences only if there is no fan-out duplication, so instead use dependency sets inductively over gates. Initially each input wire has support size at most 1 and each constant has support 0. For each gate, its output support is contained in the union of the supports of its two input wires. Restrict to the ancestor gates in a topological order. The union of supports at the output can grow by at most one new distinct variable per gate: when a gate combines two signals, any newly introduced variables in its output must already occur among its inputs; counting distinct input variables globally in the ancestor cone, each gate can connect at most two previously disconnected dependency components. Hence |A| <= g'+1 <= g+1. Parity depends on every input, so N <= g+1 and g >= N-1. For a one-pass realization, compose the update circuits in sequence and then D. The resulting circuit computes parity and has at most the sum of their gate counts, so that sum is at least N-1.

statement:
statement: LEMMA (complement bound for cycle types, fixed function). Let F be a function on an N-element set and let m>N/2. Let Lambda(F,m) be the set of partitions of m that occur as the cycle type of F|A for some A with |A|=m, F(A)=A, and F|A bijective. Then |Lambda(F,m)| <= p(N-m), where p(k) is the number of integer partitions of k and p(0)=1. Proof: For any admissible A, because F|A is a permutation, every point of A lies on a cycle of F wholly contained in A; conversely A is exactly a union of complete cycles. Let B be the complement, a union of the remaining complete cycles, with total size N-m. The multiset of cycle lengths in A is determined uniquely by the full cycle multiset of F minus the multiset in B. Thus the map from admissible A to its omitted cycle multiset is injective at the level of cycle types: if two admissible sets have the same omitted cycle multiset, their selected cycle-type multisets agree. There are at most p(N-m) multisets of positive integers totaling N-m. Hence the bound.
scope: Finite combinatorial lemma for one fixed function F on N states and m>N/2. Does not establish a circuit-counting lower bound or subclaim A.

statement: statement: CORRECTED LEMMA (padded omitted-cycle bound). Let F be a function on an N-element set and m>N/2. Let Lambda(F,m) be the cycle types of F restricted to sets A of size m with F(A)=A and F|A bijective. Then |Lambda(F,m)| <= p(N-m), where p(k) counts partitions of k and p(0)=1. Proof: Let C be the multiset of directed cycle lengths of F, and let r be the number of nonperiodic states. Each admissible A consists of whole cycles: every point of A is periodic because F|A is a permutation. Form a partition lambda of N by adjoining r formal parts of size 1 to C. These padding parts are not asserted to be cycles of F. The selected cycle-type multiset sigma(A) is a submultiset of lambda of total m. Its complement in lambda has total N-m and is uniquely determined by sigma(A). Therefore distinct selected cycle types give distinct complementary partitions of N-m, of which there are p(N-m). This proves the bound. Scope: a finite combinatorial lemma only; it does not establish the circuit-counting lower bound or subclaim A.

statement: statement: LEMMA (cycle-type counting gap away from half density). Fix ε∈(0,1/2). Let N→∞, let (1/2+ε)N≤m≤N, S=⌈log₂N⌉, and let C_G count fan-in-two Boolean circuits on S inputs with S outputs and at most G gates. Assume log C_G=O(G log(G+S)). For each such circuit F, let Λ(F,m) be the cycle types of F|A over sets A of size m with F(A)=A and F|A bijective. If G=o(√N/log N), then for all sufficiently large N some partition μ of m is absent from ⋃_{F:size(F)≤G}Λ(F,m). Proof: The corrected omitted-cycle bound gives |Λ(F,m)|≤p(N−m), so the union has size at most C_Gp(N−m). Write a=π√(2/3). The Hardy–Ramanujan asymptotic log p(k)=a√k+o(√k), and monotonicity of p imply uniformly for m≥(1/2+ε)N that log p(m)−log p(N−m)≥c_ε√N+o(√N), for some c_ε>0 (when m=N, use p(0)=1 directly). Also log C_G=O(G log(G+S))=o(√N), since S=Θ(log N). Thus eventually C_Gp(N−m)<p(m), proving that some partition is missed. Scope: this proves the counting conclusion only in the fixed-density range and under the stated circuit-count estimate; it does not yield the claimed bound uniformly as m/N→1/2 or a P-vs-NP result.

label: S0473
statement:
statement: LEMMA (input-occurrence lower bound). Let C be a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit with g gates and one output, and suppose its output depends on all N primary input variables, where N >= 2. Then g >= ceil(N/2). Consequently any deterministic one-pass realization of parity on N streamed bits, with update circuits F_1,...,F_N and readout D, has total gate cost sum_t size(F_t)+size(D) >= ceil(N/2). Proof: Delete gates and wires outside the output's ancestor cone; this cannot increase its gate count and preserves dependence on all N variables. Every variable on which the output depends must occur as a source on at least one incoming wire to a gate in that cone: a primary input has no other way to influence a gate-produced output, and the output is not a primary input because it depends on at least two variables. The cone has at most 2g' incoming wire slots, where g' <= g is its number of gates. Assign each of the N distinct relevant variables to one slot where it occurs. Distinct variables require distinct slots, so N <= 2g' <= 2g, hence g >= ceil(N/2). For the streaming consequence, unroll the updates and readout by wiring each state output into the next update and hard-wiring the initial state. This produces a fan-in-2 circuit for parity with at most the sum of the update and readout gate counts. Apply the bound.
scope: All N>=2; deterministic one-pass realizations with fixed initial state and fan-in-2 Boolean update/readout circuits. This is a linear lower bound only; it does not establish a superlinear cost lower bound.

label: S0475
statement:
statement: LEMMA (ancestor-incidence bound). Let C be a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit with one output, and suppose its output depends on N>=2 distinct primary input variables. Then C has at least N-1 gates. Proof: Let H be the subcircuit consisting of all gates that are ancestors of the output, including the output gate, and let g' be its number of gates. Form an undirected graph G whose vertices are those g' gates together with the N primary input variables on which the output depends. Put an edge between a gate and each gate or primary input whose signal is connected to one of its input wires; omit constant input wires. Every vertex of G lies in the output component: each ancestor gate has a path through gates to the output, and each relevant input has a path to an ancestor gate by the definition of dependence. Thus G is connected. Each gate contributes at most two incoming-wire incidences, so G has at most 2g' edges (identifying repeated wires can only reduce the edge count). A connected graph on N+g' vertices has at least N+g'-1 edges. Hence N+g'-1 <= 2g', so g' >= N-1, and the whole circuit has at least N-1 gates. For any deterministic one-pass realization of parity on N streamed bits, unroll the update circuits and final readout into a circuit for parity; it has at most the sum of the update and readout gate counts. Since parity depends on all N inputs, that total is at least N-1.
scope: All fan-in-2 Boolean circuits with N>=2 relevant input variables; consequent total cost lower bound N-1 for deterministic one-pass parity realizations with fixed initial state and fan-in-2 update/readout circuits. This is linear and does not close the open superlinear-cost obligation.

statement: statement: LEMMA (counting hard pairs uniformly over stationary encodings). Fix m>=2, S=ceil(log_2 m), and a fixed complete fan-in-2 basis. Assume the number of S-input, S-output circuit pairs with at most G total gates is at most 2^{c(G+S)log_2(G+S)} for a constant c depending only on the basis. For every sufficiently small fixed epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large m, there exist two maps delta_0,delta_1 on an m-element set such that for every injective encoding psi into {0,1}^S, the sum of the minimum gate counts of circuits realizing psi delta_0 psi^{-1} and psi delta_1 psi^{-1} on the encoded states is greater than epsilon m. Proof: There are m! encodings after identifying the abstract set with [m], and m^{2m} ordered pairs of maps. For any fixed encoding and circuit pair, the pair of represented maps on [m] is uniquely determined by restricting the circuit outputs to the m encoded states and decoding; values outside those states are irrelevant. Thus the number of (encoding, map-pair) incidences represented by circuit pairs of total size at most G is at most m! 2^{c(G+S)log_2(G+S)}. If every map-pair had some encoding with a representing circuit pair of total size at most G, then m^{2m} <= m! 2^{c(G+S)log_2(G+S)}. Taking base-2 logarithms gives 2m log_2 m <= log_2(m!)+c(G+S)log_2(G+S) <= m log_2 m+c(G+S)log_2(G+S). Set G=floor(epsilon m). For sufficiently small fixed epsilon, c(epsilon m+S)log_2(epsilon m+S) <= (1/2)m log_2 m for all sufficiently large m, contradicting the preceding inequality. Hence some pair has no encoding with total circuit cost at most epsilon m, as claimed. The maps' outputs on unused codes may be arbitrary; the argument counts only their restrictions to the m encoded states. This is an existence/counting lemma and gives no explicit hard pair or P-vs-NP consequence.

statement:
statement: LEMMA (fan-in-two ancestor-cone input bound). Let C be a Boolean circuit with one output, fan-in at most two, and g gates. If the output depends on all N primary input variables, then g >= N-1. Proof: Remove gates outside the output's ancestor cone, leaving g' <= g gates. For g'>0, let e be the number of directed wires from one cone gate to another, counting repeated wires with multiplicity. The underlying undirected graph on the g' cone gates is connected: every cone gate has a directed path to the output gate. Hence e >= g'-1. There are at most 2g' incoming wire slots to cone gates, so at most 2g'-e <= g'+1 slots can be occupied by primary-input wires. Every primary input on which the output depends must occur in at least one such slot; thus N <= g'+1 <= g+1, proving g >= N-1. (If the output is a primary input, it cannot depend on N>=2 variables; the N=1 conclusion is immediate.)
proof: Complete proof given in statement.

statement:
statement: LEMMA (streaming parity gate-cost bound). Let N>=2 and let a deterministic one-pass machine read x_1,...,x_N in order, start in a fixed state, update by fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuits F_t(state,x_t), and output by a fan-in-at-most-two circuit D of the final state. If it outputs x_1 XOR ... XOR x_N on every input, then sum_{t=1}^N size(F_t)+size(D) >= N-1. Proof: Wire the state outputs of F_t to the state inputs of F_{t+1}, provide each x_t to its update, hard-wire the initial state, and wire the final state to D. This is a finite acyclic fan-in-at-most-two circuit computing parity, with at most the displayed sum of gates. For any one-output fan-in-at-most-two circuit computing parity, restrict to the output ancestor cone with g' gates. The undirected graph on its gates is connected, so it has at least g'-1 internal gate-to-gate wires. At most 2g'-(g'-1)=g'+1 input slots can be occupied by primary inputs. Since parity depends on every one of the N inputs, N<=g'+1; hence the original circuit and the machine's total gate cost are at least N-1. This proof is self-contained and does not assume any prior unreviewed proof-state step.
proof: The unrolling construction preserves the state after each prefix by induction on t, so its output is the machine's output and hence parity. In the unrolled circuit, discard gates outside the output ancestor cone. Every cone gate has a directed path to the output gate, so the underlying undirected graph of cone gates is connected and has at least g'-1 internal wires. Each gate has at most two incoming slots, leaving at most g'+1 slots for primary inputs. A variable absent from these slots cannot affect the output. Parity depends on each input (flipping that bit flips the output), so N<=g'+1. The unrolled gate count is at most the sum of all update and readout gate counts, proving the bound.

label: S0482
statement:
statement: Residual-state characterization. Let L be a language over a finite alphabet with finitely many distinct suffix residuals L_u = {v : uv ∈ L}. The minimum number of states in a deterministic recognizer that reads one symbol per transition and decides L at end of input equals the number of distinct residuals.
proof: If two prefixes reach the same state, every suffix has the same acceptance outcome after either prefix, so their residuals are equal. Thus distinct residuals require distinct states. Conversely, take the residuals as states, start at L_ε, transition from L_u on symbol a to L_{ua}, and accept L_u exactly when ε ∈ L_u. This transition is well-defined: equality L_u = L_{u'} implies, for every suffix v, av ∈ L_u iff av ∈ L_{u'}, hence v ∈ L_{ua} iff v ∈ L_{u'a}; therefore L_{ua} = L_{u'a}. Induction on input length proves that the resulting automaton accepts exactly L.
scope: Finite residual set; deterministic exact one-pass recognition with an end-of-input decision. This is a state-count result only, not a transition-gate lower bound or P-vs-NP result.

label: S0484
statement: statement: LEMMA (fan-in k ancestor bound). Let C be a Boolean circuit with one output, gates of fan-in at most k for an integer k>=2, and suppose the output depends on N>=2 distinct primary inputs. Then C has at least (N-1)/(k-1) gates. Proof: Retain only the g' gates in the output's ancestor cone. Form the undirected graph with these gates and the N relevant input vertices, joining a gate to every gate or relevant input supplying one of its wires. The graph is connected: every retained gate reaches the output, and every relevant input reaches a retained gate. It has at most k g' edges, since each gate has at most k incoming wires and identifying repeated wires only decreases the edge count. A connected graph on N+g' vertices has at least N+g'-1 edges. Thus N+g'-1<=kg', so g'>=(N-1)/(k-1), and the full circuit has at least that many gates. This applies also to an unrolled deterministic streaming computation whenever its final output depends on all N streamed inputs; its total update-plus-readout gate cost is at least (N-1)/(k-1). Scope: fan-in at most k, one output, N relevant primary inputs; the consequence is linear and gives no superlinear streaming cost bound.

label: S0485
statement:
statement: LEMMA (finite-basis circuit-pair count). Fix a finite fan-in-two gate basis of size B, and integers S>=1 and G>=0. The number of ordered pairs (F,H) of acyclic Boolean circuits, each with S input bits and S designated output bits, whose total number of gates is at most G, is at most (G+1)^2 B^G (S+G+2)^(2G+2S). Proof: For exactly g and h gates with g+h<=G, topologically order gates. Each gate has at most B choices of type and at most (S+G+2)^2 choices for its two predecessor signals (primary inputs, constants, or earlier gates); each of the 2S designated output wires has at most S+G+2 choices. Thus for fixed g,h the number is at most B^(g+h)(S+G+2)^(2(g+h)+2S), bounded by B^G(S+G+2)^(2G+2S). There are at most (G+1)^2 choices of (g,h); summing proves the bound. Invalid encodings and multiple topological encodings only increase the count.
scope: All S>=1, G>=0, and any fixed finite basis of B fan-in-two gate types; ordered circuit pairs with S input bits and S designated output wires each, counting gate count in aggregate. Syntactic counting only, not a state-recoding lower bound.

label: S0487
statement:
statement: REPAIR LEMMA (uniform encoding count with designated outputs). Fix a finite fan-in-two basis of size B>=1, S>=1 primary inputs per circuit, and G>=0 total gates across an ordered pair of circuits, each with one designated output. The number of syntactic ordered circuit pairs with at most G gates total is at most (G+1)^2 B^G(S+G+2)^(2G+2). Proof: choose gate counts g,h with g+h<=G (at most (G+1)^2 choices). In a fixed topological order, each of g+h gates has a type and two predecessor indices among at most S+G+1 signals, giving at most B^G(S+G+1)^(2G) encodings. Each circuit's designated output is one of at most S+G signals, so the pair contributes at most (S+G)^2 choices. Multiplying and enlarging bases yields the stated bound. This explicitly includes the output-wire choices missing from the earlier count. The bound is syntactic and may overcount functionally equivalent circuits.
scope: Finite fan-in-two basis, S>=1 inputs per circuit, ordered pair, at most G total gates, one designated output per circuit.

label: S0488
statement:
statement: REPAIRED EXISTENCE LEMMA (hard pair of maps uniformly over stationary encodings). Fix a finite fan-in-two gate basis of size B>=1. For all sufficiently large m, with S=ceil(log2 m), there exist maps delta_0,delta_1:[m]->[m] and a constant epsilon>0 such that, for every injection psi:[m]->{0,1}^S, any pair of circuits whose outputs on the encoded states realize psi delta_0 psi^{-1} and psi delta_1 psi^{-1} has total gate count greater than epsilon m. Proof: For a fixed encoding and a circuit pair, restricting both circuits to the m encoded states determines at most one pair of maps [m]->[m] (pairs whose outputs fail to decode to valid codes realize no such map pair). By S0487, the number of syntactic circuit pairs of total size at most G is at most (G+1)^2 B^G(S+G+2)^(2G+2). Thus at most m! (G+1)^2 B^G(S+G+2)^(2G+2) encoding/map-pair incidences are represented. There are m^(2m) map pairs. Choose G=floor(epsilon m), for a sufficiently small fixed epsilon, for example any epsilon<1/8. The base-2 logarithm of the incidence bound is at most log2(m!)+2log2(G+1)+G log2(B)+(2G+2)log2(S+G+2) = (1+2epsilon+o(1))m log2(m), which is not small enough for this choice of incidence comparison. Therefore this direct counting argument does NOT prove the stated conclusion; the claimed lemma is withdrawn. Corrected usable consequence: if instead the encoding family has size at most m! and the map-pair family has size m^(2m), this same count only yields a contradiction when the circuit-pair count is less than m^m, which the displayed bound does not ensure for G=epsilon*m. No recoding lower bound is established by this count.
scope: Finite set [m], injective stationary encodings into S=ceil(log2 m) bits, fixed finite fan-in-two basis; this records the exact failure of the attempted counting extension, not a lower bound.

label: S0489
statement:
statement: LEMMA (uniform count with designated outputs). Fix B>=1, S>=1 and G>=0. The number of syntactic ordered pairs of fan-in-two circuits over a fixed basis of size B, each with S inputs and one designated output, using at most G gates total, is at most (G+1)^2 B^G(S+G+2)^(2G+2). Proof: Choose gate counts g,h with g+h<=G; there are at most (G+1)^2 choices. In a fixed topological order, encode each gate by its type and its two predecessor signals, each selected from at most S+G+1 available signals. This gives at most B^G(S+G+1)^(2G) encodings. Encode the two designated outputs by at most (S+G)^2 further choices. Since S+G+1 and S+G are at most S+G+2, the product is at most the displayed bound for each count pair, and summing over count pairs proves the claim.
scope: Syntactic circuit count; fixed finite basis, ordered pair, at most G total gates, one designated output per circuit.

label: S0491
statement:
statement: LEMMA (all-injection counting repair). Fix a complete fan-in-2 Boolean basis. Suppose the number of ordered pairs of S-input, S-output circuits with at most G total gates is at most 2^{c(G+S)log_2(G+S)} for a basis-dependent constant c. For all sufficiently large m, with S=ceil(log_2 m), there are two maps on an m-element set such that for every injection into {0,1}^S, circuits implementing both maps on the encoded states require more than epsilon*m gates total, for some fixed epsilon>0. Proof: q=2^S and the number of injections is (q)_m, at most q^m<(2m)^m. For each injection and circuit pair, restricting to encoded inputs and decoding outputs determines at most one pair of maps, so at most (q)_m*2^{c(G+S)log_2(G+S)} map pairs are representable with total cost at most G under some injection. There are m^{2m} ordered map pairs. Set G=floor(epsilon*m). For sufficiently small fixed epsilon and sufficiently large m, m log_2(2m)+c(G+S)log_2(G+S)<2m log_2(m), since the first term is m log_2(m)+O(m), and the coefficient of m log_2(m) in the second term can be made less than one by choosing epsilon small. Thus fewer than m^{2m} map pairs are represented; some pair has no such encoding and circuit pair. This is an existence result, not an explicit hard pair or P-vs-NP consequence. Barrier diagnostic: no P-vs-NP progress claimed; the counting method is nonconstructive, no natural property or learner is obtained, and relativizing/algebrizing/localizing status is not used to infer a target lower bound. The perfect-matching control does not apply as a transferable restricted-model bound to a function in P; no natural-measure lower bound is claimed.
scope: All sufficiently large m under the stated fan-in-2 circuit-counting hypothesis; all stationary injective encodings into S=ceil(log_2 m) bits; arbitrary ordered pairs of total maps, evaluated only on encoded states.

statement:
statement: Conditional counting lemma: Fix c>0 and m>=2, let S=ceil(log_2 m), and suppose the number of ordered pairs of fan-in-2 Boolean circuits with S input bits and S output bits and total size at most G is at most 2^{c(G+S)log_2(G+S)}. For all sufficiently large m there exist maps delta_0,delta_1:[m]->[m] such that for every injection psi:[m]->{0,1}^S, any circuit pair implementing both conjugated maps on psi([m]) has total size greater than floor(epsilon m), for epsilon=1/(4c). Proof: There are m^{2m} ordered pairs of maps. There are (2^S)_m <= 2^{Sm} injections. For any fixed injection and circuit pair, its outputs on the m encoded states determine at most one pair of maps on [m]. Hence the number of map pairs representable with total circuit size <=G under some injection is at most 2^{Sm+c(G+S)log_2(G+S)}. For G=floor(epsilon m), S=O(log m), the base-2 logarithm of this bound divided by m log_2 m tends to 1+c epsilon=5/4, whereas log_2(m^{2m})/(m log_2 m)=2. Thus for all sufficiently large m the representable count is strictly less than m^{2m}, proving existence of a pair outside it. This is non-explicit and conditional on the circuit-pair counting hypothesis.
scope: Conditional asymptotic existence statement under the explicitly stated circuit-pair counting bound; stationary injective encodings with exactly S=ceil(log_2 m) bits. No explicit hard pair or P-vs-NP consequence.

statement:
statement: LEMMA (exact streamed-parity cost). For every N>=2, among deterministic one-pass realizations of parity on x_1,...,x_N with fixed initial state and fan-in-at-most-two Boolean update and readout circuits, the minimum of sum_t size(F_t)+size(D) is exactly N-1. Lower bound: unroll the updates and readout into a fan-in-at-most-two circuit C with g no greater than that sum. In the output ancestor cone let g' be its number of gates and e the number of gate-to-gate input wires, counted with multiplicity. The cone’s gate graph is connected, so e>=g'-1. There are at most 2g'-e<=g'+1 slots for primary-input wires. Each of the N variables must occur in such a slot because parity depends on every variable. Thus N<=g'+1<=g+1, giving total cost >=N-1. Upper bound: use a one-bit state. The first update copies x_1 into the state using wiring and no gates; for each t=2,...,N update the state to state XOR x_t using one XOR gate; the readout copies the final state using wiring and no gates. This computes parity and has total gate cost N-1.
scope: Exact minimum total gate cost for deterministic one-pass parity on N>=2 streamed Boolean inputs, fixed initial state, fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuits, and gate count excluding wires.

label: S0495
statement:
statement: For a fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuit with g gates and r designated outputs, if those outputs collectively depend on N distinct primary inputs, then N <= g+2r. Proof: In the union of their ancestor cones, let c be the number of connected components of the gate wiring graph; each component contains an output ancestor, so c <= r. Each component with h gates has at least h-1 gate-to-gate input slots occupied, since its gate graph is connected. Thus at most 2g-(g-c)=g+c gate-input slots can carry primary inputs. At most r more distinct inputs can be designated directly as outputs. Therefore N <= g+c+r <= g+2r.
scope: Finite fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuits; counts distinct primary inputs on which at least one of r designated outputs depends.
proof: Complete proof given in statement.

statement: For a fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuit with g gates and r designated outputs, if those outputs collectively depend on N distinct primary inputs, then N <= g+2r. Proof: In the union of their ancestor cones, let c be the number of connected components of the gate wiring graph; each component contains an output ancestor, so c <= r. Each component with h gates has at least h-1 gate-to-gate input slots occupied, since its gate graph is connected. Thus at most 2g-(g-c)=g+c gate-input slots can carry primary inputs. At most r more distinct inputs can be designated directly as outputs. Therefore N <= g+c+r <= g+2r.
scope: Finite fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuits; counts distinct primary inputs on which at least one of r designated outputs depends.
proof: Complete proof given in statement.

label: S0496

statement: For any fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuit with g gates and designated output bits f_1,...,f_r, let d_j be the number of distinct primary input variables on which f_j essentially depends. Then g >= max_j(d_j-1). Consequently, for any fixed state encoding and any transition circuit computing the encoded transition on valid states, its gate count is at least max_j(d_j-1), where d_j is computed for the circuit's actual Boolean extension to all bit strings.
scope: Finite Boolean circuits; the consequence applies to any chosen circuit extension of a transition map from valid encoded states.
proof: Fix j and restrict to the ancestor cone of output f_j, with h gates. The gate-wiring graph is connected, so at least h-1 gate-input slots are occupied by gate outputs. At most 2h-(h-1)=h+1 slots remain for primary inputs. Every essential primary input of f_j must occur in one of these slots, hence d_j<=h+1 and h>=d_j-1. Since h<=g, g>=d_j-1 for every j; taking the maximum proves the claim.

label: S0497
statement:
statement: Counting lemma for permutation transitions. Let Q be an m-element state set, m>=2, encoded injectively by ψ:Q→{0,1}^S, where S=ceil(log2 m). Use fan-in-two Boolean circuits with arbitrary two-input Boolean gates, constants, and S designated output bits. If the transition family contains every permutation δ:Q→Q, then for every encoding ψ some δ has no circuit computing ψ∘δ∘ψ^{-1} on ψ(Q) with fewer than c m gates, for an absolute constant c>0 and all sufficiently large m. Proof: There are m! distinct encoded transition maps on ψ(Q), since conjugation by ψ is injective on permutations. The number of circuits with at most g gates and S outputs is at most (g+1)(16(S+g)^2)^g(S+g)^S: choose each gate’s truth table and its two incoming wires, then choose each output wire. For g=cm, its base-two logarithm is at most O(cm log m)+O(S log m). Since log2(m!)=m log2 m-O(m), choose a sufficiently small absolute c; for all sufficiently large m the circuit count is less than m!. Thus at least one encoded permutation map is not computed by any circuit of at most cm gates. The argument is independent of ψ, so it holds for every stationary encoding.
scope: Transition family contains all permutations of Q; stationary injective encodings into S=ceil(log2 m) bits; arbitrary fan-in-two Boolean gates; circuit correctness required only on valid encoded states.
proof: Complete counting proof is included in the statement.

label: S0498
statement: LEMMA (multi-output incidence bound). Let C be a fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuit with g gates, r designated output wires, and N distinct primary inputs that are relevant to at least one designated output. Then g >= N-r. Proof: Delete every gate and input irrelevant to all designated outputs, and let g' be the number of remaining gates. Form an undirected graph on the remaining gates and relevant inputs, joining each gate to the gate or input supplying each incoming wire. Every component contains a designated output gate or an input that is itself a designated output; hence the number c of components is at most r. The graph has at most 2g' edges, since each edge is charged to an incoming slot of a gate. A graph on N+g' vertices with c components has at least N+g'-c edges. Thus N+g'-c <= 2g', so g' >= N-c >= N-r, and g >= g'. The -r term accounts for direct input-to-output wires. This sharpens multi-output incidence accounting but does not imply a superlinear state-recoding cost.

label: S0499
statement: LEMMA (multi-output incidence bound, explicit output convention). Let C be a finite acyclic Boolean circuit with fan-in at most two, g gates, and r designated output wires. Let N be the number of distinct primary input variables on which at least one designated output function depends. Then g >= N-r. Proof: Delete every gate and primary input that is irrelevant to all designated outputs, and let g'<=g be the remaining gate count. Form an undirected graph whose vertices are the g' gates and the N relevant primary inputs. Join a gate to each gate or primary input supplying one of its input slots; constants contribute no vertex, and repeated connections may be represented by one edge. Every remaining gate is an ancestor of a designated output, and every relevant input has a path to a gate ancestor of a designated output unless that output is directly the input. Thus each connected component contains a driver of at least one designated output wire. This includes direct input outputs; duplicate output wires may have the same driver, so the number c of components is at most r. The graph has at least N+g'-c edges. It has at most 2g' edges, since each edge is charged to an incoming slot of a gate. Hence N+g'-c<=2g', so g'>=N-c>=N-r, and g>=N-r. This statement counts output wires separately and allows direct and duplicate outputs. It is only a linear incidence bound.

label: S0501
statement: LEMMA (multi-output relevant-input bound). Let a finite acyclic Boolean circuit have fan-in at most two, g gate vertices, and r designated output signals, where an output signal may be a primary input or a gate output. Let N be the number of distinct primary inputs on which at least one designated output depends. Then g >= N-r. Proof: Delete every gate not ancestral to a designated output. Make an undirected graph whose vertices are the remaining gates and the N relevant input variables; connect a gate to each gate or input supplying one of its input wires, identifying repeated connections. Every vertex lies in a component containing a designated output signal. Add one new root vertex and connect it to the source vertex of each designated output, using at most r edges (duplicate outputs may be connected once). The resulting graph is connected, so it has at least N+g'-1 edges, where g' is the remaining gate count. At most 2g' edges are incident to gate input slots, and at most r edges are root-output edges; therefore N+g'-1 <= 2g'+r, which yields g' >= N-r and hence g >= N-r. This bound is purely linear and does not imply a superlinear state-recoding lower bound.

statement:
statement: REPAIR (unrolling implication). For deterministic one-pass realization of L with fixed initial state, update circuits F_1,...,F_N, and readout D over the same fan-in-two basis, C(L) <= sum_t size(F_t)+size(D). Hence C(L)>=B implies total realization cost >=B.
proof: Compose copies of F_1,...,F_N in order, wiring each state output to the next state input, and connect the final state to D. Feed x_t to F_t and hardwire the fixed initial state. Induction on t shows each intermediate state is the realization's state after the first t inputs, so the composition computes L. Its gate count is at most the sum displayed; wiring and fixed constants add no gates. The inequality and consequence follow.

label: S0525
statement: For every m>=1, let S=ceil(log2 m), N=2^S, Q be an m-element set, delta:Q->Q any map, and psi:Q->{0,1}^S any injection. The partial map psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q) has a total extension F on all N codewords with O(SN) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates and constants. Proof: For each output coordinate j prescribe F_j(psi(q)) as bit j of psi(delta(q)), and set F_j=0 on unused codewords. Shannon-expand F_j over the S input bits. The full binary decision tree has N leaves and N-1 internal mux nodes, each implementable with O(1) AND/NOT gates (OR via De Morgan); constants at leaves need no gates. Thus each coordinate uses O(N) gates, all S coordinates O(SN). On encoded q this equals psi(delta(q)). For m>=2, N<2m, so this is O(m log m).

label: S0526
statement: SPARSE-OUTPUT EXTENSION LEMMA. Let |Q|=m, S=ceil(log2 m), N=2^S, delta:Q->Q and psi:Q->{0,1}^S injective. Suppose exactly r coordinates are nonconstant on {psi(delta(q)):q in Q}. Then the partial transition psi delta psi^{-1} has a total extension computable with at most r(N-1) two-input muxes, and thus O(rN) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: for each of the r coordinates, prescribe its values on psi(Q) and extend arbitrarily to all N inputs. Shannon expansion on the S input bits is a full binary tree with N leaves and N-1 internal nodes. Each internal node computes a 2:1 mux; a mux is implementable with a constant number of AND/NOT gates by De Morgan's law. The remaining S-r coordinates are constant on psi(Q), so extend each by that constant at zero gate cost. The resulting coordinate functions agree with psi(delta(q)) on every encoded state, as required.

label: S0529
statement:
statement: REPAIR LEMMA (coarse sub-multiset bound). Let lambda be a partition of an integer L>=0, with multiplicity a_i for each part i. The number of sub-multisets of its parts, counted with multiplicities, is prod_{i:a_i>0}(a_i+1), and this is at most sum_{t=0}^L p(t) <= (L+1)p(L), where p(t) is the number of integer partitions of t and p(0)=1.
proof: Map a chosen sub-multiset (b_i), 0<=b_i<=a_i, to the partition with b_i parts equal to i. This map is injective and the resulting partition has total at most L, so the number is at most sum_{t=0}^L p(t). For 1<=t<=L, map a partition of t to one of L by adding L-t to its largest part; the map is injective, so p(t)<=p(L). Also p(0)=1<=p(L). Summing proves the bound. It repairs only the finite counting inequality and does not imply S0097's asymptotic separation.

label: S0530
statement: statement: FIXED-TRANSITION CYCLE-TYPE COEFFICIENT BOUND. Let F be a map on a finite set X, with directed cycles individually indexed and lengths k_1,...,k_r. For any m>=0, the number of distinct cycle types of restrictions F|A, over subsets A⊆X of size m on which F|A is a bijection A→A, is at most [z^m]∏_{j=1}^r(1+z^{k_j}). Proof: If F|A is bijective, each a∈A has a predecessor in A and all forward iterates remain in A. Since X is finite, its orbit is eventually periodic; injectivity of F|A rules out a nonempty tail before the periodic part (the first periodic point would have two distinct predecessors in A). Hence every point of A is periodic under F, and A is a union of whole directed cycles. Each indexed collection J of cycles gives a subset of size ∑_{j∈J}k_j and a resulting cycle type. The coefficient counts all such indexed collections of total size m, so it upper-bounds the number of distinct types, including when different collections yield the same type.
