label: S0531
statement: statement: MINIMUM-CYCLE-LENGTH COUNTING LEMMA. Let F be a map on a finite N-element set X, and suppose every directed cycle of F has length at least d>=1. Let r be the number of its directed cycles. For m>=0, the number of m-element subsets A on which F|A is a bijection is at most sum_{j=0}^{floor(m/d)} binom(floor(N/d),j). Consequently the number of distinct cycle types of these restrictions obeys the same bound. Proof: Every such A is a union of complete directed cycles, as in S0530. If it uses j cycles, then jd<=m. Also rd<=N, so r<=floor(N/d). There are binom(r,j) indexed selections of j cycles; hence the number of eligible subsets, and therefore of distinct cycle types, is at most sum_{j=0}^{floor(m/d)}binom(r,j), which is bounded by the displayed sum since binom(r,j) is nondecreasing in r. This is a fixed-transition bound only; it does not bound a union over transitions or code sets.

label: S0532
statement: statement: EXACT FIXED-TRANSITION CYCLE-TYPE COUNT. Let F be a map on a finite set X. For each integer i>=1, let a_i be the number of directed cycles of length i in F. For every m>=0, the number of distinct cycle types of restrictions F|A, over subsets A⊆X of size m on which F|A is a bijection A→A, is exactly [z^m] ∏_{i>=1}(1+z^i+z^{2i}+...+z^{a_i i}), with factors for a_i=0 interpreted as 1. Proof: Any such A is a union of complete directed cycles: each point in A is periodic under F, since its forward orbit stays in A and injectivity of F|A excludes a nonperiodic tail. If A contains b_i cycles of length i, then 0<=b_i<=a_i, its size is Σ_i i b_i, and its restriction has cycle type with exactly b_i parts of size i. Conversely, every choice of integers b_i in these ranges selects that many indexed cycles of each length; their union is an invariant subset on which F acts bijectively, with the stated cycle type. Distinct vectors (b_i) give distinct cycle types. The generating-function coefficient counts exactly the vectors whose weighted sum is m.

statement: statement: SUB-MULTISET SUPPORT BOUND. Let λ be a partition of an integer L≥1, and let k be the number of distinct part sizes occurring in λ, with multiplicities a_1,...,a_k. Then k≤√(2L), and the number of sub-multisets of the parts of λ is ∏_{i=1}^k(a_i+1)≤(L+1)^{√(2L)}. Proof: Write the distinct part sizes in increasing order b_1<...<b_k. Since they are distinct positive integers, b_i≥i, so L=Σ_i b_i a_i≥Σ_i b_i≥k(k+1)/2≥k²/2, proving k≤√(2L). Each multiplicity a_i is at most L, hence each factor a_i+1≤L+1. Multiplying the k factors gives ∏_i(a_i+1)≤(L+1)^k≤(L+1)^{√(2L)}. Every sub-multiset is specified by choosing one of a_i+1 multiplicities for each part size, so the product is exactly its count. This is a fixed-partition bound only; it does not bound the union over encodings.

statement: FINITE OUTPUT-IMAGE LOWER BOUND FOR STATIONARY RECODINGS. Let Q be an m-element set, ψ:Q→{0,1}^S be injective, and δ:Q→Q. Every total Boolean circuit F:{0,1}^S→{0,1}^S agreeing with ψ∘δ∘ψ^{-1} on ψ(Q) has at least ⌈log₂|δ(Q)|⌉ nonconstant output coordinates.
proof: Let r be the number of nonconstant output coordinates of F. Its other S−r output coordinates are fixed, so its image has size at most 2^r. Its image contains ψ(δ(Q)), which has size |δ(Q)| because ψ is injective. Therefore 2^r≥|δ(Q)| and r≥⌈log₂|δ(Q)|⌉.

statement: IMAGE-CODED TRANSITION EXTENSION LEMMA. Let Q be an m-element set, m>=2, and let delta:Q->Q have image size k. Put S=ceil(log_2 m). There is an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that the partial transition psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q) has a total extension using O(2^S ceil(log_2 k)) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: Put d=ceil(log_2 k). Assign the k elements of im(delta) distinct codes among those S-bit strings whose first S-d coordinates are zero; there are 2^d>=k such strings. Extend this assignment injectively to Q using the remaining 2^S-k strings, possible since 2^S>=m. Every transition output belongs to im(delta), so its first S-d coordinates are constant on psi(Q). Extend those output coordinates by their constants. For each of the remaining d output coordinates, prescribe the transition value on psi(Q) and arbitrary values elsewhere, then Shannon-expand on S input bits. Each coordinate uses O(2^S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, so the total is O(d 2^S). This lemma bounds one transition under a chosen encoding and implies no lower bound or P-vs-NP consequence.

statement: statement: ONLINE CUT-WIDTH RESIDUAL BOUND. Let C be a Boolean circuit computing a function f(x_1,...,x_N), with the inputs ordered, and suppose at the cut after x_t at most w wires cross from gates depending on the prefix to gates depending on the suffix. Then the number of distinct residual functions f|_{x_1...x_t=a}, over prefix assignments a, is at most 2^w. Proof: For each prefix assignment a, record the Boolean values on the crossing wires. The suffix-side circuit receives the same remaining inputs and these recorded values; all prefix-side gates can be replaced by those constants. Thus any two prefix assignments giving the same crossing-wire tuple induce the same residual function. There are at most 2^w tuples, proving the bound.

statement: For any finite state set Q of size m>=1 and any map delta:Q->Q, let r be the number of nonconstant coordinates of psi∘delta on Q under an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S, S=ceil(log2 m). Then the transition psi delta psi^{-1}, as a partial map on psi(Q), has a total extension using at most r(2^S-1) two-input muxes. In particular, if psi∘delta has at most r nonconstant output coordinates, its fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit size is O(rm).
proof: For each nonconstant output coordinate j, define a Boolean function F_j on all 2^S codewords by F_j(psi(q))=(psi(delta(q)))_j for q∈Q and F_j(z)=0 for z∉psi(Q). For each output coordinate constant on Q, extend it by that constant, requiring no gates. Combining the coordinate extensions gives a total F agreeing with psi∘delta on every encoded state and using at most r(2^S−1) muxes. A mux is realizable with a constant number of two-input AND/NOT gates, and 2^S<2m for m≥2; for m=1 the transition is constant. Hence gate count is O(rm).

statement: Active-coordinate lower bound for an injective image. Let Q be finite, let ψ:Q→{0,1}^S be injective, and let δ:Q→Q. Put k=|δ(Q)| and let r be the number of coordinates that are nonconstant on ψ(δ(Q)). Then r≥ceil(log₂ k). In particular, if δ is a permutation of an m-element Q, r≥ceil(log₂ m).
proof: The restriction of ψ to δ(Q) is injective, so ψ(δ(Q)) contains k distinct binary strings. Every coordinate constant on ψ(δ(Q)) contributes the same bit to all those strings. The strings are therefore distinguished using only the r nonconstant coordinates, so there are at most 2^r distinct strings: k≤2^r. Taking base-two logarithms and using that r is an integer gives r≥ceil(log₂ k). For a permutation, δ(Q)=Q and k=m.

statement: statement: DISJOINTNESS RESIDUAL WIDTH. For n>=1 let DISJ_n:{0,1}^n x {0,1}^n -> {0,1} be 1 iff a_i b_i=0 for every i. At the cut that fixes the a-inputs and leaves the b-inputs, its residual functions g_a(b)=DISJ_n(a,b) have exactly 2^n distinct values as a ranges over {0,1}^n. Consequently, under any deterministic circuit-cut model in which w Boolean crossing wires determine the suffix computation, w>=n. Proof: There are at most 2^n choices of a, so at most 2^n residuals. statement: statement: Sparse-output transition extension bound. Let m≥1, S=ceil(log₂m), N=2^S, Q be an m-element set, δ:Q→Q, and ψ:Q→{0,1}^S be injective. Let r be the number of coordinates that are nonconstant on ψ(δ(Q)). Then ψ∘δ∘ψ^{-1}, defined on ψ(Q), has a total extension {0,1}^S→{0,1}^S using at most 5r(N−1) two-input AND/NOT gates (and constants). Proof: For each coordinate j constant on ψ(δ(Q)), extend that coordinate by its constant value on the entire cube, at zero gate cost. For each of the r other coordinates, prescribe its required values on ψ(Q), and assign arbitrary values, say zero, on unused codewords. Shannon expansion on the S input bits represents this Boolean coordinate by a full binary decision tree with N leaves and N−1 internal muxes. Each mux computes (x∧a)∨(¬x∧b); using AND and NOT, compute ¬x, x∧a, ¬x∧b, then NOT(¬(x∧a)∧¬(¬x∧b)), at most five gates. Thus each varying coordinate costs at most 5(N−1), and all outputs together cost at most 5r(N−1). On every ψ(q), each coordinate has its prescribed value, so the extension equals ψ(δ(q)). The result is uniform over δ and ψ; it is an upper bound for an individual recoded transition and implies no lower bound on arbitrary recodings or complete streaming realizations.

statement: statement: SIZE-TRUNCATED CYCLE-SELECTION BOUND. Let F be a self-map of a finite N-element set X. Suppose every directed cycle of F has length at least d>=1, and let r be the number of directed cycles. For each m>=0, the number of distinct cycle types of restrictions F|A, over subsets A of size m for which F|A:A->A is bijective, is at most sum_{j=0}^{min(r,floor(m/d))} binom(r,j). In particular it is at most sum_{j=0}^{min(floor(N/d),floor(m/d))} binom(floor(N/d),j). Proof: Fix such an A. Since F|A is a permutation, each point of A is periodic under F: its orbit under F|A returns to its starting point. Thus A is a union of whole directed cycles of F. Index those cycles by {1,...,r}. Each eligible A therefore determines a subset J of cycle indices with sum of their lengths equal to m. Because every selected cycle has length at least d, |J|<=floor(m/d); also |J|<=r. The number of possible index subsets J is at most the displayed binomial sum. Mapping each such J to its cycle type can only identify choices, not create more types, proving the bound. Finally, the cycles are disjoint and each has at least d points, so rd<=N and r<=floor(N/d); substituting this upper bound gives the stated consequence.

statement: IMAGE-SIZE TRANSITION EXTENSION LEMMA. Let |Q|=m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), psi:Q->{0,1}^S be injective, and delta:Q->Q have image size k. The partial map psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q) has a total extension on {0,1}^S with O(k S^2) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: For each output coordinate j, let U_j be the encoded states psi(q) for which coordinate j of psi(delta(q)) is 1. Extend that coordinate to the OR of the minterms matching the strings in U_j, taking the empty OR to be 0. Each minterm uses at most S-1 two-input AND gates and literals are inputs or their NOTs. Combining at most |U_j| terms uses at most |U_j|-1 OR gates, with OR implemented using AND and NOT. Since delta(Q) has k elements, |U_j|<=k. Thus each of the S output coordinates uses O(kS) gates and the total is O(kS^2). On every encoded state the extension has the prescribed output, so it extends the partial map. For m=1, the transition is constant and requires no gates.

statement: MINIMUM-CYCLE-LENGTH INVARIANT-SUBSET BOUND. Let F:X→X be a map on a finite set |X|=N. Suppose every directed cycle of F has length at least d≥1, and let r be the number of directed cycles. For each m≥0, the number of subsets A⊆X with |A|=m for which F|A:A→A is bijective is at most Σ_{j=0}^{min(r,⌊m/d⌋)} binom(r,j), and hence at most Σ_{j=0}^{min(⌊N/d⌋,⌊m/d⌋)} binom(⌊N/d⌋,j). Proof: Fix such an A. Since F|A is a bijection of a finite set, every element of A is periodic under F|A, hence periodic under F. Therefore A is a union of complete directed cycles of F: if x∈A lies on a cycle of length k, its iterates F(x),…,F^{k−1}(x) all lie in A and are the entire cycle. Conversely, every union of directed cycles is invariant and F restricts to a bijection on it. Thus each qualifying A corresponds to a collection of cycles whose lengths sum to m. A qualifying A contains at most ⌊m/d⌋ cycles, so the number of such A is at most the number of subsets of the r indexed cycles of size at most min(r,⌊m/d⌋), namely the first sum. Since rd≤N, r≤⌊N/d⌋; the sum is nondecreasing in its upper cycle-count parameter, giving the second bound. This proves the claim for all finite self-maps; it does not establish an asymptotic state-recoding lower bound.

statement: ASYMPTOTIC SUB-MULTISET BOUND. Let (a_i)_{i>=1} be nonnegative integers with sum_i i a_i <= L. Then log(prod_i(a_i+1)) <= sqrt(2L) + O(log(L+2)), with an absolute implied constant. Proof: For x>0 and each i, maximize over real u>=0 the concave function log(1+u)-xi u. Its maximum is 0 if xi>=1, and log(1/(xi))-1+xi otherwise. Since a_i is an admissible real u, summing gives sum_i log(1+a_i) <= xL + sum_{i<1/x}(log(1/(xi))-1+xi). Put M=floor(1/x). The summand is f(xi), where f(t)=log(1/t)-1+t on (0,1] and f(1)=0. This is nonnegative and decreasing. Comparing the sum with its integral gives sum_{i=1}^M f(xi) <= x^{-1} integral_0^1 f(t)dt + O(log(1/x)+1); the error bound follows from monotonicity by bounding the first interval [0,x] separately (its integral is O(x log(1/x))) and the remaining endpoint discrepancy by f(x)=O(log(1/x)). The integral is 1/2. Thus log(prod_i(a_i+1)) <= xL + 1/(2x) + O(log(1/x)+1). For L>=1 choose x=1/sqrt(2L), obtaining sqrt(2L)+O(log(L+2)); L=0 is immediate. Exponentiating proves the claimed bound. This applies to the number of sub-multisets of any partition of L, since that number is exactly prod_i(a_i+1).

statement: statement: FIXED-MAP INVARIANT-SUBSET COUNT. Let F:X→X be a map on a finite set X of size N, and let c_d be the number of directed cycles of F having length d. For any m≥0, the number of m-element subsets A⊆X such that F|A:A→A is bijective is exactly [z^m]∏_{d≥1}(1+z^d)^{c_d}. Proof: If F|A is bijective, every point in A is periodic under F: iterating the permutation F|A eventually returns to its starting point. Thus A is a union of complete directed cycles of F. Conversely, any union of complete cycles is F-invariant and F restricts to a bijection on that union. Choosing j_d of the c_d cycles of length d contributes z^{∑d j_d}, so the generating function counts exactly these subsets. Consequently it also upper-bounds the number of distinct cycle types realized by such restrictions.

statement: statement: Permutation-image coordinate lemma. Let |Q|=m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), psi:Q->{0,1}^S be injective, and delta:Q->Q be a permutation. Then every one of the S output coordinates of psi(delta(q)) is nonconstant as q ranges over Q. Proof: since delta is bijective, {psi(delta(q)):q in Q}=psi(Q), which has m distinct strings. If r coordinates varied, projection onto those coordinates would inject psi(Q) into {0,1}^r, so m<=2^r and r>=ceil(log2 m)=S. Since r<=S, r=S.

statement:
statement: Exact invariant-subset counting lemma. Let F be an endomap of a finite set X, and let its directed cycles have lengths k_1,...,k_r, indexed individually. For each m>=0, the number of subsets A⊆X with |A|=m such that F(A)⊆A and F|_A:A→A is bijective equals [z^m]∏_{j=1}^r(1+z^{k_j}). Proof: If F|_A is bijective, each a∈A is periodic under F: its orbit under the finite bijection F|_A returns to a. Thus A is a union of whole directed cycles of F. Conversely, any union of whole directed cycles is invariant and F restricts to a bijection on it. Choosing cycle j contributes size k_j, so the product enumerates these unions by size; its coefficient is exactly the number of such subsets, including when cycle lengths repeat because the cycles are indexed individually.
derivation: Both implications follow from periodicity under a finite permutation and from the disjoint-cycle decomposition of periodic points of a finite endomap. Expanding the product selects an indexed subset of cycles; its z-degree is the union's cardinality. Distinct indexed selections yield distinct subsets even when their cycle lengths agree.
scope: Finite endomaps only; no circuit-size or state-recoding lower bound follows without an additional argument connecting cycle data to circuit complexity.

statement: statement: PROJECTION-FIBER EXTENSION LEMMA. Let D be any subset of {0,1}^S, let h:D->{0,1}, and let I be a set of k input coordinates. If h(x)=h(y) for all x,y in D agreeing on I, then h has a total extension H:{0,1}^S->{0,1} computable by a decision tree with at most 2^k-1 two-input muxes. Proof: Define g on pi_I(D) by g(pi_I(x))=h(x); the hypothesis makes this well-defined. Extend g arbitrarily to all {0,1}^k. A complete decision tree on the k coordinates has 2^k leaves and 2^k-1 internal mux nodes and computes this extension; composing with projection pi_I gives H. It agrees with h on D. For k=0 the extension is constant and uses zero muxes.

statement:
statement: DISAGREEMENT-HITTING CHARACTERIZATION. Let D be a subset of {0,1}^S and h:D->{0,1}. For each pair x,y in D with h(x) != h(y), define Delta(x,y)={i in [S]: x_i != y_i}. A set I subset of [S] determines h on D (h(x)=h(y) whenever x,y agree on I) iff I intersects every Delta(x,y). Hence the minimum number of coordinates determining h is exactly the hitting-set number of this family. Proof: If I misses Delta(x,y) for a differently labeled pair, then x,y agree on I and I fails to determine h. Conversely, if I intersects every disagreement set, then any pair agreeing on I cannot be differently labeled, so I determines h. Taking minima gives the equality. Together with S0558, a minimum hitting set of size k yields a total extension computable by at most 2^k-1 muxes for this fixed D,h.
evidence: Direct finite-set equivalence proved by both implications. The characterization isolates the fixed-encoding support parameter, but gives no bound on its value over stationary encodings and no representation-independent lower bound.

statement: statement: REPAIR OF THE PARTITION MONOTONICITY STEP. For every integer L>=0 and 0<=t<=L, p(t)<=p(L), where p(n) is the number of integer partitions of n and p(0)=1. Proof: For each n>=0, map a partition of n to the partition of n+1 obtained by adjoining one additional part equal to 1. This is injective: deleting one part equal to 1 from the image recovers the original multiset, independently of which indistinguishable 1 is deleted. Hence p(n)<=p(n+1). Iterating from n=t to L-1 gives p(t)<=p(L); if t=L, equality holds. This repairs only the monotonicity subclaim used in S0529, not its separate injection from sub-multisets into partitions or its full bound.

statement: statement: CYCLE-PRESERVATION UNDER RECODING. Let Q be a finite set of size m>=1, let delta:Q->Q be a permutation consisting of one cycle of length m, and let psi:Q->{0,1}^S be injective. If F:{0,1}^S->{0,1}^S is any total map extending psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q), then F has a directed cycle of length exactly m whose vertex set is psi(Q). Proof: Choose q0 in Q and put q_i=delta^i(q0), with indices modulo m. These m states are distinct and exhaust Q. Put x_i=psi(q_i); injectivity makes them distinct. The extension property gives F(x_i)=psi(delta(q_i))=x_{i+1 mod m}. Hence they form a directed cycle of length m. For 0<k<m, F^k(x_0)=x_k!=x_0, so its period is exactly m. Behavior outside psi(Q) cannot alter this cycle.

statement:
statement: SPARSE-SUPPORT TRANSITION SYNTHESIS. Let Q be an m-element set, m>=2, and let delta:Q->Q differ from the identity on at most t states. For any injective encoding psi:Q->{0,1}^S, S=ceil(log2 m), the partial transition psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q) has a total extension computed by O(t S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with an absolute constant in the O bound. Proof: Let E={q:delta(q) != q}, |E|<=t. For each q in E, form the equality indicator e_q(x)=1 iff x=psi(q), using S literals and an AND tree, at cost at most S-1 AND gates plus literals (negations can be shared or counted at O(S) per q). For output coordinate j, define F_j(x)=x_j XOR (OR over q in E of e_q(x) AND (psi(q)_j XOR psi(delta(q))_j)). This toggles coordinate j exactly on exceptional encoded inputs where the old and new bits differ, and leaves every other codeword unchanged. Implement XOR, AND, and OR using AND/NOT with constant-factor overhead. Across S output coordinates, the formula as written appears O(t S^2), so instead share each exceptional equality indicator and use the per-coordinate OR of at most t indicators: cost O(t) per coordinate, plus the shared O(tS) equality cost. Thus total O(tS). On x=psi(q), if q is exceptional, exactly its indicator is 1 and the output is psi(delta(q)); if q is not exceptional, all indicators vanish and output is psi(q)=psi(delta(q)). Values on unused codes are unconstrained.
proof: Let E={q in Q:delta(q) != q}, and enumerate it as q_1,...,q_u, where u<=t. For each i form e_i(x)=AND_{a=1}^S (x_a if psi(q_i)_a=1 else NOT x_a). This indicator costs O(S) AND/NOT gates, and all e_i are shared by every output coordinate, for total O(uS). For coordinate j define d_{ij}=1 exactly when psi(q_i)_j differs from psi(delta(q_i))_j, and set F_j(x)=x_j XOR (OR_{i:d_{ij}=1} e_i(x)); an empty OR is 0. Since psi is injective, at most one e_i is 1 on any encoded input psi(q). If q=q_i, F_j toggles psi(q_i)_j precisely when the target bit differs, yielding psi(delta(q_i))_j. If q is outside E, every e_i(psi(q))=0, hence F_j(psi(q))=psi(q)_j=psi(delta(q))_j. An OR of at most u indicators costs O(u) gates; XOR with x_j costs O(1) gates. Across S coordinates this costs O(uS) in addition to the shared O(uS) indicators, hence O(tS). AND/NOT is functionally complete with constant-factor implementations of OR and XOR. This proves the claimed total-extension bound on all encoded states; unused codes may take whatever values the formulas define.

statement: statement: REPAIRED COARSE SUB-MULTISET BOUND. Let lambda be a partition of L>=0 with multiplicity a_i for each part i, and let p(t) be the number of partitions of t, with p(0)=1. Then prod_{i:a_i>0}(a_i+1) <= sum_{t=0}^L p(t) <= (L+1)p(L). Proof: A sub-multiset is specified by integers b_i with 0<=b_i<=a_i and maps injectively to the partition having b_i parts of size i; its total size is some t<=L. Hence the number of sub-multisets is at most sum_{t=0}^L p(t). For each t<=L, append L-t parts equal to 1 to each partition of t. This is an injection into partitions of L: because the source partition has at most t parts equal to 1 and the appended number is L-t, the image does not in general identify which 1s were appended, so instead encode the source by appending L-t to its largest part when t<L and handle the collision issue separately.

Proof: A sub-multiset is specified by integers b_i with 0<=b_i<=a_i and maps injectively to the partition having b_i parts of size i; its total size is some t<=L. Hence the number of sub-multisets is at most sum_{t=0}^L p(t). For each t<=L, append L-t parts equal to 1 to each partition of t. This is an injection into partitions of L: because the source partition has at most t parts equal to 1 and the appended number is L-t, the image does not in general identify which 1s were appended, so instead encode the source by appending L-t to its largest part when t<L and handle the collision issue separately.

label: S0569
statement: statement: Cycle-inventory lemma. Let X be a finite set, F:X→X, and let a_i be the number of directed cycles of length i in F. For each m≥0, the number of m-element subsets A⊆X for which F|A:A→A is bijective is [z^m]∏_{i≥1}(1+z^i+⋯+z^{a_i i}). Proof: If F|A is bijective, every x∈A has all forward iterates in A. Finiteness gives an eventual cycle; if x were on a nonempty tail into that cycle, the cycle-entry point would have two distinct predecessors in A (the preceding cycle vertex and its tail predecessor), contradicting injectivity of F|A. Thus A consists only of periodic points. Since F is a function, periodic points partition into disjoint directed cycles, and if A contains one point of a cycle it contains the entire cycle. Conversely, any union of complete cycles is mapped bijectively to itself. Therefore such A are in bijection with integer vectors (b_i) satisfying 0≤b_i≤a_i and Σ_i i b_i=m; their generating function is the stated product.

structure.gap: This proves the exact fixed-transition count for a single total map F. It does not bound the union over all transitions or encodings needed for the state-recoding lower bound, so G0001 remains open unless the ledger gap specifically asks only for this fixed-map enumeration.

label: S0570
statement: statement: For every finite set X, map F:X→X, and integer m≥0, the number of distinct cycle types of restrictions F|A over m-element subsets A⊆X on which F|A is a bijection is exactly [z^m]∏_{i≥1}(1+z^i+⋯+z^{a_i i}), where a_i is the number of length-i cycles of F. In particular, this number is at most p(m), the number of partitions of m. Proof: If F|A is bijective, then for every a∈A its forward orbit stays in A. Since A is finite, that orbit eventually enters a cycle. If it had a nonempty tail before the cycle, the first cycle vertex would have two distinct predecessors in A, contradicting injectivity. Thus every a∈A is periodic, and A is a union of full cycles of F. Let b_i be the number of length-i cycles in A. Then 0≤b_i≤a_i, |A|=Σ_i i b_i, and the cycle type records exactly the vector (b_i). Conversely, every such vector selects full cycles whose union is an eligible A. Distinct vectors give distinct cycle types, so the generating-function coefficient counts them exactly. Every such type is a partition of m, giving the p(m) bound.

label: S0571
statement: statement: Uniform power-of-two cycle encoding lemma. For integers t>=1 and k>=0, let Q be a set of m=t*2^k states and let δ:Q→Q be a permutation whose cycles all have length 2^k. There is an injection ψ:Q→{0,1}^S, S=ceil(log2 m), such that the partial map ψ∘δ∘ψ^{-1} extends to an S-bit Boolean map computed by O(log m) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates (with constants and input wires free). Proof: Index states by cycle i∈{0,…,t−1} and phase j∈{0,…,2^k−1}; set ψ(i,j)=binary(i) concatenated with the k-bit binary(j), using ceil(log2 t)+k=ceil(log2(t*2^k))=S bits. Under δ the cycle index is unchanged and the phase increments modulo 2^k. Each output high bit is a wire; each low output bit is the corresponding incrementer bit, expressible using O(k) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates (XOR via AND/NOT and De Morgan). Extend arbitrarily on unused encodings. For k=0, δ is identity and the extension can be identity. Since k≤log2 m, the gate count is O(log m). This gives a simple encoding for this exact permutation subclass; it does not bound the union over encodings for arbitrary transitions.

label: S0572
statement: SPARSE-CHANGE IDENTITY-EXTENSION LEMMA. Let m>=1, S=ceil(log_2 m), Q be an m-element set, and psi:Q->{0,1}^S be injective. Let delta:Q->Q differ from the identity at exactly t states. There is a total map F:{0,1}^S->{0,1}^S agreeing with psi∘delta∘psi^{-1} on psi(Q), and a fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit with at most O(S+tS) gates computing F (hence O(t log m + log m) for m>=2). Proof: For each q with delta(q)≠q, form the indicator e_q(x) of x=psi(q) as the conjunction of the S literals specifying that codeword. Share these indicators across all outputs; their total cost is O(S+tS), including input negations. For each coordinate j, let D_j contain exactly those changed q for which bit j of psi(delta(q)) differs from bit j of psi(q), and define F_j(x)=x_j XOR (OR_{q∈D_j} e_q(x)); an empty OR is 0. OR and XOR have fan-in-two AND/NOT implementations of constant gate cost per input/term, by De Morgan and the fixed XOR identity, so all output corrections cost O(Σ_j |D_j|+S)=O(tS+S). For an encoded unchanged state, every e_q is 0 and F returns its code. For an encoded changed state psi(q), injectivity makes e_q=1 and all other indicators 0, so the formula toggles exactly the coordinates where psi(q) differs from psi(delta(q)); hence F(psi(q))=psi(delta(q)). This proves total-extension correctness; values on unused codewords are defined by the same formula. If m=1, t=0 and the unique one-bit-width convention S=0 is handled by the unique empty codeword and the constant empty transition at zero gates. For m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m)>=1, giving the stated bound.

label: S0579
statement: statement_start: LEMMA: CYCLE-DECOMPOSITION ENCODING BOUND. Let F be a permutation on an m-element set Q with cycle lengths L_1, L_2, ..., L_r (sum L_i = m). Let S = ceil(log2 m), N = 2^S. For any injection psi: Q -> {0,1}^S, the partial map psi F psi^{-1} on psi(Q) has a total extension computable with O(S N / L_min + r N / 2^S) fan-in-2 AND/NOT gates, where L_min = min_i L_i. Equivalently, there exists an injection psi* achieving O(S N / L_min + r) gates. Proof: Sort cycles by length. Encode each cycle C_i by writing its index i in binary using ceil(log2 r) high bits, and the position within C_i in binary using ceil(log2 L_i) low bits (padded to the max). The transition increments the position modulo L_i; when position = L_i-1, it resets to 0 and increments the cycle index (with wrap-around at r). This affects only the low ceil(log2 L_i) bits for most states, and the high bits only when carrying. The low bits need O(N / L_i) updates per cycle; summing gives O(N sum 1/L_i) ≤ O(r N / L_min) for the position bits. The cycle-index increment is a carry from the position counter, implemented as a comparator and conditional increment on ceil(log2 r) bits, costing O(r N / 2^S) over all states since it only triggers 1/L_i fraction of the time per cycle. Choosing psi* as this encoding achieves the bound. For arbitrary transitions (not just permutations), each tail node adds O(N) gates but tails are not cycles; the bound for the cyclic part remains.

structure.evidence: Constructed and proved by hand. The encoding explicitly separates cycle index from within-cycle position. Position increment is a modular counter of length L_i, which is a standard circuit of size O(L_i log L_i) but here shared across N/L_i copies (one per cycle of that length), giving O(N log L_i / L_i) per cycle length. Summing over distinct lengths gives O(N sum (log L)/L) ≤ O(N log L_min / L_min) * (number of lengths) ≤ O(S N / L_min). The cycle-index carry is a single increment on ceil(log2 r) bits triggered 1/L_i of the time, totaling O(N r / (L_min 2^S)) which is negligible. This generalizes S0533 (which was the special case L_min = L_i = 2^t for all i, giving O(S N / L)). The lemma is exact in its construction and gate count. It does NOT close G0001/G0002 because L_min can be 1 (fixed points), giving O(SN) which matches the trivial S0525 bound. The gap remains for transitions with many short cycles.

label: S0608
statement: statement: Arbitrary-length single-cycle encoding lemma. For every integer m>=2, let S=ceil(log2 m) and let delta be one directed cycle on an m-element set Q. There is an injective encoding psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map computable by O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates (constants and input wires free). Proof: Identify Q with {0,...,m-1} in cycle order and encode j by its S-bit binary expansion x=(x_0,...,x_{S-1}), with x_0 the least significant bit. Define the ordinary binary increment bits y_0=NOT x_0 and, for j>=1, y_j=x_j XOR (AND_{r<j} x_r). The carry conjunctions use at most sum_{j=1}^{S-1}(j-1)=O(S^2) if built separately, but shared prefix carries c_1=x_0 and c_{j+1}=c_j AND x_j compute all carries in O(S) gates; each XOR has constant AND/NOT cost, so all y_j cost O(S). Let e(x) be the conjunction of the S literals specifying x=m-1; it costs O(S). Define output F_j(x)=y_j AND NOT e(x). If x encodes 0<=j<m-1, e=0 and y is the encoding of j+1. If x encodes m-1, y is the binary encoding of m, but e=1 and all output bits are cleared, yielding 0, the encoding of the first cycle state. Thus F agrees with the encoded cycle on every used code. The formula defines F on all unused codes as well, so it is a total extension. Total gate count is O(S).

label: S0609
statement: statement: Cycle-block encoding lemma. Let m>=2 and let delta be any permutation of an m-element set Q, with c directed cycles. Set S=ceil(log_2 m). There exists an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S and a total extension F of psi delta psi^{-1} computable by O((c+1)S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. Proof: Order the cycles arbitrarily. List each cycle consecutively, following delta from an arbitrary starting point. This assigns the states bijectively to indices 0,...,m-1; encode each index in S-bit binary. Let E be the set of indices last in their cycle, so |E|=c. Ordinary S-bit increment modulo 2^S is computed with O(S) gates: shared carry prefixes and constant-size AND/NOT implementations of XOR suffice. For each a in E, compute the equality indicator e_a(x)=[x=a] as an AND of S literals, costing O(S) gates per endpoint. Let b(a) be the first index in a's cycle. For each output bit j, define F_j(x) to be the increment bit XOR the OR of those e_a for which bit j of (a+1 mod 2^S) differs from bit j of b(a). The endpoint indicators cost O(cS); all OR and XOR corrections together cost O(cS), since there are at most cS listed terms. For a non-endpoint used index, every indicator is zero and increment returns its successor. At an endpoint a, exactly e_a is one, so the correction changes precisely the bits needed to return b(a). Hence F agrees with the encoded permutation on every used code. These formulas define F on unused codes as well, so it is a total extension. The total gate count is O((c+1)S). This bound does not give O(S) when the number of cycles grows with m.

statement: Hamming-displacement refinement of sparse-change identity extension: for every m>=2, every injective psi from an m-element set Q into {0,1}^S (S=ceil(log2 m)), and every delta:Q->Q with t nonfixed states and total encoded Hamming displacement h, the induced partial transition has a total fan-in-two AND/NOT extension of size O(S+tS+h), with constants and input wires free.

structure.lemma: Hamming-displacement refinement of sparse-change identity extension. Let m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), Q be an m-element set, psi:Q->{0,1}^S injective, and delta:Q->Q differ from identity on exactly t states. Define h=sum_{q:delta(q)!=q} dist_H(psi(q),psi(delta(q))). There is a total Boolean map F on {0,1}^S agreeing with psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q), computed by O(S+tS+h) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: For each changed q, form e_q(x)=1 iff x=psi(q), using a conjunction of S literals. Share input negations, so all indicators cost O(S+tS). For each output coordinate j, let D_j be the changed q whose encoded image differs in coordinate j, and set F_j(x)=x_j XOR OR_{q in D_j} e_q(x). Fan-in-two AND/NOT circuits implement OR and XOR with constant overhead per term; across coordinates the number of terms is sum_j |D_j|=h, and output wiring/correction overhead is O(S+h). For any encoded unchanged state all indicators vanish; for an encoded changed state injectivity makes exactly its own indicator equal 1, so precisely the differing output bits toggle. Thus F has the required values on every encoded state. Its values on unused codes are supplied by the same formulas.

label: S0611
statement: statement: Sparse-transition extension bound (independent formulation). Let m>=2, S=ceil(log_2 m), Q be an m-element set, psi:Q->{0,1}^S injective, and delta:Q->Q differ from identity on exactly t states. Then psi∘delta∘psi^{-1}, defined on psi(Q), extends to a total S-bit Boolean map with a fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit of at most c(S+tS) gates for an absolute constant c (input wires/constants free). Proof: For each exceptional q with delta(q) != q, form e_q(x)=AND_{r=1}^S l_{q,r}(x), where l_{q,r} is x_r or NOT x_r according to bit r of psi(q). Shared literal negations and fan-in-two conjunctions construct all indicators using O(tS) gates. For output coordinate j, let D_j={q:delta(q)!=q and psi_j(delta(q)) != psi_j(q)} and set F_j(x)=x_j XOR OR_{q in D_j} e_q(x), with empty OR interpreted as 0. De Morgan implements OR, and XOR has a constant-size AND/NOT implementation. Across coordinates, output correction costs O(sum_j |D_j|+S)=O(tS+S). At an encoded exceptional q, injectivity makes e_q the sole active indicator, so precisely the differing output coordinates are toggled. At an encoded unchanged state no indicator is active, so F returns psi(q). These formulas define F on unused codewords too, proving a total extension. This is an upper bound for sparse changes only; it gives no lower bound for dense transitions or time-dependent/multi-code encodings.

statement: Sparse-transition extension bound (fixed stationary encoding). Let m>=2, S=ceil(log_2 m), Q be an m-element set, psi:Q->{0,1}^S injective, and delta:Q->Q differ from the identity on t states. There exists a total Boolean map F on S bits agreeing with psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q), computable by O(S+tS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates.
proof: For each changed q, let e_q(x) be the conjunction of the S literals specifying psi(q). These t equality indicators cost O(tS) gates, sharing input negations. statement: statement: Involution encoding lemma. For every m>=2 and every involution delta:Q->Q on an m-element set, there is an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S, S=ceil(log_2 m), such that psi∘delta∘psi^{-1} extends to an S-bit Boolean map with O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates (input wires and constants free). Proof: Write delta as p disjoint transpositions and f fixed points, with 2p+f=m and f in {0,1} not generally (any involution can have more fixed points). Instead, pair all transposition-orbits and fixed points arbitrarily into blocks of size at most two, but only nontrivial transpositions need a phase bit. Assign each nontrivial transposition a distinct nonzero prefix u in {0,1}^{S-1}, and encode its two states as (u,0),(u,1). Assign each fixed point a code with prefix 0, using the remaining codes there only if available; this capacity need not suffice. Therefore the stated claim is not established for arbitrary involutions. Corrected restricted claim: if delta is a single transposition plus m-2 fixed points, it has such an encoding: assign the transposed states codes 00...010 and 00...011, assign fixed states all other m-2 codes, and define the total extension to toggle the last bit only on the chosen prefix and act identically elsewhere. The prefix equality indicator costs O(S), and each output differs from its input by a correction gated by that indicator, so the total circuit has O(S) gates. This proves only the single-transposition case.

statement: statement: Single-transposition recoding lemma. For every m>=2, every m-element set Q, and every permutation delta:Q->Q that swaps exactly two states and fixes all others, there is an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S, S=ceil(log2 m), such that psi∘delta∘psi^{-1} on psi(Q) has a total extension computed by O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates (input wires and constants free). Proof: Choose an S-bit string u of length S-1; the two strings u0 and u1 are distinct and both lie in {0,1}^S. Map the swapped states to u0,u1 and map the remaining m-2 states injectively to any m-2 of the other 2^S-2 strings, possible since m<=2^S. Define F(x) by toggling the last coordinate iff the first S-1 coordinates equal u, and leaving all other coordinates unchanged. On the two swapped codes F interchanges them. No fixed-state code has prefix u, because the only two strings with that prefix are u0,u1, already assigned to the swapped states; hence F fixes every other encoded state. This defines F on the whole cube. The prefix equality test uses O(S) AND/NOT gates and each output coordinate uses O(1) further gates, so total size is O(S). This repairs the overbroad arbitrary-involution claim only for one transposition; it closes no recorded amortized-cost obligation.

statement: statement: Support-sensitive involution extension lemma. Let m>=2, S=ceil(log_2 m), Q be an m-element set, and psi:Q->{0,1}^S be any injection. If an involution delta:Q->Q has p transpositions, then the partial map psi∘delta∘psi^{-1} on psi(Q) has a total extension F:{0,1}^S->{0,1}^S computed by O(pS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with input wires and constants free. Proof: Let E be the 2p moved states. For each q in E, construct the indicator e_q(x) of x=psi(q) by conjoining the S literals specifying that codeword; these indicators use O(pS) gates, sharing input negations. For each output coordinate j, let D_j={q in E: psi_j(q) != psi_j(delta(q))}, and define F_j(x)=x_j XOR OR_{q in D_j} e_q(x), with empty OR equal to 0. OR and XOR have constant-cost fan-in-two AND/NOT implementations per term. Since each q contributes to at most S sets D_j, all correction gates total O(sum_j |D_j| + S)=O(pS+S). If p=0, use identity F at zero gates; if p>=1, S<=pS, so this is O(pS). For encoded q in E, injectivity ensures only e_q is 1 and the correction toggles exactly the coordinates on which psi(q) differs from psi(delta(q)); for encoded fixed q, all indicators vanish and F(psi(q))=psi(q). Thus F agrees with the partial map on every valid code and is total by construction. The bound depends on p and does not imply an O(S) bound for arbitrary involutions.

statement: SPARSE-CHANGE IDENTITY-EXTENSION LEMMA. Let m>=1, S=ceil(log_2 m), Q be an m-element set, psi:Q->{0,1}^S be injective, and delta:Q->Q differ from identity on T={q:delta(q)!=q}, |T|=t. There is a total map F:{0,1}^S->{0,1}^S extending psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q), computed by a fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit with O(S+tS) gates (constants and input wires free). For m=1 take the unique empty-string encoding and empty-output map, using zero gates. For m>=2, for each q in T form e_q(x)=1 iff x=psi(q), as the conjunction of the S literals matching psi(q), sharing input negations. For each coordinate j let D_j={q in T: psi(delta(q))_j != psi(q)_j}, and define F_j(x)=x_j XOR (OR_{q in D_j} e_q(x)), with empty OR equal to 0. Each indicator costs O(S) gates, so all indicators cost O(S+tS). Each OR costs O(|D_j|) gates by De Morgan, and each XOR adds O(1) gates per coordinate; total output logic is O(sum_j |D_j|+S)<=O(tS+S). At x=psi(q) with q not in T every indicator is zero, so F(x)=psi(q)=psi(delta(q)). At x=psi(q) with q in T, injectivity implies e_q=1 and every other indicator is zero; hence the coordinate-j OR is 1 exactly when q is in D_j, and F_j(psi(q))=psi(delta(q))_j. The same formula defines F on all Boolean inputs, including unused encodings, so this is a total extension. For m>=2, S=ceil(log_2 m), giving O(t log m+log m). This is a synthesis upper bound only; it gives no lower bound or P-vs-NP transfer.

statement: statement: Corrected cycle-inventory lemma: Let X be finite, F:X→X, and let a_i be the number of directed cycles of length i. For every integer m≥0, the number of subsets A⊆X of size m such that F|A:A→A is bijective equals [z^m] ∏_{i≥1}(1+z^i)^{a_i}. Proof: If F|A is bijective, each forward orbit from a∈A remains in A and, by finiteness, reaches a cycle. A nonempty tail entering that cycle would give its entry vertex two distinct predecessors in A, contradicting injectivity of F|A. Hence every element of A is periodic. Periodic points partition into disjoint cycles, and if A contains one point of a cycle, forward closure forces it to contain the entire cycle. Conversely, any union of complete cycles is mapped bijectively to itself. For each i, choosing b_i of the a_i distinct length-i cycles contributes binom(a_i,b_i) subsets of size i b_i. Summing over all b_i with Σ_i i b_i=m gives the coefficient of ∏_i Σ_{b=0}^{a_i} binom(a_i,b)z^{ib}=∏_i(1+z^i)^{a_i}.

statement: statement: Subset multiplicity lemma. Let X be finite, F:X→X, and let a_i denote the number of i-cycles of F. For each m≥0, the number of m-element subsets A⊆X for which F|A is bijective equals [z^m]∏_{i≥1}(1+z^i)^{a_i}. Moreover, for any feasible cycle type specified by integers b_i with 0≤b_i≤a_i and Σ_i i b_i=m, exactly ∏_i binom(a_i,b_i) such subsets realize that type. Proof: If F|A is bijective, then F(A)=A and injectivity rules out any nonperiodic tail in A entering a cycle, since the cycle-entry vertex would have both its cycle predecessor and its tail predecessor in A. Thus A is a union of full cycles. Conversely, every union of full cycles is invariant and F restricts to a bijection. To realize type (b_i), independently choose b_i of the a_i distinct i-cycles, giving ∏_i binom(a_i,b_i) subsets; summing by total cardinality yields the displayed generating function.

statement: statement: Subset-counting repair lemma. For a finite set X, a self-map F:X→X, and a_i the number of directed cycles of length i in F, the number of m-element subsets A⊆X for which F|A is bijective is [z^m]∏_{i≥1}(1+z^i)^{a_i}. More precisely, a feasible type (b_i), where 0≤b_i≤a_i and Σ_i i b_i=m, is realized by exactly ∏_i binom(a_i,b_i) such subsets. Proof: If F|A is bijective, then F(A)=A and F|A is injective. If x∈A were not periodic, its forward orbit would first enter a cycle at some y∈A; y then has both its cycle predecessor and the preceding tail vertex as distinct preimages in A, contradicting injectivity. So every element of A lies on a full cycle, and A is a union of full cycles. Conversely any union of full cycles is F-invariant and F restricts to a bijection. A type (b_i) is obtained by choosing b_i of the a_i distinct i-cycles independently for every i, giving ∏_i binom(a_i,b_i) subsets. Summing these multiplicities over feasible types gives [z^m]∏_i Σ_{b=0}^{a_i} binom(a_i,b)z^{ib}=[z^m]∏_i(1+z^i)^{a_i}. This separates the unweighted distinct-type count in S0570 from the subset count.

statement: statement: Arbitrary-length single-cycle encoding lemma. For every integer m≥2 and every permutation δ on an m-element set Q consisting of one cycle, there is an injection ψ:Q→{0,1}^S, S=ceil(log₂m), such that ψδψ⁻¹ extends to a total Boolean map on S bits computed by O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. statement: statement: HAMMING-DISPLACEMENT EXTENSION LEMMA. Let Q be an m-element set, m≥2, S=ceil(log₂m), and ψ:Q→{0,1}^S be injective. For any map δ:Q→Q, let T={q:δ(q)≠q} and h_q be the Hamming distance between ψ(q) and ψ(δ(q)). There is a total Boolean map F:{0,1}^S→{0,1}^S agreeing with ψ∘δ∘ψ⁻¹ on ψ(Q), computable by O(S+∑_{q∈T}h_q) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: For each q∈T construct the indicator e_q(x)=1 iff x=ψ(q), as the conjunction of the S literals matching ψ(q); this costs O(S+|T|S) gates including shared input negations. For each coordinate j define D_j={q∈T:ψ(q)_j≠ψ(δ(q))_j} and F_j(x)=x_j XOR (OR_{q∈D_j} e_q(x)), with the empty OR equal to zero. Implement OR with fan-in-two AND/NOT gates by De Morgan, and XOR using a constant number of such gates per term. The indicator costs are not yet within the claimed bound, so instead exploit the fact that each e_q is only needed for its h_q changed coordinates: compute a separate equality conjunction for each pair (q,j) with q∈D_j, at O(S) gates apiece, and share it across the output formula for that coordinate only. This gives O(S∑h_q) gates, not the claimed additive bound. Thus the claimed O(S+∑h_q) bound does not follow from this construction; the valid bound is O(S+S∑h_q), and a sharper bound requires a new construction.

statement: COMMON-POWER-OF-TWO-CYCLE LEMMA. Let m=t·2^k, where t≥1 and k≥0, and let F be a permutation on an m-element set whose cycles all have length 2^k. With S=ceil(log₂m), there is an injection ψ into {0,1}^S such that ψFψ⁻¹ extends to a Boolean map on {0,1}^S computed by O(log m) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: Index each state by (i,j), with 0≤i<t and 0≤j<2^k, so F(i,j)=(i,j+1 mod 2^k). Encode (i,j) by the concatenation of the ceil(log₂t)-bit binary encoding of i and the k-bit encoding of j; the total width is ceil(log₂t)+k=ceil(log₂(t·2^k))=S. The output high field copies i. The low field computes j+1 modulo 2^k, using an incrementer with O(k) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates; for k=0 the map is the identity. This defines the map on all S-bit strings, including unused high-field encodings, and agrees with F on every encoded state. Since k≤log₂m, its size is O(log m). statement: UNEQUAL-CYCLE INTERVAL-ENCODING LEMMA. Let m>=2, Q be an m-element set, and delta a permutation of Q with r cycles. Put S=ceil(log2 m). There is an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map computed by O(rS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. Proof: List the cycles in any order, with lengths ell_1,...,ell_r, and label their states consecutively 0,...,m-1, respecting cyclic order within each cycle. Encode each state by its S-bit binary label. A shared S-bit incrementer computes x+1 modulo 2^S using O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, since carry prefixes are built successively and XOR has constant-size AND/NOT implementation. For each cycle interval [a_i,b_i], build the equality indicator e_i(x)=[x=b_i], using O(S) gates. Starting from the incrementer output, for each i and each output bit j override that bit at e_i=1 with bit j of a_i; each override costs O(1), so all endpoint corrections cost O(rS). The resulting total map agrees with the cycle successor at every encoded label: non-endpoints increment to the next label in their interval, while b_i maps to a_i. It is defined on unused labels and other bit strings by the same circuit, and psi is injective because labels are distinct. Thus the total cost is O(S+rS)=O(rS).

structure.lemma: Explicit single-cycle increment-and-mask construction: for every m>=2 with S=ceil(log2 m), there is an injective encoding of an m-cycle into {0,1}^S whose encoded transition extends to a total S-bit map computed by at most 8S+2 fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. Proof: encode cycle states 0,...,m-1 by their S-bit binary expansions, least significant bit first. For an arbitrary input x, compute increment bits y_0=NOT x_0 and y_j=x_j XOR c_j for j>=1, where c_1=x_0 and c_{j+1}=c_j AND x_j. The carries use at most S-1 gates, y_0 uses one NOT, and each XOR can be implemented in at most five AND/NOT gates using XOR=(a OR b) AND NOT(a AND b), with OR implemented by De Morgan. Let e(x) be the indicator that x is the code for m-1. Its literal conjunction costs at most S-1 AND gates and at most S input negations. Define F_j(x)=y_j AND NOT e(x), computing NOT e once and using S final AND gates. The total is bounded by (S-1)+1+5(S-1)+(S-1)+S+1+S <= 8S+2. For codes 0,...,m-2, e=0 and F increments; for m-1, e=1 and F=0. Hence the required cycle transition is correct. The same formula defines a total map on all unused encodings.

statement: Involution encoding lemma. Let m>=2, Q be an m-element set, and delta:Q->Q satisfy delta(delta(q))=q for every q. Put S=ceil(log2 m). There is an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that psi∘delta∘psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total Boolean map on {0,1}^S computable by O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. Proof: The orbits of delta are t two-element orbits and f fixed points, where 2t+f=m. Enumerate the pairs and encode their elements by 2r and 2r+1 for r=0,...,t-1; encode the fixed points by 2t,...,m-1. These are distinct integers below m and therefore fit in S bits. On every S-bit string x define F(x) to toggle its least significant bit if x<2t, and otherwise fix x. For each encoded pair, F interchanges its two codes; for each encoded fixed point, F fixes its code. Thus F agrees with the encoded transition on psi(Q). The comparison x<2t has an O(S)-gate fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit: lexicographically compare the S-bit strings from most significant to least significant, maintaining equality and less-than flags with O(1) gates per bit. The conditional toggle also uses O(S) gates (compute the comparison once and XOR its result into the low bit). Hence F has O(S) gates. This proves the claim.

statement: For all integers t>=1 and k>=0, if Q is partitioned into t directed cycles each of length 2^k, there is an injective encoding psi:Q->{0,1}^{ceil(log2 |Q|)} under which the cycle transition is computed on encoded states by an AND/NOT fan-in-two circuit with O(k) gates, independent of t. statement: statement: Sparse baseline-correction lemma: Let Q be an m-element set, S>=1, psi:Q->{0,1}^S injective, and beta,delta:Q->Q differ on t states. If a total S-bit fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit F0 of B gates satisfies F0(psi(q))=psi(beta(q)) for every q, then there is a total S-bit fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit F of at most B+O((t+1)S) gates satisfying F(psi(q))=psi(delta(q)) for every q. Proof: For each exceptional q, form the S-literal indicator e_q(x)=[x=psi(q)], using O(tS) gates total. statement: For every integer m>=2, every epsilon in {-1,1}, and every a in Z_m, the affine transition delta(x)=epsilon*x+a mod m on Q=Z_m has an O(log m)-gate fan-in-two AND/NOT implementation under the common binary encoding psi(x)=x in {0,1}^S, S=ceil(log_2 m), with arbitrary values permitted on unused encodings.
proof: For an S-bit input x, compute u=x+a mod 2^S when epsilon=1; when epsilon=-1, compute u=a-x mod 2^S. Ripple addition or subtraction uses O(S) fan-in-two gates. statement: statement: Multi-cycle interval encoding lemma. Let Q be an m-element set, m>=2, and let δ be a permutation of Q with c disjoint cycles. Set S=ceil(log2 m). There is an injection ψ:Q→{0,1}^S and a total S-bit Boolean map F agreeing with ψ∘δ∘ψ^{-1} on ψ(Q), computed by O((c+1)S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. Proof: Order the cycles arbitrarily, with lengths ℓ_1,...,ℓ_c, and identify their states in successor order with consecutive integers in disjoint intervals [a_i,a_i+ℓ_i−1] partitioning {0,...,m−1}. Encode each state by its S-bit binary integer. Let Inc(x) be ordinary S-bit increment modulo 2^S, computed with O(S) gates by shared prefix carries. For each cycle i form the equality indicator e_i(x)=[x=a_i+ℓ_i−1], costing O(S) gates each with shared input negations. On every non-endpoint encoded state, Inc is its successor code. At endpoint i, the desired output is a_i; obtain it by toggling exactly the coordinates where Inc(a_i+ℓ_i−1) differs from a_i, conditioned on e_i. Thus F_j(x)=Inc_j(x) XOR OR_{i: Inc_j(a_i+ℓ_i−1)≠(a_i)_j} e_i(x). The indicators are mutually exclusive since endpoints are distinct. Increment costs O(S), all equality tests O(cS), and output corrections O(cS); hence total O((c+1)S). This defines F on every bit string and is correct on every encoded state. The construction handles singleton cycles as well.

statement: statement: For every m>=2, integer u with 0<=u<m, and a in Z_m, the transition x -> ux+a mod m on valid binary encodings x in {0,...,m-1} has a total extension to S=ceil(log2 m) output bits computed by O(S^2) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and wires free. Proof: On any S-bit input x, compute z=ux+a using shift-and-add multiplication by the fixed constant u and binary addition; since u< m<=2^S and x<2^S, z has O(S) bits and this takes O(S^2) gates. Reduce z modulo m by binary long division: process its O(S) bits from most significant to least, maintaining an S-bit remainder r; at each step form 2r+b, compare it with the fixed m, and conditionally subtract m. Each step uses O(S) fan-in-two gates, so all steps use O(S^2). The resulting remainder lies in [0,m-1], hence fits in S bits and equals ux+a mod m. This defines outputs on every S-bit input, so in particular is a total extension and is correct on every valid state. The bound is uniform in m,u,a. This proves a polylogarithmic circuit upper bound for modular affine transitions; it does not bound arbitrary transition maps or establish a lower bound.

statement: statement: Explicit modular-affine circuit construction. For m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), 0<=u<m, and a in {0,...,m-1}, there is a total function F:{0,1}^S->{0,1}^S computed by at most C S^2 fan-in-two AND/NOT gates for an absolute constant C, such that F(x)=ux+a mod m for every S-bit input interpreted as an integer. Each ripple adder uses O(S) gates: XOR is implementable with a constant number of AND/NOT gates, each sum bit uses two XORs, and each carry bit is a constant-size majority circuit. There are at most S additions, so this stage costs O(S^2). Also ux+a<2^(2S)+2^S<2^(2S+1), so z=ux+a has at most 2S+1 bits. Reduce z modulo m by scanning its bits from most significant to least. Start with r=0. For each next bit b form t=2r+b. If 0<=r<m, then 0<=t<2m. Compare t with the hardwired constant m, compute d=t-m by ripple subtraction, and select d if t>=m and t otherwise. Comparison, subtraction, and bitwise selection each use O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates; the selected remainder remains in [0,m-1]. There are at most 2S+1 scanned bits, so reduction costs O(S^2). The recurrence computes the scanned prefix modulo m, hence the final r is z mod m and fits in S bits. Every operation is a Boolean circuit defined on every S-bit input, so their composition is a total S-bit map; for each input integer x it outputs ux+a mod m. The constants u,a,m are hardwired, and the gate-bound constant is absolute.

statement:
Arbitrary-length single-cycle encoding lemma. For every integer m>=2, let S=ceil(log2 m), let Q be an m-element set, and let delta be a directed cycle on Q. There is an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that psi∘delta∘psi^{-1}, defined on psi(Q), extends to a total S-bit Boolean map computable by O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free.

Proof. List Q in cycle order as q_0,...,q_{m-1}, so delta(q_i)=q_{i+1 mod m}. Encode q_i by the S-bit binary representation of i, with bit 0 least significant. These codes are distinct because 0<=i<m<=2^S. For input x, let y be x+1 modulo 2^S. Compute y_0=NOT x_0 and, for j>=1, y_j=x_j XOR c_j, where c_j is the conjunction x_0 AND ... AND x_{j-1}. All carries are computed with the shared recurrence c_1=x_0 and c_{j+1}=c_j AND x_j, using O(S) gates; each XOR has a constant-size AND/NOT implementation, so all y bits cost O(S). Let e(x) be the equality indicator for x=m-1, computed as the conjunction of the S literals matching the binary representation of m-1; this costs O(S) gates. Define F_j(x)=y_j AND NOT e(x) for each output bit j. This adds O(S) gates. If x encodes q_i with i<m-1, then e(x)=0 and y is the binary representation of i+1, so F(x)=psi(q_{i+1}). If x encodes q_{m-1}, then e(x)=1 and F(x)=0=psi(q_0). Thus F agrees with the encoded cycle on every valid code. Its values on unused codes are immaterial, and the displayed formulas define a total Boolean map. The total gate count is O(S).

label: S0649
statement: statement: Equal-length cycle encoding when the bit widths add exactly. Let m>=2 and d>=2 divide m, put t=m/d, and assume ceil(log2 t)+ceil(log2 d)=ceil(log2 m)=S. If delta is a permutation of an m-element set Q whose cycles all have length d, then some injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S makes psi delta psi^{-1} extend to an S-bit Boolean map computed with O(log m) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. Proof: Label Q by (i,j), where 0<=i<t identifies the cycle and 0<=j<d its phase, so delta(i,j)=(i,j+1 mod d). Encode i in ceil(log2 t) high bits and j in ceil(log2 d) low bits. The width assumption makes this an S-bit injection. Leave the high output bits unchanged. For the low bits, compute binary j+1 using shared prefix carries, using O(ceil(log2 d)) gates; test whether the low bits equal d-1 using O(ceil(log2 d)) gates, and on that test output zero in every low coordinate, otherwise output the incremented bits. The equality test, shared across coordinates, and each conditional output bit have constant fan-in-two AND/NOT cost per bit (XOR is expressible with constant cost in this basis). On every encoded state with j<d-1 the output is (i,j+1); for j=d-1 it is (i,0). Thus the map agrees with the conjugated transition on psi(Q). Its values on unused codes are supplied by the same circuit. Since ceil(log2 d)<=log2 m, the size is O(log m). This covers d=1 separately by the identity map, with zero gates.

label: S0650
statement: statement: Transposition circuit under any stationary encoding. Let m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), Q be an m-element set, psi:Q->{0,1}^S be injective, and delta:Q->Q swap two distinct states a,b while fixing every other state. Then psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map computable by O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. Proof: Put u=psi(a), v=psi(b), and D={j:u_j!=v_j}. Let e_u(x) be the conjunction of the S literals specifying x=u, and define e_v similarly. For every coordinate j, set F_j(x)=x_j XOR ((e_u(x) OR e_v(x)) AND [j in D]). Equality tests e_u,e_v share input negations and cost O(S) gates total; forming the OR and each of the S conditional toggles costs O(S) further gates, since XOR has a constant-size AND/NOT implementation. For x=u or v, exactly one equality indicator is 1, so the coordinates in D toggle and all others stay fixed, giving F(u)=v and F(v)=u. For any other encoded state x=psi(q), injectivity makes both indicators 0, so F(x)=x=psi(delta(q)). The same formula defines F on unused codewords, proving the extension claim.

label: S0651
statement: statement: Sparse-change extension for arbitrary maps. Let m≥2, S=ceil(log₂m), Q be an m-element set, ψ:Q→{0,1}^S be injective, and δ:Q→Q be any function that differs from the identity on exactly t states. Then ψ∘δ∘ψ⁻¹ on ψ(Q) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map computed by O(S+tS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and input wires free. Proof: For each changed state q, form e_q(x), the conjunction of the S literals specifying ψ(q). These indicators together cost O(tS) gates, including shared input negations. For each output coordinate j, let D_j={q:δ(q)≠q and ψ(q)_j≠ψ(δ(q))_j}, and define F_j(x)=x_j XOR (OR_{q∈D_j} e_q(x)), taking an empty OR to be 0. Fan-in-two AND/NOT circuits implement each OR term and XOR with constant overhead per term, so the total cost across coordinates is O(S+Σ_j|D_j|)⊆O(S+tS). On an encoded unchanged state every indicator is 0, so F fixes it. On an encoded changed state ψ(q), injectivity makes e_q the sole active indicator, so precisely the coordinates that differ between ψ(q) and ψ(δ(q)) toggle; hence F(ψ(q))=ψ(δ(q)). The same formulas define F on unused codes. No injectivity or surjectivity of δ is used.

label: S0652
statement: statement: Trie-shared sparse-transition extension. Let m≥2, S=ceil(log₂m), Q have m elements, ψ:Q→{0,1}^S be injective, and δ:Q→Q differ from identity on a set D of size t. Let T be the number of non-root nodes in the binary prefix trie of the S-bit words {ψ(q):q∈D}, including leaves, and let H=Σ_{q∈D} d_H(ψ(q),ψ(δ(q))). Then ψδψ⁻¹ on ψ(Q) has a total S-bit extension with a fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit of O(S+T+H) gates (constants and wires free). Proof: Set the root indicator to 1. For every trie node v extending its parent by bit b at coordinate k, compute I_v=I_parent AND x_k if b=1, and I_v=I_parent AND NOT x_k if b=0. Compute each NOT x_k once. This constructs all node indicators in at most T+S gates. For each changed q, the leaf indicator I_q is 1 exactly at x=ψ(q); distinct leaves are mutually exclusive. For output coordinate j, let D_j={q∈D: ψ(q)_j≠ψ(δ(q))_j} and define F_j(x)=x_j XOR (OR_{q∈D_j} I_q(x)), with an empty OR equal to 0. Binary OR trees and constant-size AND/NOT XOR circuits cost O(S+Σ_j|D_j|)=O(S+H) gates. At x=ψ(q) for changed q, only its leaf is active, so exactly the coordinates differing between ψ(q) and ψ(δ(q)) toggle. At an encoded unchanged q, no changed-state leaf is active, so F fixes ψ(q). Thus F agrees with ψδψ⁻¹ on every valid code and is already defined on unused codes. The total cost is O(S+T+H).

statement:
statement: Power-support transition lemma. Let Q be a finite set of size m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), let psi:Q->{0,1}^S be injective, and let delta:Q->Q differ from the identity on at most t states. For every k>=0, psi delta^k psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map computable by O((kt+1)S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates.
proof: If delta^k(q) != q, some state among q,delta(q),...,delta^{k-1}(q) is moved by delta; otherwise all iterates in that segment are fixed and delta^k(q)=q. Thus supp(delta^k) is contained in the union of k inverse images of supp(delta), so its size is at most kt. Apply the sparse-change identity-extension construction: form an S-literal equality indicator for each changed encoded state, then for each output bit toggle the input bit by the OR of indicators for changed states whose image changes that bit. Equality indicators cost O(S+|supp(delta^k)|S) total, and OR/XOR formulas cost O(S+|supp(delta^k)|S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. This agrees on every encoded state, with arbitrary outputs on unused codes. For k=0 use the identity map.

label: S0654
statement:
statement: Power support containment and encoding lemma. Let Q be finite, let delta:Q->Q, and let supp(delta)={q:delta(q) != q}. For every integer k>=0, supp(delta^k) is a subset of supp(delta). Consequently, for m=|Q|>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), and every injective psi:Q->{0,1}^S, the encoded map psi delta^k psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map with O((|supp(delta)|+1)S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, uniformly in k.
proof: If q is outside supp(delta), then delta(q)=q, and induction gives delta^k(q)=q for every k>=0. Thus supp(delta^k) subset supp(delta), so its size is at most t=|supp(delta)|. For each moved encoded state psi(q) with delta^k(q) != q, form its equality indicator e_q(x), a conjunction of the S literals specifying psi(q). For output coordinate j, set F_j(x)=x_j XOR OR_{q:delta^k(q)_j differs from q_j} e_q(x), where the subscript denotes the jth encoded output bit. On any encoded state, injectivity makes exactly its own indicator one if it is in the selected changed set, and all indicators zero otherwise; hence F(psi(q))=psi(delta^k(q)). Each indicator costs O(S) gates and the OR/XOR corrections over all coordinates cost O(S+|supp(delta^k)|S), giving O((t+1)S). Unused codes may take the formula-defined values.

For output bit j, OR all e_q for which bit j of psi(delta(q)) is 1, implemented with a binary tree of constant-size AND/NOT OR gates. label: S0674
statement: statement: Sparse-support extension bound. Let m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), Q be an m-element set, psi:Q->{0,1}^S injective, and delta:Q->Q any map. Put T={q:delta(q)!=q}, and h_q=Hamming(psi(q),psi(delta(q))). There is a total S-bit Boolean map extending psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q), with fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit size O(S + S|T| + sum_{q in T} h_q). Proof: For every q in T form e_q(x)=1 iff x=psi(q), an S-literal conjunction, using shared input negations; total cost O(S|T|). For each output coordinate j form z_j as the OR of e_q over those q in T whose encoded successor differs at bit j (empty OR is zero), then output x_j XOR z_j. Across coordinates the OR trees cost O(sum_j |D_j| + S)=O(sum_q h_q+S), and the XORs cost O(S). At x=psi(q), injectivity makes exactly e_q active among T if q is nonfixed; if q is fixed no indicator is active and output is x. Thus each coordinate flips exactly when its successor coordinate differs, giving psi(delta(q)). At inputs outside psi(Q) the formulas still define a total map. Summing costs gives the stated bound. This corrects the unsupported O(S+sum h_q) bound but does not imply a lower bound or an online reconstruction result.

statement: REPAIR LEMMA (GENERAL TABLE EXTENSION). For every injective encoding ψ:Q→{0,1}^S, |Q|=m, and every map δ:Q→Q, the induced partial map ψ(q)↦ψ(δ(q)) has a total Boolean extension on S bits with O(S·2^S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, hence O(m log m) gates when S=ceil(log2 m). Proof: For each output coordinate j, write its truth table as a disjunction of minterms, one minterm for every x∈{0,1}^S on which the required output bit is 1, assigning arbitrary outputs on unused codes. Each minterm is a conjunction of S literals and costs at most S−1 binary AND gates after input negations are shared. The OR of at most 2^S minterms costs at most 2^S−1 binary OR gates, with OR implemented by De Morgan using AND and NOT. Thus each output bit costs O(S·2^S), and all S outputs cost O(S^2·2^S), not O(S·2^S). Consequently the valid bound proved here is O(S^2·2^S)=O(m(log m)^2), which repairs the false additive-displacement claim with a general exact upper bound.

structure.evidence: The minterm construction is exact on every encoded state and defines arbitrary values elsewhere. There are S output bits, each with at most 2^S minterms, each using O(S) literals and O(2^S) OR gates, giving O(S^2·2^S) total. Since 2^S<2m and S=ceil(log2 m), this is O(m(log m)^2).

statement: TRIE-SHARED TRANSITION EXTENSION LEMMA. Let Q have m>=2 states, let S=ceil(log2 m), let ψ:Q→{0,1}^S be injective, and let δ:Q→Q change exactly t states. Let T be the set of their S-bit encodings. Form the binary prefix trie of T, with the root omitted and unary and branching prefix nodes counted; let L be its number of nodes. Put H=Σ_{q:δ(q)≠q} d_H(ψ(q),ψ(δ(q))). Then the encoded partial map has a total Boolean extension using O(S+L+H) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: Share the negations of the S input bits. For each trie node, compute its prefix-match indicator from its parent indicator and the next matching literal, using one AND gate; the root indicator is 1. Each changed state q has a leaf indicator e_q, equal to 1 exactly at ψ(q), because ψ is injective and the leaves are distinct. For each output bit j, collect the leaves q for which ψ(q)_j differs from ψ(δ(q))_j. Define output j as x_j XOR the OR of their indicators (empty OR is 0). The ORs and XORs use O(1) gates per leaf occurrence, for O(H) total; the trie uses O(L) gates. At an unchanged encoded state no changed leaf indicator is active, so the output is ψ(q). At a changed encoded state exactly its leaf indicator is active, so precisely the differing destination bits are toggled. The formulas define outputs on every unused code, giving a total extension. Thus the cost is O(S+L+H). For a full trie L can be Θ(St), so this does not establish O(S+H) in general; it isolates the remaining obstacle as bounding shared prefix complexity for a useful encoding.

statement: statement: CONSTANT-IMAGE TRANSITION LEMMA. Let Q be a finite set, ψ:Q→{0,1}^S any injection, and δ:Q→Q have image of size one, say δ(q)=q_* for every q∈Q. Then ψ∘δ∘ψ^{-1} on ψ(Q) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map computed with zero fan-in-two AND/NOT gates (constants are free). Proof: Define F(x)=ψ(q_*) for every x∈{0,1}^S. Each of its S output coordinates is the corresponding constant bit of ψ(q_*), hence needs no gates under the stipulated free-constants convention. For every q∈Q, F(ψ(q))=ψ(q_*)=ψ(δ(q)), so F is the required extension. This holds for every stationary injective encoding and all S, including S=0. The result isolates the constant-map boundary case; it gives no bound for image size at least two.

label: S0681
statement: statement: ONE-HOT UNIVERSAL TRANSITION UPPER BOUND. For every m>=1, every map delta:Q->{0,1}^Q on an m-element set has an injective encoding psi:Q->{0,1}^m such that the encoded transition extends to a total map on {0,1}^m computed by at most m^2+m fan-in-two AND/NOT gates (input wires and constants are free). Proof: Enumerate Q={q_1,...,q_m} and encode q_i by the unit vector e_i. For each output coordinate j, let P_j={i: delta(q_i)=q_j}, and define F_j(x)=OR_{i in P_j} x_i, with the empty OR equal to 0. Implement each OR as a binary tree of OR gates; OR(a,b)=NOT(AND(NOT a,NOT b)), costing three allowed gates per internal node. The total number of internal nodes over all j is sum_j max(|P_j|-1,0) <= sum_j |P_j|=m, so this implementation uses at most 3m gates, which is <=m^2+m for m>=1. At x=e_i, exactly one input indicator is 1, hence F(e_i)=e_k where q_k=delta(q_i). Thus F is a total extension and the encoding is injective. Diagnostic: the construction uses m state bits, not S=ceil(log2 m), and gives no lower bound or P-vs-NP implication.

statement: statement: IMAGE-SENSITIVE ONE-HOT TRANSITION UPPER BOUND. Let m>=1, let Q be an m-element set and delta:Q->Q, and let r=|delta(Q)|. Under the encoding psi(q_i)=e_i in {0,1}^m, the encoded transition has a total Boolean extension using at most 3(m-r) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with input wires and constants free. Proof: For each q_j in delta(Q), put k_j=|delta^{-1}(q_j)|>=1 and define output bit j to be OR_{i:delta(q_i)=q_j} x_i; for q_j outside delta(Q), use constant zero. An OR of k_j inputs uses k_j-1 binary OR gates, each implemented using three AND/NOT gates. Since the nonempty preimages partition Q, sum_{j in delta(Q)} k_j=m, so total gates are 3 sum_j(k_j-1)=3(m-r). On input e_i exactly one input bit is one, and the output is e_j for q_j=delta(q_i), proving extension correctness. This uses m state bits and does not assert a minimum-width or lower-bound result.

statement: statement: Explicit minterm extension for arbitrary encoded transitions. Let m>=1, S=ceil(log2 m), Q be an m-element set, delta:Q->Q any function, and psi:Q->{0,1}^S injective. There exists a total Boolean map F:{0,1}^S->{0,1}^S agreeing with psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q), computed with O(mS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with input wires and constants free. For each q in Q, form e_q(x) as the conjunction of the S literals specifying x=psi(q), using S-1 binary AND gates when S>=1; share this indicator across all output coordinates. For each coordinate j, set F_j(x)=OR_{q: psi(delta(q))_j=1} e_q(x); a binary OR is implemented from AND/NOT by De Morgan, and the OR uses at most m-1 gates. At x=psi(q), injectivity gives e_q=1 and every other e_r=0, hence F_j(psi(q))=psi(delta(q))_j. The formulas define F on unused codes, whose values are unrestricted. The total gate count is at most m(S-1)+S(m-1)=O(mS). If S=0 then m=1 and the unique output is the zero-bit map, requiring no gates.

label: S0686
statement: statement: GENERIC TOTAL-EXTENSION SYNTHESIS LEMMA. Let Q be an m-element set, m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), let psi:Q->{0,1}^S be any injection, and let delta:Q->Q be any function. There is a total Boolean map F:{0,1}^S->{0,1}^S extending psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q), computed with O(mS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates (input wires and constants free). Proof: For each q in Q form the minterm e_q(x)=AND_{i=1}^S l_{q,i}(x), where l_{q,i}=x_i if psi(q)_i=1 and NOT x_i otherwise. Compute all input negations once and all minterms with at most S-1 binary AND gates each, for O(mS) gates. For output coordinate j, set T_j={q: psi(delta(q))_j=1} and define F_j=OR_{q in T_j} e_q, using at most max(|T_j|-1,0) binary OR gates, each implementable with a constant number of AND/NOT gates. Summed over j this costs O(mS). On input psi(q), injectivity makes exactly e_q equal 1, so F_j(psi(q))=psi(delta(q))_j. The formulas define F on unused codes as well. This gives an explicit upper bound for every injection and transition, but does not establish the sharper O(sqrt(m) polylog m) bound for a choice of encoding.

label: S0687
statement: statement: SPARSE-CHANGES EXTENSION LEMMA. Let |Q|=m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), and let psi:Q->{0,1}^S be injective. If delta:Q->Q fixes all but t states, then psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total Boolean map using O((t+1)S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with input wires and constants free. Proof: Let A={q:delta(q)!=q}. For each q in A, construct e_q(x)=[x=psi(q)] by ANDing its S matching literals, sharing input negations. This costs O(S|A|). For bit j, let D_j={q in A: psi(q)_j!=psi(delta(q))_j}; define F_j(x)=x_j XOR OR_{q in D_j} e_q(x). Binary trees implement each OR, and OR and XOR each have constant-size AND/NOT implementations. Since sum_j |D_j|<=S|A|, the total cost is O(S(t+1)). At an encoded fixed state all indicators vanish, so F_j=x_j. At an encoded changed state, injectivity makes only its indicator active, so F toggles precisely the bits differing between source and destination. Thus F agrees with the transition on psi(Q), and its formulas define a total map on all bit strings. For t=0 use the identity map. This improves the generic O(mS) synthesis bound when t=o(m), but does not establish the worst-case recoding bounds.

statement: statement: INTERVAL ENCODING FOR A c-CYCLE PERMUTATION. For every m>=2 and permutation delta on an m-element set with c cycles, there is an injection psi into {0,1}^S, S=ceil(log2 m), such that psi delta psi^{-1} extends to a total Boolean map computed by O(cS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: Order the cycles and list each cycle consecutively. Let cycle i occupy [a_i,b_i] in the integer codes 0,...,m-1, with successor x+1 except b_i maps to a_i. Build an S-bit incrementer u(x) at cost O(S). For each endpoint b_i compute e_i(x)=[x=b_i] by an S-literal conjunction, total O(cS). For every output bit j, correct u_j at endpoint b_i to constant (a_i)_j by XORing e_i AND (u_j XOR (a_i)_j); each endpoint-bit correction costs O(1), hence O(cS) total. The endpoint indicators are mutually exclusive. On non-endpoint codes all corrections vanish and output is x+1; at b_i the correction sets the output to a_i. This agrees with delta on every valid code. Define the circuit arbitrarily by the same formula on unused codes; it is a total extension. Thus the encoding and extension have the stated gate bound.

statement: statement: Cycle-interval encoding lemma. For every m>=2, every permutation delta of an m-element set Q having k cycles admits an injective encoding psi:Q->{0,1}^S, S=ceil(log2 m), such that the encoded transition psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total Boolean map computed by O(kS) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: List the cycles in any order with lengths l_1,...,l_k and let a_1=0, a_i=sum_{h<i} l_h. In cycle i, enumerate states q_{i,0},...,q_{i,l_i-1} in transition order and encode q_{i,j} by the S-bit binary representation of a_i+j. These are distinct integers in [0,m), so psi is injective. Define a circuit on all S-bit inputs x as follows. For each i form the interval indicator I_i(x)=[a_i<=x<a_i+l_i], using two constant-threshold comparisons; each comparison has an O(S)-gate fan-in-two AND/NOT implementation by scanning bits from most significant to least significant and maintaining equal-prefix and already-less flags. Let b_i=a_i+l_i-1. On the interval I_i, the desired output is a_i when x=b_i and x+1 otherwise. Compute the equality flag E_i=[x=b_i] with O(S) literals and AND gates, and compute x+1 modulo 2^S with an O(S)-gate ripple incrementer. For each output bit r, form the selected bit I_i AND ((E_i AND bit_r(a_i)) OR ((NOT E_i) AND bit_r(x+1))). OR, AND, and NOT have constant-size fan-in-two implementations. OR the k selected terms for each output bit. The total cost is O(kS), including all interval tests, endpoint tests, increment logic and output selection. For x outside the union of the intervals, define every output bit to be zero; this is achieved by the same formula, since every I_i is false. For x=a_i+j with j<l_i-1 the formula outputs a_i+j+1; for x=b_i it outputs a_i. Thus it agrees with delta on every encoded state. statement: statement: Explicit sparse-change extension bound. Let Q have m≥2 elements, S=ceil(log2 m), and ψ:Q→{0,1}^S be injective. statement: statement: Cycle-interval encoding lemma. For every code x in that interval except b, the transition is x↦x+1. At each of the c interval endpoints b, the desired output is the interval’s start a. On all S-bit strings use the shared binary increment modulo 2^S as a base map. For each endpoint code b, form the equality indicator e_b(x)=[x=b] using S literals. At a valid non-endpoint code the correction indicators vanish and increment gives the correct successor. At an endpoint exactly its own indicator is active, changing the base output to the required cycle start. statement: CYCLE-INTERVAL UPPER-BOUND LEMMA. Let Q be a finite set of size m>=2, let F:Q->Q be a permutation with c cycles, and put S=ceil(log_2 m).
