Proof: If q is outside ⋃_i supp(δ_i), every δ_i fixes q. Inductively, after each successive map the state is still q, so the composite fixes q. This proves the support inclusion and bounds the composite support by Σ_i t_i. Apply the sparse-transition construction: for each moved state u of the composite, form its encoding equality indicator [x=ψ(u)] using O(S) gates, and for each output bit XOR the OR of indicators for moved states whose destination bit differs from their source bit. Shared input negations and fan-in-two implementations give O(S(1+t)) gates for t moved states; injectivity ensures exactly the intended indicator is active at each valid moved code, while unchanged codes activate none. The formula defines a total map on all bit strings and agrees with the composite on ψ(Q). Since t≤Σ_i t_i, the asserted bound follows. label: S0703
statement: statement: PERIODIC TIME-VARYING RECODING LEMMA. Let Q be a finite set, let δ:Q→Q be a permutation of finite order L, and let ψ:Q→{0,1}^S be any injection. For each integer t define ψ_t=ψ∘δ^{-t}, with t interpreted modulo L. Then for every q∈Q, ψ_{t+1}(δ(q))=ψ_t(q). Thus each transition from time t to t+1 is the identity on valid encoded states and has a zero-gate implementation; the encoding schedule is periodic with period L. Proof: ψ_{t+1}(δ(q))=ψ(δ^{-(t+1)}(δ(q)))=ψ(δ^{-t}(q))=ψ_t(q). Since δ^L is the identity, ψ_{t+L}=ψ_t. This lemma concerns the transition between changing codebooks; it does not bound the cost of maintaining or synchronizing the time-dependent decoder.

label: S0704
statement: statement: FIXED-DECODER ZERO-UPDATE OBSTRUCTION. Let Q be a set, δ:Q→Q a map, C a code set, and D:C→Q a fixed decoder. Suppose encodings ψ_t:Q→C satisfy D(ψ_t(q))=q for every t,q, and updates preserve code words: ψ_{t+1}(δ(q))=ψ_t(q). Then δ is the identity. Proof: Apply D to the update equality. Correct decoding at time t+1 gives D(ψ_{t+1}(δ(q)))=δ(q); at time t it gives D(ψ_t(q))=q. The code words are equal, so their decoder outputs are equal, and δ(q)=q. Therefore any nonidentity transition with zero code-word updates requires changing the decoder.

statement: statement: PHASE-DECODER DISTINCTNESS FOR A CYCLE. Let Q={q_0,...,q_{m-1}} with m>=2 and δ(q_j)=q_{j+1 mod m}. Consequently, if the decoder is determined by a phase state z_t through one fixed map H, so D_t=H(z_t), then there are at least m distinct phase states and any binary representation of them needs at least ceil(log2 m) bits. Proof: If D_a=D_b, evaluate both at ψ(q_0): q_a=D_a(ψ(q_0))=D_b(ψ(q_0))=q_b. The cycle states are distinct, so a=b modulo m. Thus the decoders are pairwise distinct. If z_a=z_b, then H(z_a)=H(z_b), hence D_a=D_b and a=b; therefore the phase states are pairwise distinct. B bits encode at most 2^B states, so 2^B>=m and B>=ceil(log2 m).

label: S0706
statement: statement: BOUNDED-SUPPORT EXTENSION WITH EMPTY-SUPPORT BOUNDARY. Let m>=2, S=ceil(log_2 m), Q be an m-element set, psi:Q->{0,1}^S be any injection, and delta:Q->Q. If supp(delta)={q:delta(q)!=q} has size t, then the partial map psi(q)->psi(delta(q)) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map with O(S(1+t)) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. If t=0 the extension is the identity and uses zero gates. Proof: For every q in supp(delta), let e_q(x) be the conjunction of the S literals specifying psi(q), using shared input negations; all these indicators cost O(St). For each output coordinate j define F_j(x)=x_j XOR OR_{q in D_j} e_q(x), where D_j={q in supp(delta): psi(q)_j != psi(delta(q))_j}. A conjunction and each OR can be built with fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, and XOR has a constant-size AND/NOT implementation. Sharing all e_q gives total cost O(St+S+sum_j |D_j|)=O(S(1+t)); when t=0 each D_j is empty and F_j=x_j, so no gates are needed. On an encoded unchanged state, every e_q is zero. On an encoded changed state, injectivity ensures exactly its own e_q is one, so each coordinate toggles precisely when source and destination bits differ. Thus F(psi(q))=psi(delta(q)) for every q; values on unused codes are unrestricted. This is a constructive stationary upper bound only, not a representation-independent lower bound.

statement: TRIE-SHARED SPARSE TRANSITION EXTENSION. Let Q have m>=1 elements, S=ceil(log2 m), psi:Q->{0,1}^S be injective, and D={q:delta(q)!=q}, with |D|=t. Let T be the number of non-root nodes in the binary prefix trie of {psi(q):q in D}, and D_j={q in D:psi(q)_j!=psi(delta(q))_j}. A total extension of the encoded transition has a fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit of size O(S+T+sum_j max(0,|D_j|-1)). Proof: Compute each equality indicator [x=psi(q)] by extending shared prefix conjunctions in the trie, costing O(T) gates and O(S) shared input negations. For each j, OR the indicators for q in D_j, using max(0,|D_j|-1) gates, with empty OR equal to 0. Output bit j as x_j XOR that OR, using constant-size AND/NOT circuits. At unchanged encoded states all indicators vanish. At changed encoded state psi(q), injectivity makes exactly its indicator true, so precisely the differing coordinates toggle and the output is psi(delta(q)). The formulas define outputs on all other strings, hence give a total extension. If D is empty the identity uses only wires.
proof: As stated: shared prefix tests identify changed encoded states; each output coordinate toggles exactly when its active changed-state indicator belongs to D_j. The gate count is the sum of trie extensions, coordinate OR trees, and constant-size XOR circuits.

statement: HAMMING-SENSITIVE SPARSE TRANSITION EXTENSION. Let Q be a finite set of size m>=1, S=ceil(log2 m), psi:Q->{0,1}^S injective, and delta:Q->Q. A total extension of the encoded transition is computable by fan-in-two AND/NOT gates using O(S+T+H) gates. Proof: For each trie node, compute the conjunction testing its prefix by extending its parent conjunction with the next matching input literal; share input negations. This uses O(T+S) gates and yields each equality indicator e_q(x)=[x=psi(q)] at its leaf. For each output coordinate j, OR the indicators e_q for q in D_j, using max(0,|D_j|-1) binary OR gates, and use constant 0 if D_j is empty. Thus the output is psi(delta(q)); the formulas define a total map on all strings. Finally, sum_j |D_j|=H by counting each changed state once for every differing coordinate. statement:
statement: PREFIX-TRIE BOUND. Let A be a set of t distinct binary strings of length S, and let T(A) be the number of non-root nodes in their prefix trie. Then T(A) <= sum_{d=1}^S min(t,2^d). For t>=1, this is at most t(S-floor(log2 t))+2t-2. For t=0, T(A)=0. Proof: At depth d, trie nodes correspond to distinct length-d prefixes of strings in A. There are at most t such prefixes and at most 2^d binary strings of length d, so that level has at most min(t,2^d) nodes. Summing over depths proves the first inequality. For t>=1 let k=floor(log2 t). The sum through depth k is 2^(k+1)-2 <= 2t-2; the remaining S-k levels contribute at most t each. This proves the second bound. The statement concerns trie size only and does not assume or prove a circuit lower bound.
proof: At each depth d, every trie node is a prefix of at least one member of A, giving at most t nodes, and there are only 2^d possible prefixes, giving at most 2^d nodes. Add these bounds level by level. For the explicit estimate, depths 1 through k contribute at most sum 2^d=2^(k+1)-2 <= 2t-2, while depths k+1 through S contribute at most t per level, for t(S-k). The empty set has no trie nodes.

statement: CYCLE-CONCATENATION TRANSITION UPPER BOUND. Let Q be an m-element set, m>=2, and let δ be a permutation of Q with c cycles. Put S=ceil(log2 m). There is an injection ψ:Q→{0,1}^S such that the transition ψδψ^{-1}, defined on ψ(Q), extends to a total S-bit Boolean map computed by O(S(c+1)) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: Order the cycles arbitrarily and concatenate their cyclic orderings into a list q_0,...,q_{m-1}; encode q_i by the S-bit binary representation of i. Let b_i be the index of δ(q_i). For every i that is not the last index of its cycle, b_i=i+1, so ordinary binary increment agrees with the required transition. Let E be the set of cycle-end indices; |E|=c. Build a total increment-modulo-2^S map I on S bits: each carry into bit j is the conjunction of the lower j bits (with the empty conjunction equal to 1), and output bit j is x_j XOR that carry. Shared prefix conjunctions and constant-size AND/NOT implementations of XOR give O(S) gates. For each i∈E, compute e_i(x)=[x=i] by an S-literal conjunction. For output bit j, set F_j(x)=I_j(x) XOR OR_{i∈E : (i+1 mod 2^S)_j != b_i,j} e_i(x). OR trees use O(c) gates per bit, so all corrections use O(Sc) gates; equality tests use O(Sc) gates as well. At a valid non-end code i the correction is zero and I(i)=i+1=b_i. At a valid end code i, injectivity makes exactly e_i active, toggling precisely the bits where I(i) differs from b_i; hence F(i)=b_i. The formulas define F on unused codes too, giving a total extension. Therefore the circuit size is O(S(c+1)). The finite verification cm-fc5355a099b84193 checked the cycle-concatenation identity on 362,879 transitions through m=8; it is sanity evidence only, while the argument above proves the stated bound.

For every m>=2 and every permutation delta on an m-element set Q with exactly d distinct cycle lengths l_1,...,l_d, there is an injective encoding psi:Q->{0,1}^S, S=ceil(log2 m), such that psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total Boolean map computed by O(d log m + log m * sum_{i=1}^d log(l_i+1)) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. These codes partition 0,...,m-1, hence their S-bit binary encodings are injective. On each such cycle delta sends x to x+1 unless j=l_i-1, in which case it sends x to x-l_i+1. For each i make an interval indicator I_i(x) for A_i<=x<A_i+c_i*l_i; binary comparison to constants costs O(log m) fan-in-two gates. Within that interval the boundary indicator is E_i(x)=[(x-A_i+1) mod l_i=0]. statement: INTERVAL-ENCODING LEMMA. Let Q be an m-element set, m>=2, and let delta be a permutation of Q with d cycles. Put S=ceil(log2 m). There is an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that the transition on psi(Q) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map of fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit size O((d+1)S). Proof: List the cycles in any order, with lengths ell_1,...,ell_d, and let a_i=sum_{h<i} ell_h. Enumerate cycle i as q_{i,0},...,q_{i,ell_i-1}, and encode q_{i,j} by the S-bit binary representation of a_i+j. These are distinct codes in [0,m-1], so psi is injective. Let B(x)=x+1 mod 2^S, computed by a shared ripple incrementer using O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates: the carry into bit j is the conjunction of lower bits, and XOR has a constant-size AND/NOT implementation. For each cycle endpoint e_i=a_i+ell_i-1, compute the indicator E_i(x)=[x=e_i] using an S-literal conjunction, costing O(S). On endpoint e_i, the base output B(e_i) must be changed to a_i. For each output bit r define F_r(x)=B_r(x) XOR OR_{i: B(e_i)_r differs from (a_i)_r} E_i(x). The endpoint indicators are mutually exclusive because the e_i are distinct; OR and XOR each have constant-size fan-in-two AND/NOT implementations per operation. Thus all endpoint tests and corrections cost O(dS), and the total circuit costs O((d+1)S). At a non-endpoint encoded state a_i+j with j<ell_i-1, no E_i is active and B outputs a_i+j+1, the next cycle state. At endpoint e_i exactly E_i is active and the correction changes B(e_i) to a_i, the cycle successor. This includes e_i=m-1, whether or not m is a power of two, since B is explicitly modulo 2^S. The formulas define outputs on every S-bit input, giving a total extension. This proves only an upper bound depending on the number of cycles; it does not establish a uniform O(sqrt(m) polylog(m)) bound for arbitrary permutations.

statement: CANDIDATE REPAIR — grouped-length interval encoding. Let a permutation on m states have d distinct cycle lengths. Set S=ceil(log2 m), order the cycles by length, and assign each cycle of length ℓ its own consecutive interval of ℓ integers, with all cycles of the same length in one contiguous block beginning at a. On a valid code x in that block, the transition is x+1 unless (x-a+1) mod ℓ=0, in which case it is x+1−ℓ. Proof: write x=a+uℓ+r with 0≤r<ℓ and u the cycle index in the block. If r<ℓ−1 then x+1=a+uℓ+(r+1), the next state in that cycle. If r=ℓ−1 then x+1−ℓ=a+uℓ, the first state of that same cycle. The endpoint predicate is equivalent to r=ℓ−1. This proves the transition identity on every encoded state. This claim is only the arithmetic transition identity; it does not assert a circuit-size bound.

statement: Universal extension upper bound for a fixed encoding. Let m≥2, S=ceil(log2 m), Q be an m-element set, ψ:Q→{0,1}^S be any injection, and δ:Q→Q be any map. Then ψ∘δ∘ψ⁻¹ on ψ(Q) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map with at most S + m(S−1) + 3S(m−1) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with constants and wires free. Proof: For each q∈Q, form e_q(x)=[x=ψ(q)] by ANDing its S matching literals using S−1 gates; share the S negated input bits. For output bit j, let I_j={q∈Q : ψ(δ(q))_j=1}. Define F_j(x)=OR_{q∈I_j} e_q(x), taking an empty OR as 0. A binary OR is implemented as NOT(AND(NOT a,NOT b)), at most three gates, so all output ORs use at most 3S(m−1) gates. On any encoded input ψ(q), injectivity makes e_q=1 and all other indicators 0; hence F_j(ψ(q))=ψ(δ(q))_j. On unused inputs every indicator is 0, so the circuit is a total extension (with output 0 there). Thus the stated gate count holds and is O(m log m). This is an upper bound for a fixed encoding and arbitrary transition; it gives no lower bound over encodings.

statement: statement: EVEN INVOLUTION ONE-GATE RECODING LEMMA. For every even m=2p>=2 and every fixed-point-free involution delta on an m-element set Q, with S=ceil(log2 m), there exists an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that psi delta psi^{-1} extends to a total S-bit Boolean map using at most one NOT gate (input wires and constants free). Proof: Partition Q into its p unordered delta-pairs and enumerate the pairs by i=0,...,p-1. Let k=ceil(log2 p). Since p<=m/2, k+1<=ceil(log2 m)=S. Encode the two members of pair i as the S-bit words 0^{S-k-1} bin_k(i) 0 and 0^{S-k-1} bin_k(i) 1, where bin_k is the k-bit binary encoding (for p=1, k=0 and the empty index field is omitted). These 2p words are distinct, so psi is injective. Define the total Boolean map F on all S-bit strings by copying every bit except the final tag bit, which it negates. F uses one NOT gate and satisfies F(psi(q))=psi(delta(q)) for each q, because delta swaps the two members of each pair while preserving its index. This includes p=1 and arbitrary even m, including non-powers of two; unused strings require no special behavior.

statement: ENDPOINT-CORRECTION CIRCUIT LEMMA. Let δ be a permutation of an m-element set Q, m≥2, with d distinct cycle lengths, and set S=⌈log₂m⌉. There is an injection ψ:Q→{0,1}^S for which ψδψ⁻¹ on ψ(Q) extends to a total Boolean map using O((d+1)S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: List the cycles in any order and each cycle in its δ-order, assigning consecutive integer codes from 0. Each cycle occupies an interval [a,e], and δ acts as x↦x+1 except at its endpoint e, where the desired output is a. The codes 0,…,m−1 fit in S bits. Compute the ordinary S-bit modular increment B(x)=x+1 with O(S) gates: the carry into bit j is the conjunction of input bits 0,…,j−1 (the empty conjunction is 1), and XOR has a constant-size AND/NOT implementation. For each of the at most d cycle endpoints e, compute I_e(x)=[x=e] as a conjunction of S literals, sharing input negations, at cost O(S) gates per endpoint. For each output bit j, XOR B_j with all indicators I_e for which bit j of (e+1 mod 2^S) differs from bit j of the start a_e of e's cycle. On a valid non-endpoint code, every indicator is zero, so the output is its successor. On a valid endpoint e, exactly I_e is one, so exactly the differing bits are toggled and the output equals a_e. This defines a total map on all S-bit inputs and has O(S+dS) gates (the dS output-bit corrections and the dS equality tests dominate). If the distinct positive cycle lengths are l_1<⋯<l_d, then l_i≥i and each length occurs at least once, so m≥∑l_i≥d(d+1)/2. Hence d≤⌊(√(8m+1)−1)/2⌋, and the gate bound is O(√m log m).

statement: statement: COMMON-ARBITRARY-CYCLE-LENGTH LEMMA. Let m=t*l with integers t>=1 and l>=1, and let F be a permutation of an m-element set Q whose cycles all have length l. Set S=ceil(log2 m). There is an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that psi F psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total Boolean map on S bits of fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit size O((log m)^2). Proof: Index the cycles by i in {0,...,t-1} and positions by j in {0,...,l-1}, so F(i,j)=(i,(j+1) mod l). Encode (i,j) by the S-bit binary representation of x=i*l+j, which is injective since 0<=x<m<=2^S. On valid x, let r=x mod l and define y=x+1 if r<l-1, and y=x-(l-1) if r=l-1. If r<l-1, x=i*l+r, hence y=i*l+(r+1), the encoding of F(i,r). If r=l-1, x=i*l+l-1, hence y=x-(l-1)=i*l, the encoding of F(i,l-1). Thus y is always in [0,m) and the map agrees with F on every encoded state. To realize a total Boolean extension, compute r by a bit-serial remainder circuit: process the S input bits from most significant to least; at each step replace the current remainder u by (2u+b) mod l. Since 0<=u<l, this uses O(log l) gates per bit using compare/subtract circuitry, for O(S log l) gates. Compute the two candidate arithmetic expressions x+1 and x-(l-1) with ripple carry/borrow circuits of O(S) gates each, compare r with l-1 in O(log l) gates, and select the appropriate S output bits with O(S) mux gates. Total size O(S log l+S)=O((log m)^2). Define this same circuit on all S-bit inputs; behavior outside psi(Q) is arbitrary. The l=1 case is the identity and has an O(S) extension. This gives a constructive arbitrary-common-cycle-length extension of the power-of-two-cycle subclass, at exact width S.

statement: statement: BOUNDED-DISTINCT-CYCLE-LENGTH ENCODING LEMMA. For every m>=2 and permutation F on m states whose cycles have r distinct lengths, there is an injection into {0,1}^S, S=ceil(log2 m), such that the encoded transition extends to a total fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit of size O(r*S*log m). Proof: For each cycle length ell, group its c_ell cycles in a consecutive interval of length c_ell*ell, with offset B_ell equal to the total size of shorter-length groups. Index cycles i and positions j, and encode as x=B_ell+i*ell+j. The intervals partition [0,m), so this is injective. On the interval for ell, compute q=(x-B_ell) mod ell. Output x+1 if q<ell-1 and x-(ell-1) otherwise. For x=B_ell+i*ell+j, these outputs encode (i,j+1) modulo ell, so they equal F. A remainder circuit scans the S input bits, updating u to (2u+b) mod ell; because u<ell implies 2u+b<2ell, each update uses O(log ell) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, for O(S log ell) per group. Interval tests, subtraction, comparison, addition/subtraction candidates, and output selection use O(S) gates per group. Multiplexing across r groups yields O(r*S*log m). Assign arbitrary outputs outside [0,m) to make a total extension. This bound is useful for fixed r and leaves growing r unresolved.

statement: statement: Support-sensitive recoding lemma. Let Q have m states, S>=1, psi:Q->{0,1}^S be injective, and delta:Q->Q differ from the identity on exactly t states. There is a total S-bit fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit F, with constants and input wires free, using O(tS) gates, such that F(psi(q))=psi(delta(q)) for every q in Q. Proof: Use the identity map x as a zero-gate baseline. For each moved state q construct e_q(x)=[x=psi(q)] as the conjunction of S matching literals, using O(S) gates per q and shared input negations. For each output bit j let E_j be the moved states q for which psi(q)_j differs from psi(delta(q))_j. Set F_j(x)=x_j XOR OR_{q in E_j} e_q(x). Fan-in-two AND/NOT gates implement each OR and XOR with O(|E_j|+1) gates when E_j is nonempty; when E_j is empty use the wire x_j. Across coordinates, sum_j |E_j|<=tS, and the nonempty-coordinate overhead is at most S; for t>0 this is O(tS). For t=0 use the identity wires alone. On a valid code exactly its own equality indicator is true if it is moved, so precisely the required output bits toggle; on unmoved codes all indicators vanish. The formulas define a total circuit off the code set as well.

statement: statement: Sparse correction under a fixed injective encoding: Let Q be finite, psi:Q->{0,1}^S injective, and beta,delta:Q->Q differ on E={q:beta(q)!=delta(q)}. If a total fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit F0 computes psi∘beta∘psi^{-1} on psi(Q), then a circuit computes psi∘delta∘psi^{-1} on psi(Q) with at most size(F0)+O(S|E|+sum_{q in E} d_H(psi(beta(q)),psi(delta(q)))) gates. Proof: for each q in E, form e_q(x)=[x=psi(q)] using O(S) AND/NOT gates. The e_q are mutually exclusive on psi(Q). For output bit j, let E_j be those q in E on which the baseline and target outputs differ in bit j, and define F_j=F0_j XOR OR_{q in E_j} e_q. Fan-in-two AND/NOT circuits implement each OR and XOR with constant gates per term. The equality tests cost O(S|E|), and the output corrections cost O(sum_j |E_j|), which equals O(sum_{q in E} d_H(psi(beta(q)),psi(delta(q)))). At psi(q), exactly e_q is true for q in E, so precisely the differing coordinates are toggled; outside E all correction indicators vanish. Hence F has the required values on every encoded state.

statement: statement: Adjacent-pair encoding for involutions. For every m>=2 and every involution δ on an m-element set Q, put S=ceil(log2 m). There is an injection ψ:Q→{0,1}^S and a total S-bit fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit F of O(S) gates such that F(ψ(q))=ψ(δ(q)) for all q∈Q. Proof: Decompose δ into p transposition pairs and f fixed points, so 2p+f=m. Enumerate pairs (a_i,b_i), i=0,...,p−1, and fixed points c_j, j=0,...,f−1. Set ψ(a_i)=binary(2i), ψ(b_i)=binary(2i+1), and ψ(c_j)=binary(2p+j), using S-bit representations; these codes are distinct and valid because their integer values lie in [0,m−1] and m≤2^S. Define F on every S-bit input x to toggle the least significant bit iff x<2p, and otherwise leave x unchanged. A comparison against the fixed constant 2p and a conditional low-bit toggle use O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates; all other output bits are wires. Each paired code 2i,2i+1 is exchanged by the toggle, and every fixed-point code is at least 2p and remains unchanged. Thus the circuit is correct on every encoded state and total on all inputs.

statement: Sparse-update-from-identity lemma. Let Q be a set of m states, S>=1, and psi:Q->{0,1}^S an injection. Let delta:Q->Q agree with the identity except on a set E of t states. There is a total S-output-bit fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit F with constants and input wires free, of size O(S+tS), such that F(psi(q))=psi(delta(q)) for every q in Q.
proof: For each q in E define e_q(x)=1 exactly when x=psi(q), implemented as the conjunction of the S literals specifying psi(q). The input-bit negations are shared, so all indicators cost O(S+tS). For each output bit j, let E_j={q in E: psi(delta(q))_j != psi(q)_j}. Set F_j(x)=x_j XOR (OR_{q in E_j} e_q(x)); an empty OR is 0. A binary OR and XOR are implementable with a constant number of AND/NOT gates per term (De Morgan for OR; XOR has a fixed constant-size AND/NOT implementation), so all output corrections cost O(sum_j |E_j|+S)=O(tS+S). On x=psi(q), injectivity implies e_q(x)=1 only for the corresponding state, and all other indicators are zero. If q is outside E no correction fires, hence F(x)=psi(q)=psi(delta(q)); if q is in E, precisely the coordinates differing between psi(q) and psi(delta(q)) are toggled. Thus the circuit has the required values on every encoded state. The formula defines a total Boolean map on all {0,1}^S, including unused codes.

statement: statement: LEMMA (fixed-point-free involutions). For every even m >= 2, every m-element set Q, and every fixed-point-free involution δ:Q→Q, there is an injective stationary encoding ψ:Q→{0,1}^{ceil(log2 m)} such that the encoded transition extends to a total Boolean map computable with one NOT gate and wires. Proof: Put r=m/2 and list the two-element orbits of δ as P_0,...,P_{r-1}. Choose one representative q_i from each orbit and assign each orbit a distinct index u_i in {0,1}^{ceil(log2 r)}. Define ψ(q_i)=(u_i,0) and ψ(δ(q_i))=(u_i,1). These codes are distinct. Also ceil(log2 r)+1=ceil(log2(2r))=ceil(log2 m), so they have the required length. Define T(u,b)=(u,¬b) on every bit string of that length, including unused codes. Then T(ψ(q))=ψ(δ(q)) for each state q: on either member of each orbit, T preserves its index and flips its tag. T copies the index bits and negates the tag, so it uses one NOT gate plus wires.

statement: Common-cycle-length constructive bound. Let δ be a permutation on an m-element set, m≥2, all of whose cycles have one common length L (so L divides m), and set S=⌈log₂m⌉. There is an injective stationary encoding into {0,1}^S such that the encoded transition on valid codes extends to a total Boolean map computed by O(SL) fan-in-two gates.
proof: Write the cycles as C_0,...,C_{r−1}, each in successor order C_i=(q_{i,0},...,q_{i,L−1}), where r=m/L. Encode ψ(q_{i,t}) as the S-bit binary representation of iL+t. These m codes are distinct and lie in [0,m−1]. For valid code x=iL+t with t<L−1, the successor code is x+1; if t=L−1, it is x−(L−1)=iL. Define the total extension on every S-bit input x by F(x)=x−(L−1) when x mod L=L−1, and F(x)=x+1 modulo 2^S otherwise. This agrees with the desired transition on every valid code. To implement x mod L=L−1, scan its S bits from most significant to least significant, maintaining a one-hot remainder in {0,...,L−1}; each input bit updates remainder a to (2a+b) mod L. Each layer's L output indicators are computed from the preceding L indicators and the input bit with O(L) fan-in-two gates, for O(SL) total. Testing the final remainder costs O(L). Increment by one modulo 2^S and subtraction of the fixed constant L−1 modulo 2^S each have O(S) fan-in-two implementations; selecting the result bitwise costs O(S). statement: CYCLE-GROUPED SUCCESSOR RULE. Let delta be a permutation of a finite set Q. For each cycle length ell, place the cycles of that length consecutively in a block, with each cycle occupying ell consecutive integer codes. For a state with code x, block start a, and offset r=x-a, define its successor code to be x+1 if r mod ell != ell-1, and x-(ell-1) if r mod ell = ell-1. Then this rule sends every encoded state to the code of its delta-successor. Proof: In a cycle, offsets j<ell-1 are followed by offset j+1, whose code is x+1. The final offset ell-1 is followed by the first state of that cycle, whose code is x-(ell-1). Thus the rule is correct on every cycle. This proves only transition-table correctness; it makes no circuit-size claim. Diagnostic: not a P-vs-NP claim; relativizing/natural/algebrizing/localizing labels are not applicable to this finite combinatorial lemma.

statement: ONE-HOT PERMUTATION RECoding. For every finite set Q of size m and every permutation δ:Q→Q, there is an injective encoding ψ:Q→{0,1}^m such that the encoded transition ψ∘δ∘ψ⁻¹ on valid codewords is implemented by a permutation of the m input bits, using zero fan-in-2 gates when wire permutations are free (or O(m) gates if output copies are charged). Proof: Fix a bijection e:Q→{1,…,m} and encode q by the unit vector ψ(q) whose only 1 is at coordinate e(q). For each output coordinate j, set y_j=x_{e(δ⁻¹(e⁻¹(j)))}. If x=ψ(q), the selected input coordinate is e(q), so y has its sole 1 at coordinate e(δ(q)); hence y=ψ(δ(q)). The coordinate map is a permutation because δ is bijective. Thus the construction is exact on all encoded states; it makes no claim about extensions on invalid codewords or compact encodings.

statement: ONE-HOT FINITE-MAP UPDATE. Let Q be a finite set of size m and let δ:Q→Q be any map, not necessarily injective. Proof: The orbits of δ are p disjoint pairs. Assign each pair a distinct index i∈{0,…,p−1}, represented with k=ceil(log2 p) bits, and assign its two elements tags 0 and 1. Encode them as (i,b). This is injective and uses k+1=ceil(log2(2p)) bits. On every encoded state, δ changes (i,b) to (i,1−b). On all k+1-bit strings, define the extension to leave the index unchanged and negate the tag; this is a total Boolean map implemented by one NOT gate.

statement: statement: Let δ be a permutation of a finite set Q whose cycles all have the same length d=2^r, where r≥1, and let m=|Q|=p·2^r. statement: EQUAL-LENGTH CYCLE CONSTRUCTION. Let a permutation on m states consist of cycles all of the same length l, where l divides m, and let S=ceil(log2 m). There is an injective stationary encoding into S bits whose transition extends to a total fan-in-two Boolean map of O(S log(l+1)) gates. Proof: enumerate the m/l cycles and assign each cycle a consecutive block of l codes, so the used codes are 0,...,m-1. On a code x, the desired successor is x+1 except at a cycle endpoint. The endpoint test is [(x+1) mod l=0], because all block starts are multiples of l. The increment modulo 2^S costs O(S) gates. A left-to-right binary remainder computation modulo the constant l uses O(S log(l+1)) gates: maintain the remainder in ceil(log2 l) bits; for each input bit, double and add the bit, then conditionally subtract l, using O(log(l+1)) fan-in-two gates per bit. At an endpoint, x-(l-1) is the start of its cycle and is computed with O(S) gates; select this value at endpoints and the increment otherwise, bit by bit, at O(S) cost. Define the resulting formulas on all S-bit strings; unused strings may take either branch and the formulas are total. The total is O(S log(l+1)) gates. This construction is independent of the general cycle-grouping arguments.

statement: statement: PAIR-INDEX RECODING FOR FIXED-POINT-FREE INVOLUTIONS. Let Q be a set of size m=2p, and let δ:Q→Q be a fixed-point-free involution. There is an injective stationary encoding ψ:Q→{0,1}^S, S=ceil(log₂m), for which the encoded transition on ψ(Q) is implemented by one NOT gate. Proof: The orbits of δ partition Q into exactly p unordered pairs; choose and label them P_0,…,P_{p−1}. Choose a bijection h from these labels to {0,…,p−1}, represented in b=ceil(log₂p) bits (with b=0 if p=1). For each q∈P_i, encode ψ(q)=(h(i),τ(q)), where τ chooses distinct tags 0 and 1 for the two elements of P_i. This is injective because different pairs have different indices and the two elements within a pair have different tags. Since δ exchanges the elements of each pair, ψ(δ(q))=(h(i),1−τ(q)); thus the transition preserves the index and negates only the tag bit. It is implemented by one NOT gate, with the index output wires copied unchanged. Finally, S=ceil(log₂(2p))=ceil(log₂p)+1=b+1, so the encoding uses exactly the permitted number of bits. The construction applies to every fixed-point-free involution, with no uniformity or decoder-cost assertion.

statement: For every integer m≥1, let D(m) be the maximum number of distinct cycle lengths of a permutation on an m-element set. Then D(m) is the largest integer d≥1 with d(d+1)/2≤m. statement: statement: For integers ℓ≥1 and S≥1, the predicate x mod ℓ = ℓ−1 on S-bit inputs x∈{0,…,2^S−1} has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of O(Sℓ) gates. Proof: process the S bits of x from most significant to least significant while storing the current remainder r∈{0,…,ℓ−1} in one-hot form, with indicators z_j=[r=j]. On input bit b, the next remainder is (2r+b) mod ℓ. For each target j, its next indicator is the OR of terms z_i AND [b=ε] over pairs (i,ε) satisfying (2i+ε) mod ℓ=j. There are at most 2ℓ terms across all targets; implementing each conjunction and each OR with fan-in-two gates costs O(ℓ) gates per input bit. Initialize the one-hot state to r=0. After S updates, output the indicator for r=ℓ−1. Induction on the processed prefix proves that the stored remainder equals that prefix modulo ℓ, so the output is correct. The total gate count is O(Sℓ).

statement: Fixed-modulus remainder circuit lemma. For integers l>=2 and S>=1, there is a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with O(S ceil(log2 l)) gates that, on input x in {0,1}^S interpreted as an unsigned integer, outputs x mod l in binary. Consequently it tests x mod l = a for any fixed a in {0,...,l-1} within the same asymptotic gate bound.
proof: Process the bits of x from most significant to least significant. Maintain a binary register r for the remainder of the prefix processed so far, with invariant 0<=r<l. Initially r=0. On reading a bit b, form u=2r+b, so 0<=u<2l. The new remainder is u if u<l and u-l otherwise. The comparison u>=l against a fixed constant and the conditional subtraction of that constant are each computable by O(ceil(log2 l)) fan-in-two Boolean gates: a constant comparator is a chain of bitwise equality/ordering tests, subtraction by a fixed binary constant is a ripple borrow circuit, and muxing between u and u-l costs O(ceil(log2 l)) gates. Thus each input bit updates the register using O(ceil(log2 l)) gates, and after S updates the register equals x mod l by induction on the processed prefix. The invariant ensures the register width is ceil(log2 l); comparing the final register to fixed a costs O(log l) gates, absorbed in O(S ceil(log2 l)) for S>=1.

statement: CYCLE-BLOCK SUCCESSOR LEMMA. Let a cycle of length l>=1 occupy consecutive integer codes a,a+1,...,a+l-1. On its valid codes, the successor map is x+1 except at x=a+l-1, where it is a. Equivalently, for valid x in this block, successor(x)=x+1-l*[x=a+l-1]. Proof: If x<a+l-1, its next listed code is x+1. The last listed code is the cycle's final state, whose successor is the first state with code a. The indicator is zero in the first case and one in the second, giving the formula in both cases. Hence encoding disjoint cycles as consecutive blocks reduces the transition specification to identifying block endpoints; behavior on unused codes can be assigned arbitrarily. This is an exact structural reduction and makes no gate-complexity claim.

statement: statement: ENDPOINT-TO-SUCCESSOR REDUCTION. Let a cycle occupy the consecutive integer interval [a,a+l-1], with l>=1, and define E(x)=[x=a+l-1]. On codes in this interval, the successor map is x+1-lE(x). Thus, if a Boolean circuit computes E on the interval and has arithmetic addition/subtraction by the fixed constants l and 1 available as fan-in-two Boolean circuits, composing those circuits computes the correct successor on the interval; the behavior outside the interval may be arbitrary. Proof: For x<a+l-1 the endpoint indicator is zero, so the expression is x+1, the next code. For x=a+l-1 the indicator is one, so the expression is x+1-l=a, the first code in the cycle. These are all codes in the interval, including l=1, where the sole code is the endpoint and the expression returns a.

statement: statement: CYCLE-BLOCK ENDPOINT CIRCUIT. For any fixed S-bit code e, the predicate E_e(x)=[x=e] is computable by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with at most 3S+1 gates, using NOT, AND, and OR gates. Consequently, for a fixed cycle interval [a,a+l-1] contained in {0,1}^S, its endpoint predicate is computable within this bound. Proof: For each bit i, compute the literal x_i if e_i=1 and ¬x_i if e_i=0; this uses at most S NOT gates. The conjunction of the S literals uses S−1 binary AND gates when S≥1. The result is 1 exactly when every input bit agrees with e. Thus the total is at most 2S−1 gates, which is at most 3S+1. For S=0 the domain has one code and the predicate is constant, also within the bound. Composing this predicate with the cycle-block formula x+1−lE_e(x) gives the correct successor on the interval, with fixed-constant arithmetic implementable by standard ripple circuits using O(S) fan-in-two gates; hence this particular cycle transition has an O(S)-gate implementation on its valid codes. This is an upper-bound construction for one consecutively encoded cycle, not a bound for arbitrary permutations.

statement: Exceptional-input correction lemma: For S>=1 and any f:{0,1}^S->{0,1}^S differing from modular increment B(x)=x+1 mod 2^S at exactly r inputs, there is a fan-in-two Boolean circuit for f with O((r+1)S) gates. Set E_a(x)=[x=a], d_a=B(a) XOR f(a), and output F(x)=B(x) XOR OR_a(E_a(x) AND d_a), bitwise. This agrees with f on every input.
proof: Compute each equality indicator E_a with O(S) gates. For each output coordinate, form the OR of the r terms E_a AND d_a[j], then XOR it with B_j. Total gate count is O(S+rS), including an O(S)-gate increment circuit. Outside the exception set all indicators vanish, so F=B=f. At an exceptional input a, its indicator alone is 1, hence F(a)=B(a) XOR (B(a) XOR f(a))=f(a).

statement: statement: For every fixed-point-free involution δ on a set Q of even size m=2p, there is an injective stationary encoding ψ:Q→{0,1}^{ceil(log2 m)} such that the encoded transition on valid codes is implemented by one NOT gate and wires. Proof: Partition Q into its p unordered pairs {u_i,v_i}. Since 2^S≥m=2p, we have 2^{S-1}≥p (for S=ceil(log2(2p))). Choose distinct (S−1)-bit strings a_i for the pairs. Set ψ(u_i)=a_i||0 and ψ(v_i)=a_i||1. Then δ swaps the two members of each pair, so its encoded action preserves the first S−1 bits and complements the last bit. This uses one NOT gate; unused codes may be assigned arbitrary behavior. The encoding is injective because pair indices are distinct and the two tags differ.

statement: statement: PAIR-TAG ENCODING LEMMA. Let Q be a finite set with |Q|=m=2p≥2, and let δ:Q→Q be a fixed-point-free involution (δ(δ(q))=q and δ(q)≠q for every q∈Q). Set S=ceil(log2 m). There is an injective stationary map ψ:Q→{0,1}^S such that, for every q∈Q, ψ(δ(q)) is obtained from ψ(q) by complementing its last bit and leaving its first S−1 bits unchanged. Thus the induced transition on ψ(Q) is implemented by one NOT gate and wires; its action on unused codes is unrestricted. Proof: Because δ is a fixed-point-free involution, its orbits partition Q into exactly p disjoint sets of size two, say {u_i,v_i} for i=1,...,p. From S=ceil(log2(2p)) we have 2^S≥2p, hence 2^(S−1)≥p. Choose p distinct strings a_i∈{0,1}^{S−1}. Define ψ(u_i)=a_i||0 and ψ(v_i)=a_i||1. Different orbits have different a_i, and the two states in each orbit have different final bits, so ψ is injective. Since δ swaps u_i and v_i, the first S−1 bits are preserved and the final bit is complemented on every encoded state. A Boolean circuit consisting of wires on the first S−1 coordinates and one NOT gate on the last coordinate realizes this transition on ψ(Q).

statement: statement: CYCLE-CLASS UPDATE LEMMA. Let δ be a permutation of a set Q of size m≥2, let S=ceil(log2 m), and let r be the number of distinct cycle lengths of δ. There is an injective stationary encoding ψ:Q→{0,1}^S whose induced transition extends to a total Boolean map on {0,1}^S using O(r S^2) fan-in-two gates. Proof: For each distinct cycle length l, concatenate the codes of all δ-cycles of length l into a block of consecutive integers, with each cycle occupying l consecutive codes. Concatenate these blocks in any order and assign the resulting m integers to the corresponding states in successor order. These codes lie in {0,...,m−1}⊆{0,1}^S, so ψ is injective. Let B(x)=x+1 modulo 2^S. On a valid code x in a block for length l, B gives the successor except at a cycle endpoint. If the block starts at a, its endpoints satisfy x≥a and (x−a+1) mod l=0. For each length l, compute the block-membership predicate, the endpoint predicate using a bit-serial remainder computation, and the correction value x−(l−1). The membership and endpoint computations cost O(S log l) gates per length; the correction and selection cost O(S) per length. Apply the corresponding correction at endpoints and use B elsewhere. The endpoint predicates for distinct blocks are disjoint, so the corrections can be combined with O(rS) additional gates. The default incrementer costs O(S); summing gives O(r S log m + rS + S)=O(r S^2). Assign arbitrary outputs to invalid codes not covered by the construction; the described circuit already defines outputs there. Thus the bound holds for every permutation, with the stated dependence on its number r of distinct cycle lengths.

statement: LEMMA (cycle-length-block upper bound). Let \(\delta\) be any permutation of an \(m\)-element set, where \(m\ge2\), and let \(S=\lceil\log_2m\rceil\). There is an injective stationary encoding \(\psi:Q\to\{0,1\}^S\) such that the encoded transition \(\psi\delta\psi^{-1}\) on encoded states extends to a total Boolean map computed by \(O(\sqrt m\,S^2)\) fan-in-2 gates over a fixed complete basis. Proof: Decompose \(\delta\) into disjoint cycles. For each distinct cycle length \(l\), place all cycles of length \(l\) consecutively in a block, each cycle occupying an interval of \(l\) codes; assign states in successor order within each interval. The number \(d\) of distinct lengths satisfies \(d(d+1)/2\le m\), hence \(d\le\sqrt{2m}\). On a cycle interval, the successor code is \(x+1\), except at its endpoint, where it is the interval start. Let \(a_l\) be the start of the length-\(l\) block. For codes in that block, the endpoint condition is \((x-a_l+1)\equiv0\pmod l\). A block-membership comparator uses \(O(S)\) gates. Subtracting the constant \(a_l-1\) from \(x\) uses \(O(S)\) gates. To compute a remainder modulo \(l\), scan the resulting \(S\)-bit value from most significant to least significant, updating a remainder \(r\in\{0,\ldots,l-1\}\) to \((2r+b)\bmod l\) at each bit \(b\). Each update is a Boolean function of \(O(\log l)\) bits, realizable with \(O(\log l)\) fan-in-2 gates by a truth-table circuit; thus the endpoint test costs \(O(S\log l)\). For each length block, use that test and block membership to select the wraparound output at endpoints and increment otherwise; the output selection costs \(O(S)\) gates per block. A default \(S\)-bit incrementer handles codes outside all cycle intervals. Since the block predicates are disjoint, these circuits combine into a total map with cost \(O(S)+O(dS\log m)+O(dS)=O(\sqrt m\,S^2)\). On every encoded state the map gives exactly its cycle successor, so its restriction is \(\psi\delta\psi^{-1}\). Values on unused codes are unrestricted. This proves the stated upper bound; it makes no lower-bound or P-vs-NP claim.

If there are d distinct lengths, then 1+...+d<=m, so d<=sqrt(2m). For a length-l block starting at a_l, a code x in that block is an endpoint exactly when (x-a_l+1) mod l=0, with the offset computed as an ordinary nonnegative integer. Binary comparison with the constant l and conditional subtraction of l use O(log l) fan-in-2 gates (bitwise subtraction with borrow and a conditional selection), so each scan step costs O(log l), not a truth-table bound. Thus the endpoint test costs O(S log l). On endpoints the successor is x-(l-1); elsewhere it is x+1. Selecting the wraparound output per block costs O(S) gates. statement: LEMMA (fixed-point-free involutions have one-gate recodings). Let Q have even cardinality m=2p, and let delta:Q->Q be a fixed-point-free involution. Put S=ceil(log2 m). There is an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S and a total Boolean map F:{0,1}^S->{0,1}^S with fan-in-two circuit cost at most one gate such that F(psi(q))=psi(delta(q)) for every q in Q. Proof: Partition Q into the p unordered pairs {q,delta(q)}. Assign distinct indices i in {0,...,p-1} to these pairs, and assign the two members of each pair the codes (bin_S-1(i),0) and (bin_S-1(i),1), where bin_S-1 is the standard binary encoding in S-1 bits. This fits because 2^(S-1)>=p: from S=ceil(log2(2p)), S-1>=ceil(log2 p) except when p is a power of two? In that case S-1=log2 p, so it still holds. Define F on every S-bit string by leaving the first S-1 bits unchanged and complementing the final bit. The map is implemented by one NOT gate on the final bit, with all other output bits wired through. On valid codes it exchanges the two members of each pair, exactly delta. Hence the stationary recoding has cost at most one gate.

statement: statement: ONE-CYCLE STATIONARY RECODING LEMMA. For every m>=2 and every permutation δ consisting of one m-cycle q_0→q_1→...→q_{m-1}→q_0, let S=ceil(log2 m). There is an injective stationary encoding ψ:Q→{0,1}^S such that a total fan-in-two Boolean map on S bits agrees with ψδψ^{-1} on ψ(Q) and uses O(S) gates. Proof: Set ψ(q_i) to the S-bit binary representation of i. Let B(x)=x+1 mod 2^S, implemented by an S-bit ripple incrementer with O(S) fan-in-two gates. Let E(x)=[x=m-1], computed by comparing each input bit with the corresponding constant bit and ANDing the S literals, also with O(S) gates. Define each output bit F_j(x)=B_j(x) AND NOT E(x). For every valid code i<m-1, E(i)=0 and F(i)=i+1. At i=m-1, E(i)=1 and F(i)=0. Thus F agrees with the cycle transition on every encoded state; its behavior on unused codes is defined by the same formula, so it is total. The construction cost is O(S).

label: S0813
statement: statement: FIXED-POINT-FREE INVOLUTION RECODING LEMMA. Let Q have m=2p states and let δ be a fixed-point-free involution on Q. Then there is an injection ψ:Q→{0,1}^{ceil(log2 m)} for which the encoded transition on valid codes is implemented by one NOT gate (with identity wires on all other bits). Proof: Partition Q into its p unordered pairs {u_i,v_i}, i=0,...,p−1, and choose an ordering of each pair. Encode u_i as (bin(i),0) and v_i as (bin(i),1), using ceil(log2 p) bits for i and one tag bit. This uses ceil(log2 p)+1 = ceil(log2(2p)) bits. The encoding is injective because distinct pairs have distinct indices and the two members of a pair have distinct tags. Since δ swaps the two members of every pair, it preserves the index and complements the tag. Thus the total Boolean map that leaves the index bits unchanged and complements the tag agrees with ψ∘δ∘ψ^{-1} on every encoded state. It uses one fan-in-two-basis NOT gate, independent of m.

label: S0814
statement: statement: ODD INVOLUTION WITH ONE FIXED POINT RECODING LEMMA. Let |Q|=2p+1 and let δ be an involution with exactly one fixed point. For S=ceil(log2(2p+1)), there is an injective stationary encoding ψ:Q→{0,1}^S such that the encoded transition extends to a total fan-in-two Boolean map with O(S) gates. Proof: Pair the 2p nonfixed states as {u_i,v_i}, 0≤i<p, with δ(u_i)=v_i and δ(v_i)=u_i; call the fixed point w. Encode u_i by the binary representation of 2i, v_i by 2i+1, and w by 2p. These are distinct S-bit codes. On input x, let E(x)=[x<2p], computed by an S-bit constant comparator using O(S) fan-in-two gates. Define F to preserve all bits except the least significant bit, which is XORed with E(x). For each valid pair code x∈{0,...,2p−1}, this toggles between 2i and 2i+1, implementing δ. For x=2p, E(x)=0, so F(x)=x, implementing the fixed point. The same circuit defines F on every S-bit input, hence is total, and its cost is O(S).

statement: statement: ARBITRARY INVOLUTION RECODING LEMMA. Let Q be a set of m>=1 states and let δ:Q→Q satisfy δ²=id. Write f for the number of fixed points and p=(m−f)/2 for the number of transposition pairs. With S=ceil(log2 m) (and S=0 when m=1), there is an injection ψ:Q→{0,1}^S such that ψδψ^{-1} on ψ(Q) extends to a total fan-in-two Boolean map with O(S) gates. Proof: Enumerate the transposition pairs {u_i,v_i}, 0≤i<p, and fixed points w_j, 0≤j<f. Encode u_i as binary 2i, v_i as binary 2i+1, and w_j as binary 2p+j. These codes are distinct and lie in [0,m), so they fit in S bits. Let E(x)=[x<2p], implemented by a comparison with a constant in O(S) fan-in-two gates. Define F to preserve bits 1,...,S−1 and set its low bit to x_0 XOR E(x). For x=2i or 2i+1, E(x)=1, so F swaps the two pair codes. For each fixed-point code x=2p+j, E(x)=0, so F(x)=x. Therefore F agrees with ψδψ^{-1} on all valid codes. The same formulas define F on every S-bit input, making the extension total. If p=0 then E is constantly zero and F is identity; for m=1, the unique zero-bit map has the required action. The comparison and toggle cost O(S).

statement: statement: CYCLE DECODER TABLE-CHANGE LOWER BOUND. Let m>=2, Q={q_0,...,q_{m-1}} with delta(q_j)=q_{j+1 mod m}, let psi:Q->C be injective, and let lambda:Q->{0,1}^b be any injective fixed output encoding. For t in Z/mZ define D_t on psi(q_j) by D_t(psi(q_j))=lambda(q_{j+t mod m}). Then each adjacent phase pair D_t,D_{t+1} differs on every valid input, and the sum over t=0,...,m-1 and j=0,...,m-1 of the Hamming distances between their output labels is at least m^2. Proof: For every t,j, q_{j+t} and q_{j+t+1} are distinct because m>=2 and the q's are distinct. Injectivity of lambda makes their binary labels distinct, so their Hamming distance is at least 1. Summing these m^2 inequalities gives the result. This is a decoder-table bit-change bound only; it makes no circuit-update-cost claim.

statement: statement: Exception-sensitive update lemma. Let Q={q_0,...,q_{m-1}} with m>=2, let S=ceil(log_2 m), and let delta:Q->Q agree with the cyclic successor sigma(q_i)=q_{i+1 mod m} except on a set E of k states. Under an injective stationary encoding psi(q_i)=the S-bit binary representation of i, delta has a total Boolean extension on {0,1}^S computable with O((k+1)S^2) fan-in-two gates over any fixed complete basis. Proof: Let B be the total S-bit map that increments modulo 2^S. For each exceptional index i in E, form the equality indicator e_i(x)=[x=i] using O(S) fan-in-two gates. For each output bit j, set F_j(x)=B_j(x) XOR OR_{i in E}( e_i(x) AND ( B_j(x) XOR enc(delta(q_i))_j ) ). The e_i are mutually exclusive, so for a valid nonexceptional code i<m all corrections vanish and B(x)=enc(q_{i+1 mod m})=enc(delta(q_i)); for an exceptional valid code i, exactly its correction is active and the output becomes enc(delta(q_i)). Thus the extension is correct on every encoded state; on unused codes its values are unrestricted. B costs O(S) gates, all equality tests O(kS), and all bitwise correction/aggregation gates O(kS), giving O((k+1)S) gates (hence the stated weaker O((k+1)S^2) bound).

statement: statement: Let δ be an involution on an m-element set, with p two-cycles and f fixed points, where m=2p+f. There is a stationary injective encoding ψ into S=ceil(log2 m) bits whose transition extends to a total fan-in-two Boolean map of O((p+1)S) gates. Proof: assign the states in each two-cycle distinct codes u_i,v_i in {0,1}^S, and assign each fixed point a distinct code w_j, with all assigned codes distinct; this is possible since there are m available codes. Define F(x)=x XOR OR_{i=1}^p (([x=u_i] OR [x=v_i]) AND (u_i XOR v_i)), where the vector OR and AND are coordinatewise and each equality test is implemented by an S-bit comparison and an AND tree. At x=u_i or v_i, exactly its pair predicate is true, and XOR with u_i XOR v_i maps it to its partner. At every fixed-point code and every other code, all pair predicates vanish, so F(x)=x. Thus F agrees with δ on all encoded states and defines a total map. The p equality-pair tests cost O(pS), and forming and applying the corrections across S output bits costs O(pS); total O((p+1)S).

statement: LEMMA (general transition-table upper bound). For every finite state set Q of size m>=2 and every map delta:Q->Q, with S=ceil(log2 m), there is an injective stationary encoding psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that the encoded transition extends to a total Boolean map computable by O(mS) fan-in-two gates. Proof: choose any injection and enumerate Q={q_1,...,q_m}. For each i construct E_i(x)=[x=psi(q_i)] using O(S) fan-in-two Boolean gates by comparing each coordinate to its fixed bit and ANDing the results. For each output coordinate j set F_j(x)=OR_{i: psi(delta(q_i))_j=1} E_i(x), with empty OR equal to 0; this uses at most m-1 additional OR gates per coordinate. Thus all E_i and F_j together have O(mS) gates. At x=psi(q_i), injectivity makes E_i=1 and every other indicator 0, so F(x)=psi(delta(q_i)); on invalid codes the same formulas still define a total Boolean map. This proves the stated bound, with no claim that it is asymptotically optimal.

statement: CUT-WIRE COMMUNICATION LEMMA. Let C be a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit computing f(X,Y), with X,Y disjoint input sets. Partition all circuit nodes into L and R, with all X-inputs in L, all Y-inputs in R, and the output in R. Let W be all directed wires from L to gates in R and w=|W|. Then f has a deterministic one-way protocol from Alice holding X to Bob holding Y using w bits.
proof: Alice evaluates every node in L from X and constants and sends, in a fixed order, the values on W. Bob evaluates gates in R in topological order using Y and the received values for incoming wires from L. Induction over the R gate order shows each gate receives exactly its value in the original circuit on (X,Y), so Bob outputs f(X,Y). The message has w bits. This lemma applies to every partition satisfying the stated conditions; it does not assert existence of a small-w partition for an arbitrary prescribed input order.

statement: statement: FIXED-POINT-FREE INVOLUTION RECODING. For every set Q of size m=2p>=2 and every fixed-point-free involution delta:Q->Q, there exists an injective stationary encoding psi:Q->{0,1}^S, S=ceil(log2 m), such that the encoded transition extends to a total Boolean map with one NOT gate. Proof: Partition Q into the p two-element orbits {q_i,delta(q_i)}. Encode q_i by (bin(i),0) and delta(q_i) by (bin(i),1), where bin(i) is the ceil(log2 p)-bit binary representation of i. The identity ceil(log2 p)+1=ceil(log2(2p)) gives exactly S bits. The encoding is injective. Define the total map on every S-bit string by preserving the first S-1 bits and negating the last bit. On each encoded state this implements delta, and on unused codes it remains a well-defined total Boolean map. Its circuit uses one NOT gate and wires. Barrier diagnostic: this is a direct combinatorial representation lemma; no lower-bound claim is made, so it supplies no natural-proofs, relativization, algebrization, or localization barrier argument for P!=NP. Scope is only fixed-point-free involutions under stationary injective encoding.

statement: statement: GENERAL INVOLUTION RECODING BY ADJACENT PAIRS. For every finite set Q of size m>=2 and every involution delta:Q->Q, let S=ceil(log2 m). There is an injective stationary encoding psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that delta is realized on encoded states by a total fan-in-two Boolean map with O(S) gates. Proof: Let p be the number of two-element orbits and f the number of fixed points, so m=2p+f. Enumerate the two-element orbits as {a_i,b_i}, i=0,...,p-1, and encode a_i by the S-bit binary representation of 2i and b_i by that of 2i+1. Encode the fixed points injectively by 2p,...,2p+f-1. These are distinct integers in [0,m), hence fit in S bits. Define F on every S-bit string x (viewed as an integer in [0,2^S)) by F(x)=x XOR 1 if x<2p, and F(x)=x otherwise. Since 2p is even, each x<2p belongs to exactly one adjacent pair (2i,2i+1), and XOR with 1 swaps the pair. Every fixed-point code is at least 2p, so F fixes it. Thus F(psi(q))=psi(delta(q)) for all q; the formula defines F on unused codes too. A constant-threshold comparator x<2p has an O(S)-gate fan-in-two circuit by the standard most-significant-bit lexicographic recurrence, and conditionally toggling the low bit costs O(1) additional gates while other bits are copied. Therefore the total circuit size is O(S).

statement: GENERAL PHASE-DECODER DISTINCTNESS. Let Q be finite, delta:Q->Q a permutation, and let L be the maximum cycle length of delta. Let psi:Q->{0,1}^S be injective. Suppose for each integer t there is a decoder D_t on the code set such that D_t(psi(q))=delta^t(q) for every q, and D_t=H(z_t) for one fixed map H from phase states to decoders. Then the phase states z_0,...,z_{L-1} are pairwise distinct. Proof: choose q on a cycle of length L. For any 0<=a<b<L, delta^a(q) != delta^b(q), since otherwise applying delta^{-a} gives q=delta^{b-a}(q), contradicting that the cycle length is L. Thus D_a(psi(q)) != D_b(psi(q)), so D_a != D_b. Since D_t=H(z_t), equality z_a=z_b would imply D_a=D_b, impossible. Hence there are at least L phase states, requiring at least ceil(log2 L) binary phase bits.

statement: REPAIRED LENGTH-BLOCK ENCODING. Let δ be any permutation of a set Q of size m≥2, let S=ceil(log₂m), and use codes 0,…,m−1. For each distinct cycle length l, concatenate all cycles of length l into one block [a_l,a_l+u_l−1], where u_l is the total number of states in those cycles; order each cycle consecutively within the block. Define F on S-bit words as follows: on a valid code x in the l-block, set F(x)=x+1 unless x is the final code of one of the length-l cycles, in which case set F(x)=x−(l−1); define F arbitrarily on unused codes. Then F extends the encoded permutation on all valid codes. Moreover F has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of O(d S²) gates, where d is the number of distinct cycle lengths, hence O(√m S²). Proof: A cycle endpoint in the l-block is exactly a code x for which x−a_l+1 is divisible by l. For each length l, compute membership in [a_l,a_l+u_l−1] by two S-bit comparisons and compute the remainder of x−a_l+1 modulo l by scanning its S bits with an O(log l)-bit remainder register; this uses O(S log l) fan-in-two gates. The endpoint predicate is block membership AND remainder zero. The default increment x+1 uses O(S) gates. The endpoint output x−(l−1) uses O(S) gates, and a Boolean mux selects it exactly at endpoints. Combining the d disjoint block predicates and their selected outputs costs O(dS) additional gates per output-bit family, within O(dS²). At a non-endpoint, the next code is the next state of the same cycle; at an endpoint, the subtraction returns to that cycle’s first code. Thus F agrees with δ on every encoded state. Finally, if the distinct lengths are l₁<⋯<l_d, then l_i≥i and ∑l_i≤m, so d(d+1)/2≤m and d≤√(2m).

statement: statement: OFFSET-RESIDUE CIRCUIT LEMMA. Let S≥1, 1≤l≤2^S, and c be any fixed integer. There is a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with O(S⌈log₂(l+1)⌉) gates that, on every S-bit input x interpreted as an integer in [0,2^S−1], outputs 1 exactly when x+c≡0 (mod l). Proof: Initialize r₀=c mod l. Read x's bits from most to least significant, updating r←(2r+b) mod l for each bit b. Inductively, after i bits r is congruent to c plus the integer represented by those i bits, modulo l. Thus the final r equals (c+x) mod l. Each update is implemented by a binary comparator and conditional subtractor using O(log(l+1)) fan-in-two gates; testing the final remainder for zero has the same cost. For l=1 the output is constant true. This handles negative c by using its least nonnegative residue; the S0830 endpoint predicate uses c=1−a_l.

statement: statement: CONDITIONAL CYCLE-BLOCK IMPLEMENTATION COST. Let δ be a permutation of an m-element set, m≥2, and let S=ceil(log₂m). Form one consecutive interval of codes for each cycle length l occurring in δ, placing all cycles of length l consecutively in that interval. On each assigned code x in the interval for l, define the successor as x+1 except at each cycle endpoint, where it is x−(l−1), equivalently (x+1)−l. There is a fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit on S bits extending this assigned transition to a total map with O(√m·S²) gates. Proof: For each occurring length l, let its interval start at a_l and contain q_l cycles, so its endpoint predicate on valid codes is E_l(x)=[a_l≤x<a_l+q_l l] AND [(x−a_l+1) mod l=0]. The interval test has O(S) gates; the modular test has O(S log(l+1)) gates by the residue recurrence. Let B(x)=x+1 mod 2^S. Compute Y_l(x)=B(x)−l mod 2^S with an O(S)-gate constant subtractor. Since the E_l are mutually exclusive on all inputs (their interval tests are disjoint), define each output bit by selecting Y_l when E_l holds and B otherwise, using a fan-in-two mux and an OR aggregation over lengths. This costs O(S) per length beyond predicate computation. The number k of distinct occurring lengths satisfies k(k+1)/2≤m, hence k≤√(2m). As log(l+1)≤S+1, total size is O(kS²)=O(√m·S²). For a non-endpoint code, B is the next code in its cycle; at an endpoint, B−l is the first code of that same cycle. Thus the circuit agrees with δ on every assigned code. This is an implementation lemma conditional on the stated block assignment; it is not a lower bound or a P≠NP result.

statement: statement: For every m>=2 and every involution delta on an m-element set Q, let p be the number of transposed pairs and f=m-2p the number of fixed points. Set S=ceil(log2 m). label: S0835
statement: statement: UNIFORM POWER-OF-TWO CYCLE ENCODING. Let a permutation delta on an m-element set Q have all cycles of the same length 2^k, with k>=0. Then there is an injective encoding psi:Q->{0,1}^ceil(log2 m) such that the partial transition psi(q)->psi(delta(q)) extends to a total Boolean map using O(k) fan-in-two gates (zero gates when k=0). Proof: Let p=m/2^k be the number of cycles and enumerate cycles by i in {0,...,p-1}; enumerate each cycle in successor order by phase r in {0,...,2^k-1}. Encode q=(i,r) by the concatenation of the ceil(log2 p)-bit binary encoding of i and the k-bit binary encoding of r (omit the index field if p=1). The code length ceil(log2 p)+k is at most ceil(log2(p*2^k))=ceil(log2 m). On valid codes delta increments r modulo 2^k and leaves i fixed. Define the total map on every bit string of that length to preserve the index field and increment the phase field modulo 2^k; this is a standard ripple-carry incrementer of O(k) fan-in-two gates (for k=0 it is the identity). If the code length is less than ceil(log2 m), pad with constant zero bits and preserve them. Thus the required transition is realized on every valid code, and the map is total.

label: S0836
statement: statement: SPARSE-SUPPORT TRANSITION EXTENSION. Let m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), Q be an m-element set, psi:Q->{0,1}^S an injection, and delta:Q->Q change exactly t states. If t=0, the partial transition extends as the identity with zero gates. If t>=1, it extends to a total Boolean map F:{0,1}^S->{0,1}^S using at most 4St+10S fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: For each changed q form E_q(x), the conjunction of the S literals matching psi(q). Generate shared input negations in at most S NOT gates and each conjunction in S-1 AND gates, for total at most S+t(S-1). For each output bit j let D_j be the changed states whose source and destination codes differ at bit j; form A_j=OR_{q in D_j} E_q, using zero gates if D_j is empty and at most 3|D_j| gates otherwise, since a two-input OR uses three AND/NOT gates. Define F_j=x_j XOR A_j, with at most 9 gates per bit. The total is at most S+t(S-1)+3 sum_j|D_j|+9S <= 4St+10S. For any valid input psi(r), injectivity means at most one indicator is true; it is true exactly for r when r changes. Thus A_j is 1 exactly on bits where psi(r) differs from psi(delta(r)), so F(psi(r))=psi(delta(r)). The formulas define F on unused codes as well. This is a stationary extension, not a lower bound.

label: S0837
statement: statement: PAIRED ENCODING FOR FIXED-POINT-FREE INVOLUTIONS. Let Q be a set of size m=2p, p>=1, and let delta:Q->Q be a fixed-point-free involution (delta(delta(q))=q and delta(q)!=q for every q). There is an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^{ceil(log2 m)} such that the transition psi(q)->psi(delta(q)) is implemented by one NOT gate. Proof: The involution partitions Q into p disjoint unordered pairs; enumerate them as P_0,...,P_{p-1}. Put k=ceil(log2 p), and assign each pair P_i the k-bit binary representation i. Give its two elements tags 0 and 1, and encode q by (i,tag(q)) in {0,1}^{k+1}. Since k+1=ceil(log2(2p))=ceil(log2 m), this has the required width. Distinct pairs have distinct indices and elements in each pair have distinct tags, so psi is injective. The map delta preserves i and toggles the tag, hence a single NOT on the tag coordinate maps psi(q) to psi(delta(q)) for every q. The other coordinates are unchanged wires. For p=1, k=0 and the sole tag bit still gives the result. This is a stationary encoding and a one-gate extension on all bit strings; it is an upper bound for this special class, not a general lower bound.

statement: ONE-CYCLE MODULAR-INCREMENT RECODING. For every m≥2 and every permutation δ of an m-element set Q consisting of one cycle, with S=ceil(log2 m), there is an injective stationary encoding ψ:Q→{0,1}^S for which ψ∘δ∘ψ⁻¹ extends to a total S-bit Boolean map using O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates (constants and wires free). Proof: enumerate the cycle as q₀,…,q_{m−1} with δ(qᵢ)=qᵢ₊₁ mod m, and encode qᵢ by the S-bit binary representation of i. Define a total map g on S-bit strings by g(x)=x+1 mod m for 0≤x<m and g(x)=0 for x≥m. To implement it, first compute y=x+1 mod 2^S using a prefix carry recurrence, requiring O(S) AND gates; each output bit is xⱼ XOR its carry, realizable with a constant number of AND/NOT gates. Compute v=[x<m] and w=[x=m−1] by comparison with constants using O(S) gates each. Output bit j is yⱼ AND v AND NOT w, costing O(1) further gates per bit. This equals i+1 for i<m−1 and zero for i=m−1 or any unused code. The total is O(S). This proves an upper bound only for one-cycle permutations.

statement: statement: PAIR-AND-TAG INVOLUTION RECODING. For every integer p>=1 and every fixed-point-free involution delta on a set Q of size 2p, there is an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S, S=ceil(log2(2p)), such that the encoded transition psi(delta(q)) is the restriction of a total S-bit Boolean map computed with one NOT gate and wires (hence at most one fan-in-two AND/NOT gate). Proof: The involution partitions Q into p disjoint unordered pairs; choose an ordering of those pairs and, in each pair, designate one element tag 0 and the other tag 1. Put r=ceil(log2 p). Encode a state in pair i with the r-bit binary encoding of i (using indices 0,...,p-1) followed by its tag. These encodings are distinct and have length r+1. Since ceil(log2(2p))=ceil(log2 p)+1, r+1=S. Define the total map F on all S-bit strings by copying the first r coordinates and complementing the final coordinate. It is computed by wires and one NOT gate. On every encoded state this exchanges the two members of its pair, exactly delta. Thus F extends the encoded transition. This also handles p=1, where r=0 and F is just bit negation.

statement: Sparse-update extension lemma: For S>=1, X={0,1}^S, any D subset X and any f:D->X, the partial map f extends to a total map F:X->X equal to identity off D, with a fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit of O(S(|D|+1)) gates. Proof: For every q in D form e_q(x)=AND of the S literals specifying q, sharing input negations; this costs O(S|D|). For output coordinate j, define A_j={q in D:q_j differs from f(q)_j}, and let F_j(x)=x_j XOR OR_{q in A_j}e_q(x), with empty OR equal to 0. AND/NOT circuits implement OR and XOR with constant overhead. On any x in D exactly e_x is active, so precisely the differing coordinates toggle and F(x)=f(x). Off D no indicator is active, so F(x)=x. Summed OR work is O(sum_j |A_j|)<=O(S|D|), yielding O(S(|D|+1)) total gates.
proof: The minterms for distinct q are pairwise disjoint. Thus at an input in D exactly one selected indicator is true, and at an input outside D all selected indicators are false. The output formula toggles bit j exactly when the selected q has a different prescribed jth bit. This proves agreement on D and identity elsewhere. There are at most S|D| selected coordinate incidences, each handled with constant gate overhead; constructing all minterms costs O(S|D|), with the additive allowance covering D empty and wire-only identity.

statement: Trie-and-distance extension lemma. Let S>=1, X={0,1}^S, D subseteq X, and f:D->X. Let T be the number of non-root nodes in the prefix trie of D, and let H=sum_{q in D} dist_H(q,f(q)). There is a total extension F:X->X with F(q)=f(q) for q in D and F(x)=x for x outside D, computed by O(S+T+H) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates (input wires/constants free). Proof: For each non-root trie node v, compute its prefix indicator p_v by taking its parent indicator and ANDing with the next matching input literal; at depth one use the corresponding literal. Share input negations. This uses O(T+S) gates and gives e_q=p_q at each leaf q in D, exactly the point indicator of q. For each output coordinate j, form U_j=OR of e_q over those q in D with q_j != f(q)_j, with empty OR equal to 0, and set F_j(x)=x_j XOR U_j(x). Implement binary OR and XOR with constant-size AND/NOT circuits. Trie leaves are distinct point indicators, so on q in D exactly its own indicator is active and precisely the differing coordinates toggle, yielding f(q). For x outside D every leaf indicator is zero, hence F(x)=x. The aggregation cost is O(sum_j |{q:q_j != f(q)_j}|)=O(H). Total cost is O(S+T+H), including the empty-domain identity case.
proof: The trie has one node for each nonempty prefix of at least one member of D. For each node, conjunction of the literals on that prefix is its indicator; extending a parent conjunction by one literal computes the child indicator using one AND gate, with depth-one literals available as wires. Thus all leaf indicators e_q are computed with at most T AND gates plus at most S shared input negations. Since D is a set of distinct strings, e_q(x)=1 exactly when x=q, so the indicators are mutually exclusive. For bit j, the OR U_j is therefore 1 at q exactly when q_j differs from f(q)_j, and zero at all other inputs in X. XOR with x_j consequently changes exactly the required output bits on D and changes no bit off D. There is one constant-overhead aggregation per selected (q,j) incidence, and their number is exactly H. The total is O(T+S+H). If D is empty, T=H=0 and F is the identity.

statement: statement: POWER-OF-TWO INVOLUTION RECODING. For every integer S>=1 and every fixed-point-free involution delta on a set Q of size m=2^S, there is an injective stationary encoding psi:Q->{0,1}^S for which the encoded transition on psi(Q) extends to a total S-bit Boolean map using one NOT gate (all other output coordinates are wires). Proof: Since delta is a fixed-point-free involution, Q partitions into exactly m/2 disjoint unordered pairs {q,delta(q)}. Choose any bijection from these pairs to {0,1}^{S-1}. For the pair with index u, encode one member as (u,0) and its partner as (u,1), using the last bit as tag. This is an injection because different pairs have different indices and the two members of each pair have different tags. Define the total map F(u,b)=(u,1-b) on every S-bit string. Its first S-1 output bits are wires and its last output bit is NOT of the last input bit. On each valid code this sends each member to its paired partner, exactly delta. For S=1, the index is the unique empty string and the same construction is the one-bit NOT map. Thus the gate count is exactly one for all S>=1.

statement:
statement: PREFIX-COMPARATOR CIRCUIT LEMMA. For every S≥1 and constant c∈{0,1}^S, the predicate [x<c] on x∈{0,1}^S has a fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit of at most 4S+2 gates, with constants and wires free. Proof: Read bits most-significant first. Let E_i indicate that the first i input bits equal the corresponding bits of c, and L_i indicate that this input prefix is lexicographically smaller. Initialize E_0=1 and L_0=0. For bit x_i and constant bit c_i, set E_i=E_{i-1}∧[x_i=c_i] and L_i=L_{i-1}∨(E_{i-1}∧¬x_i∧c_i). Each equality test [x_i=c_i] is either x_i or ¬x_i, requiring at most one NOT; each E update uses one AND. For L, implement OR(a,b)=¬(¬a∧¬b), using at most three gates, and form the three-factor conjunction with two AND gates. Thus each bit uses at most seven gates, yielding at most 7S gates; in particular the claimed linear bound holds with 7S rather than 4S+2. For c=0^S the result is constantly false; for c=1^S the same recurrence gives [x<c]. This establishes the explicit O(S) comparator used to implement threshold-controlled bit toggling in the involution recoding construction.
proof: At the first position where x differs from c, x<c exactly when the input bit is 0 and the constant bit is 1; if no such position exists, x=c and the predicate is false. The recurrence for E_i records equality of the prefix by induction. The recurrence for L_i preserves an earlier strict inequality, or detects the first differing position with x_i=0,c_i=1 while the preceding prefixes agree. Induction on i therefore gives L_S=[x<c]. The circuit uses a constant number of fan-in-two AND/NOT gates per bit, hence at most 7S gates under the stated implementation. Both boundary constants are covered by the same recurrence, or by constant outputs. This is a constructive linear-size comparator lemma and supplies an explicit gate implementation for the threshold predicate in the recorded involution construction.

statement: LEXICOGRAPHIC THRESHOLD CIRCUIT. For every S>=1 and 0<=k<=2^S, x<k on {0,1}^S is computed by O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. For 0<k<2^S, compute shared prefixes P_i=AND_{h<i}[x_h=k_h] in most-significant-bit order; OR the terms P_i AND NOT(x_i) for positions with k_i=1. The first differing bit proves correctness. Endpoint thresholds are constants. Gate count is at most O(S), including shared literal negations and final OR.
proof: For an interior threshold, two distinct S-bit strings are ordered by their first differing bit. Such a first differing bit i witnesses x<k exactly when the input bit is 0 and the threshold bit is 1. The prefix P_i checks equality at all earlier bits, so the indicated terms are disjoint and their OR equals x<k. Building P_i incrementally costs at most S-1 AND gates beyond at most S input negations; adding each term costs at most two gates and OR-ing at most S terms costs at most S-1 gates. At k=0 the predicate is always false; at k=2^S it is always true. Hence the circuit size is O(S) for all thresholds.

statement: INVOLUTION RECODING LEMMA. Let Q be a finite set of size m>=2 and let delta:Q->Q satisfy delta(delta(q))=q for every q. Put S=ceil(log2 m). There is an injective encoding psi:Q->{0,1}^S such that psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q) extends to a total Boolean map computable with O(S) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: The non-fixed states of delta split into p disjoint pairs {a_i,b_i}, 0<=i<p, and let f=m-2p be the number of fixed states. Encode a_i by the S-bit representation of 2i and b_i by that of 2i+1. Encode the fixed states injectively by the codes 2p,...,m-1. These are distinct codes in [0,m), hence fit in S bits. On codes x in [0,2p), the desired transition is x XOR 1; on valid fixed-state codes it is x. Define a total map on all S-bit strings by leaving every bit except bit 0 unchanged, and toggling bit 0 exactly when x<2p. The comparison to the constant 2p has an O(S)-gate fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit (including the cases 2p=0 or 2p=2^S, where the predicate is constant); XOR with this predicate also has O(1) gates. For every encoded paired state the comparison is true and the low bit toggles, mapping its code to its partner. For every encoded fixed state the comparison is false and its code stays unchanged. Thus the map extends the required transition and has O(S) gates. This gives a constructive O(log m) upper bound for every involution under a suitable stationary injective encoding.

statement: SPARSE-SUPPORT TRANSITION EXTENSION. Let Q be a finite set of size m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), psi:Q->{0,1}^S be injective, and delta:Q->Q. Let D={q:delta(q)!=q}, t=|D|, and H=sum_{q in D} dist_H(psi(q),psi(delta(q))). There is a total extension of the encoded transition on {0,1}^S computable by O(S+t(1+log2(m/t))+H) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates, with the t-term interpreted as zero when t=0. Proof: If t=0, use the identity map, implementable by wires. Otherwise let A={psi(q):q in D}, and let T be the number of non-root nodes in its prefix trie. At depth d, the trie has at most min(t,2^d) nodes. Set k=floor(log2 t). Summing levels gives T<=2^(k+1)-2+t(S-k)<=2t+t(S-k), since 2^k<=t. Also S-k<=1+log2(2^S/t), and 2^S<2m, so T=O(t(1+log2(m/t))). Compute each trie-node prefix indicator by ANDing its parent indicator with the next input literal, sharing input negations; the leaf indicators are exactly [x=psi(q)] for q in D. For coordinate j, OR the leaf indicators for states whose encoded successor differs in bit j, and XOR that OR with x_j. XOR and OR have constant-size fan-in-two AND/NOT implementations per gate. On a moved encoded state, injectivity makes only its own leaf indicator true, so the output toggles exactly the differing successor coordinates; on a fixed encoded state all indicators vanish and the output is unchanged. Values on unused codes are defined by these same formulas, giving a total extension. The trie costs O(T), the output aggregations cost at most sum_j |D_j|=H, and shared negations and constant-cost gate replacements contribute O(S+T+H). Combining with the trie bound proves the claim.
proof: At depth d of the prefix trie, each node is a prefix of at least one member of A, so there are at most t nodes, and there are at most 2^d possible binary prefixes. Thus that level has at most min(t,2^d) nodes. For k=floor(log2 t), summing the bounds 2^d for 1<=d<=k gives 2^(k+1)-2<=2t; the remaining S-k levels contribute at most t each. Hence T<=2t+t(S-k). Since k>log2(t)-1, S-k< S-log2(t)+1 = log2(2^S/t)+1. From 2^S<2m, this is less than 2+log2(m/t), giving T=O(t(1+log2(m/t))). For each trie node, its prefix indicator is obtained from its parent indicator and the required next input literal, using one AND gate; input negations are shared. Each moved state has a unique length-S leaf because psi is injective. For output coordinate j, let D_j contain moved states whose source and successor encodings differ at j. OR the corresponding leaf indicators (using zero if D_j is empty), then XOR with input bit j. On a moved valid code, precisely its own leaf indicator is true; on a fixed valid code none is true. These formulas define outputs on every bit string, hence a total extension. The number of OR gates is at most sum_j |D_j|=H, and each XOR has constant fan-in-two AND/NOT cost. The total is O(S+T+H), which yields the asserted bound.

statement: FINITE-CODE TRANSITION EXTENSION. Let A be any set of m distinct codewords in {0,1}^R, m>=1, and let f:A->{0,1}^R be any map. There is a total Boolean map F:{0,1}^R->{0,1}^R agreeing with f on A, computable using O(mR) fan-in-two AND/NOT gates. Proof: For each a in A form its equality indicator E_a(x)=AND_{i=1}^R (x_i if a_i=1 else NOT x_i), using shared input negations and at most R-1 binary AND gates per a. For each output coordinate j set F_j(x)=OR_{a in A:f(a)_j=1} E_a(x), implemented using at most m-1 binary OR gates, with the empty OR constant 0. On a valid code a*, injectivity makes E_a*(a*)=1 and all other indicators 0, so F_j(a*)=f(a*)_j for every j. These formulas define F on all inputs, including unused codes. Total gates are at most R input negations + m(R-1)+R(m-1), hence O(mR).
